items.title: From Sewers to Surveillance: Monitoring Salmonella Through Wastewater.
items.summary: Wastewater surveillance offers a population-level complement to traditional clinical reporting, which frequently misses asymptomatic or unreported infections, and this study examined its utility for tracking Salmonella. The researchers developed and validated methods for detecting Salmonella in wastewater, combining polyethylene glycol precipitation for sample concentration, magnetic bead-based nucleic acid extraction, and quantitative PCR. When these methods were applied across a statewide surveillance network, the system revealed seasonal transmission patterns and provided approximately one week of advance warning relative to clinical case reporting. Wastewater surveillance also detected outbreak activity that passive clinical surveillance had failed to capture, demonstrating its value as an early warning tool. The authors note remaining limitations including low pathogen concentrations in environmental samples and insufficient resolution to distinguish Salmonella serovars, but conclude that integrating wastewater surveillance with traditional public health systems can meaningfully improve understanding of Salmonella transmission dynamics.
items.citation: Kuhn KG, Shelton K, Rimal B et al.. From Sewers to Surveillance: Monitoring Salmonella Through Wastewater.. Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.). 2027

items.title: A Rapid Decision Framework for Wastewater and Environmental Surveillance (WES) during Rapidly Emerging and Evolving Outbreak Settings
items.citation: Ahmed W, Medlicott K, Nolan M. A Rapid Decision Framework for Wastewater and Environmental Surveillance (WES) during Rapidly Emerging and Evolving Outbreak Settings. ACS ES&T water. 2026

items.title: Machine learning-enabled wastewater-based surveillance for emerging pathogen detection and monitoring: current applications, challenges, and future prospects.
items.summary: This review examined the use of machine learning to enhance wastewater-based surveillance as a public health tool for detecting and monitoring emerging pathogens. The authors conducted a narrative review by searching multiple literature sources and classifying studies according to a four-layer framework spanning classical statistical models, conventional machine learning, deep learning, and hybrid mechanistic approaches, across five analytical tasks including forecasting, anomaly detection, and data harmonization. They found that the evidence base is heavily dominated by studies focused on SARS-CoV-2, that demonstrated early-warning capability came predominantly from classical statistical methods rather than more complex approaches, and that reported performance varied considerably depending on context. Key barriers identified include sampling variability, environmental and laboratory inconsistencies, population-dependent biases, and the high-dimensional complexity of wastewater molecular data. The authors conclude that future progress depends on standardized collaborative frameworks, multimodal data integration, mechanistic and digital-twin modelling with uncertainty quantification, and transparent analytics, while broader application beyond SARS-CoV-2 remains constrained by governance and public acceptability challenges.
items.citation: Song A, Jia P, Luo J et al.. Machine learning-enabled wastewater-based surveillance for emerging pathogen detection and monitoring: current applications, challenges, and future prospects.. Emerging microbes & infections. 2026

items.title: Multimodal genomic surveillance for respiratory pathogens at four U.S. international airports: A comparison of air, wastewater, clinical, and national surveillance data.
items.summary: This study evaluated whether monitoring airborne pathogens at international airports could serve as an effective public health surveillance tool, particularly for detecting respiratory viruses introduced through international travel. Researchers collected air samples across congregate areas at four U.S. international airports over roughly ten months, analyzing them using PCR, targeted amplicon sequencing, and targeted enrichment sequencing, while comparing results against aviation wastewater, traveler nasal swabs, and national clinical surveillance data. SARS-CoV-2 was detected in nearly all air samples, while influenza A was detected in a smaller fraction, and influenza A positivity showed meaningful correlations with the other surveillance modalities, whereas SARS-CoV-2 measurements did not correlate consistently across data sources. Sequencing approaches successfully identified contemporaneous viral lineages and recovered high-quality genomes for multiple pathogens, including influenza, bocavirus, and seasonal coronaviruses, demonstrating the genomic resolution achievable from air samples. The authors conclude that airport air sampling can complement wastewater-based surveillance at ports of entry, though its effectiveness varies depending on the pathogen and the surveillance modality being compared.
items.citation: Gratalo D, Friedman CR, Morley VJ et al.. Multimodal genomic surveillance for respiratory pathogens at four U.S. international airports: A comparison of air, wastewater, clinical, and national surveillance data.. PLOS global public health. 2026

items.title: Progress and Expansion of the National Wastewater Surveillance System, United States, 2020-2024.
items.summary: The paper chronicles the development of the United States National Wastewater Surveillance System from its origins as an emergency pandemic response tool into a permanent component of national public health infrastructure. Over its first four years, the system expanded its geographic coverage, the range of pathogens it monitors, its analytical and data visualization capabilities, and its laboratory methodologies. Progress was driven by collaborations spanning public, private, and academic sectors, with shared goals of standardizing practices and translating wastewater signals into actionable public health decisions. The authors argue that the system has demonstrated meaningful adaptability and scalability, supporting timely, community-level surveillance for a broadening set of health threats.
items.citation: Mark-Carew M, Bias M, Reckling S et al.. Progress and Expansion of the National Wastewater Surveillance System, United States, 2020-2024.. Emerging infectious diseases. 2026

items.title: Laboratory Evaluation of Cyclospora cayetanensis in Wastewater: Expanding Pathogen Targets for Regulatory Public Health Surveillance
items.citation: Lin C, Gonzalez DS, Poretsky RS. Laboratory Evaluation of Cyclospora cayetanensis in Wastewater: Expanding Pathogen Targets for Regulatory Public Health Surveillance. 2026

items.title: Inferring variant-specific effective reproduction numbers from combined case and sequencing data
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of accurately estimating the transmission rates of distinct SARS-CoV-2 variants circulating simultaneously during the pandemic. The authors developed a statistical framework that jointly analyzes confirmed case counts and genetic sequencing data to infer variant-specific effective reproduction numbers alongside variant frequencies over time. Unlike approaches that rely solely on sequence frequency dynamics, their method captures broader epidemiological behavior by integrating both data streams, and it allows structured relationships between reproduction numbers to be estimated, including fixed growth advantages for specific variants across locations. Applying this approach to data from United States states spanning early 2021 through early 2022, they estimated variant-specific effective reproduction numbers for multiple variants of concern and interest. Their findings demonstrate that consistent, location-independent growth advantages can be attributed to particular variants, offering a more complete picture of variant fitness than frequency-based methods alone.
items.citation: Marlin D Figgins, Trevor Bedford. Inferring variant-specific effective reproduction numbers from combined case and sequencing data. eLife. 2026

items.title: Soil microbes are the tiny bioengineers running Earth’s underground factory
items.summary: This paper examines the functional roles of diverse microbial communities in soil ecosystems and the mechanisms by which they regulate broad environmental processes. The authors synthesized existing soil microbiome research across ecological, agricultural, and environmental contexts using a function-centred framework. They identified four conserved functional axes — secondary metabolism, nutrient cycling, community interactions, and stress tolerance — that together govern ecosystem-level outcomes including plant productivity, climate regulation, and pollutant transformation. The authors propose that soil operates as a self-organizing system in which microbial interactions produce emergent ecosystem behaviour, though the expression of these functions is strongly context dependent. This framework is offered as a foundation for predictive, ecology-informed strategies to manage soil microbiomes for sustainable agriculture, environmental remediation, and climate mitigation.
items.citation: Suzanne Hassan-Dalléac, Wafa Guiga, Antonia Suau. Soil microbes are the tiny bioengineers running Earth’s underground factory. Communications Earth & Environment. 2026

items.title: Beyond the visible: metal-ion-doped inorganic UV phosphors for advanced photonics
items.summary: This review examines inorganic ultraviolet luminescent materials doped with metal ions, including rare-earth and heavy main-group metal ions, which display distinctive electronic transitions, strong photostability, and tunable emission properties. The authors systematically survey the luminescence mechanisms and recent advances across three principal emission modes—persistent luminescence, upconversion luminescence, and mechanoluminescence—organizing the discussion by dominant mode and supplemented by spectral classification. Optimization strategies and future research opportunities are critically assessed for each mode, with particular attention to mechanistic insights and progress in material design and device integration. Applications of these ultraviolet phosphors in optoelectronics, environmental remediation, and biomedicine are analyzed under the principle that material performance determines application suitability. The review concludes by identifying key remaining challenges and outlining future directions for advancing inorganic ultraviolet luminescent materials.
items.citation: Yu Zhang, Yanjie Liang, Feng Liu et al.. Beyond the visible: metal-ion-doped inorganic UV phosphors for advanced photonics. Light Science & Applications. 2026

items.title: Quantitative Microbial Risk Assessment of Human H5N1 Infection From Consumption of Fluid Cow's Milk
items.summary: This paper used quantitative microbial risk assessment to evaluate the public health threat posed by the H5N1 influenza strain that has spilled over into dairy cattle, specifically examining the risk of human infection through drinking fluid cow's milk. Using stochastic farm-to-table models parameterized with data emerging from the ongoing outbreak, the researchers estimated infection probabilities per serving for pasteurized milk and two categories of raw milk sourced from different supply chains, and they modeled several potential risk-reduction interventions. The analysis found that pasteurized milk carries an effectively negligible infection risk, while raw milk—whether purchased at farm stores or retail outlets—carries substantially higher estimated risk. Testing bulk tank milk by quantitative real-time reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction was identified as an effective intervention for reducing raw milk risk. The authors also highlight important knowledge gaps regarding human dose-response to H5N1 via ingestion and raw milk consumption patterns, underscoring the value of mechanistic epidemiological modeling during outbreaks with foodborne transmission potential.
items.citation: Katherine J Koebel, Ece Bulut, Samuel David Alcaine et al.. Quantitative Microbial Risk Assessment of Human H5N1 Infection From Consumption of Fluid Cow's Milk. Risk Analysis. 2026

items.title: Pharmaceuticals in Water: Fate, Health Risks, Treatment and Governance for Sustainable Management
items.summary: This review examines the presence, behavior, and management of pharmaceutical compounds as emerging contaminants in aquatic environments, recognizing that their continuous release, persistence, and biological activity pose risks even at trace concentrations. The authors synthesized current evidence on the occurrence, fate, transport, and removal of major therapeutic classes—including antibiotics, anti-inflammatory drugs, antidepressants, hormones, and beta-blockers—across aquatic systems using a cradle-to-grave lifecycle perspective. Both established and emerging water treatment technologies were critically assessed alongside existing regulatory and governance frameworks. The review identifies gaps in current approaches and proposes an integrated management framework that links lifecycle thinking, advanced treatment strategies, and adaptive regulatory governance to better protect drinking-water resources. The work aims to provide a holistic understanding of pharmaceutical water pollution and to guide future research priorities and policy development.
items.citation: Asvinidevi Arumugam, Khai Ern Lee, Pei Yuen Ng et al.. Pharmaceuticals in Water: Fate, Health Risks, Treatment and Governance for Sustainable Management. Water Air & Soil Pollution. 2026

items.title: Antimicrobial resistance in aquaculture an overview of current status and possible solutions to the issue
items.summary: This review paper examines the growing problem of antimicrobial resistance in aquaculture, tracing how widespread antibiotic use in the sector has driven resistance development and dissemination across aquatic environments. The authors surveyed global patterns of antibiotic use across species, the ecological and genetic mechanisms underpinning resistance spread—including horizontal gene transfer, biofilm formation, and persistence of antibiotic resistance genes in sediments and water—and the public health risks posed by resistant pathogens transmitted through seafood and occupational exposure. The review also assessed the adequacy of existing national and international regulatory frameworks, identifying significant gaps in monitoring, enforcement, and cross-border harmonization. A range of potential solutions were considered, spanning biological alternatives such as vaccines, probiotics, phage therapy, and plant antimicrobials, as well as technological approaches including nanotechnology and precision aquaculture, alongside molecular surveillance tools like metagenomics and quantitative PCR. The authors conclude by advocating for a One Health approach that integrates veterinary, environmental, and public health sectors, and call for policy harmonization, capacity building, and sustained research investment to advance antibiotic-responsible aquaculture.
items.citation: Shafiya Mushtaq, Tasaduq Hussain Shah, Nahida Quyoom et al.. Antimicrobial resistance in aquaculture an overview of current status and possible solutions to the issue. Discover Environment. 2026

items.title: Bad Diagnosis: Analyzing Consent and Data Collection Practices of Mobile Medical Apps
items.summary: This paper examined the consent practices and data collection behaviors of over ten thousand mobile health applications available on the Google Play Store. The researchers developed a framework to distinguish genuine health apps from general wellness tools, then combined static code analysis with privacy policy examination to detect permission misuse and consent violations. They found that the majority of apps request permissions with no apparent functional justification relative to their stated purpose, including widespread requests for location, camera, and microphone access. Most strikingly, nearly all apps in the dataset failed to provide users with any consent form, directly contravening regulations such as GDPR, and even the small minority that did offer consent forms frequently exhibited discrepancies between what users consented to and what data was actually collected. The authors conclude that the mHealth app ecosystem is in urgent need of stronger regulatory enforcement to protect users' sensitive medical information.
items.citation: Ethan Myers, Lorenzo De Carli, Shantanu Sharma et al.. Bad Diagnosis: Analyzing Consent and Data Collection Practices of Mobile Medical Apps. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Entering the Era of Circumplanetary Ring Detection with Direct Imaging
items.summary: This paper investigates how circumplanetary rings around exoplanets would affect reflected light observations from direct imaging telescopes, motivated by the upcoming Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. The researchers developed a hybrid forward model that combines ray casting to compute mutual shadowing between a planet and its rings with empirical reflectance spectra derived from Cassini observations of Saturn's rings, applied to Jupiter-like planets with icy rings of varying sizes, inclinations, and obliquities. Their simulations reveal that rings can substantially enhance peak flux ratios at favorable geometries, with Saturn-equivalent rings boosting peak flux considerably and more extended rings producing even larger contrasts, though at certain geometries rings can actually suppress total system brightness below that of a ringless planet. The flux contribution of rings is found to be highly sensitive to orbital geometry and obliquity, and the authors identify multi-band photometry as a useful diagnostic for detecting exorings. They conclude that unaccounted-for circumplanetary rings could bias inferred planetary properties from direct imaging data, and must be considered in the planning and interpretation of observations with instruments like the Roman Coronagraph.
items.citation: Samantha N. Hasler, Alexandra Z. Greenbaum, Geoffrey Bryden et al.. Entering the Era of Circumplanetary Ring Detection with Direct Imaging. arXiv. 2026

items.title: AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery
items.summary: This paper investigates whether large language model agents can automate the evaluation of reproducibility and analytical robustness in scientific research, using cancer registry studies as a testbed. The authors constructed a benchmark of published studies based on a widely used U.S. cancer registry, pairing each paper with the data and resources needed to reproduce its findings. An AI agent was then developed to reproduce atomic claims from these studies and to systematically identify the analytical choices underlying each finding, propose defensible alternatives, and rerun analyses to assess whether different choices would change the conclusions. The agent successfully reproduced a substantial majority of atomic claims and, among fully reproduced findings, flagged a meaningful fraction as potentially sensitive to analytical decisions warranting expert review. The authors conclude that LLM agents can meaningfully support scientific peer review by automating reproduction, stress-testing analytical robustness, and directing human expert attention to the most consequential methodological choices.
items.citation: Shicheng Liu, Krista Opsahl-Ong, Andrew Drozdov et al.. AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Detecting Exoplanetary Rings with Roman CGI Reflected Light Phase Curve Observations
items.summary: The paper investigates whether Saturn-like ring systems around giant exoplanets could be detected using the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope's Coronagraph Instrument through reflected light observations. The authors developed an analytical framework for modeling reflected-light phase curves of ringed planets and simulated observations of a specific nearby giant exoplanet as a representative target. They found that rings can outshine their host planets by one to two orders of magnitude or more, making them substantially easier to detect than the unringed planets themselves. A key diagnostic signature is that ringed planets can produce phase curves with four brightness extrema rather than the two expected for ringless planets, enabling rings to be distinguished from bare planets across multiple observation epochs. The study concludes that ring systems may broaden the pool of viable telescope targets beyond planets previously considered too faint to observe, and that such observations could yield the first constraints on how common Saturn-like rings are around giant exoplanets.
items.citation: Elizabeth Lane, Mary Anne Limbach, Logan Pearce et al.. Detecting Exoplanetary Rings with Roman CGI Reflected Light Phase Curve Observations. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Lyapunov Exponents in Power Systems: A Survey of Theory and Applications in Stability, Control, Forecasting, and Protection
items.summary: This survey paper examines the application of Lyapunov exponents, a mathematical tool from nonlinear dynamical systems theory that measures the rate at which nearby trajectories in phase space converge or diverge, to problems in power systems engineering. The authors conducted a comprehensive review spanning several decades of literature, organizing the applications into four domains: stability analysis and real-time monitoring, chaos characterization and control, forecasting and predictability analysis, and protection and fault diagnosis. The review traces the evolution from early demonstrations of chaotic behavior in simplified machine models through to contemporary data-driven and machine-learning-augmented methods applied to modern grids dominated by inverter-based resources. For each domain, the authors compare model-based and data-driven estimation strategies, assess benchmarking and validation practices, and identify open research problems. The paper concludes by highlighting gaps between theoretical developments and practical implementation that remain to be addressed by the research community.
items.citation: Mohammad Almomani, Venkataramana Ajjarapu. Lyapunov Exponents in Power Systems: A Survey of Theory and Applications in Stability, Control, Forecasting, and Protection. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Large Language Model LLM Approach to COVID-19 Fake News Detection
items.summary: This study investigated the use of transformer-based large language models and transfer learning approaches to automatically detect fake news about COVID-19 circulating on social media. The researchers applied seven pretrained models, including BERT, GPT-2, XLNet, and T5 variants, to a labeled dataset of tweets classified as real or fake, and additionally tested six late-fusion ensemble optimization techniques to combine model predictions. Performance was assessed using standard classification metrics alongside confusion matrix visualizations. GPT-2 emerged as the top-performing individual model, while among the fusion strategies, the Nelder-Mead optimization method achieved the highest accuracy. The authors conclude that large language models offer strong utility for pandemic misinformation detection and suggest future work should address multiclass classification, multilingual content, and real-time detection scenarios.
items.citation: Muhammad Arif, Samah Fodeh-Jarad, Elyas Irankhah et al.. A Large Language Model LLM Approach to COVID-19 Fake News Detection. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Trends of nucleic acid – based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases
items.summary: This review examines the landscape of nucleic acid-based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases, motivated by the global need for decentralized, rapid, and accessible testing outside conventional laboratory settings. The authors surveyed the full diagnostic workflow by organizing existing technologies into three operational stages: nucleic acid extraction, amplification, and detection. For extraction, they assess approaches such as magnetic bead-based, paper-based, and integrated microfluidic methods, emphasizing designs that remain simple, rugged, and equipment-free. Amplification strategies reviewed include both thermal cycling methods like PCR and isothermal alternatives such as LAMP, RPA, and NASBA, all of which have been adapted for portable and low-power conditions. On the detection side, the review covers platforms ranging from colorimetric and fluorescent lateral flow assays to advanced biosensors incorporating CRISPR-Cas systems and toehold switch principles, which offer highly sensitive and programmable nucleic acid recognition.
items.citation: Hossam Hatem, Mohamed Mysara, Raghda Ramadan. Trends of nucleic acid – based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases. Journal of Biological Engineering. 2026

items.title: Rapid and Sensitive Detection of <i>Schistosoma mansoni</i> in the Intermediate Snail Hosts Using Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP) Diagnostics.
items.summary: The study addressed the need for improved detection of *Schistosoma mansoni* in its intermediate snail hosts, which is critical for controlling and eliminating schistosomiasis but hampered by the low sensitivity of conventional parasitological methods. Researchers developed a loop-mediated isothermal amplification assay targeting the mitochondrial NADH dehydrogenase subunit 1 gene of *S. mansoni*, optimized it under simple thermal conditions, and evaluated its performance against microscopy, conventional PCR, and real-time PCR using both laboratory-infected snails and field-collected samples from two African countries. In laboratory settings the assay achieved perfect specificity and high sensitivity, outperforming microscopy and matching the performance of real-time PCR. In field surveys, the new assay detected a higher proportion of infected snails than conventional PCR, while microscopy failed to identify any positive specimens in the same samples. The authors conclude that the assay is a sensitive, specific, and practically deployable tool suitable for routine snail surveillance and early detection of shifts in schistosomiasis transmission.
items.citation: Li HM, Qin ZQ, Lv S et al.. Rapid and Sensitive Detection of <i>Schistosoma mansoni</i> in the Intermediate Snail Hosts Using Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP) Diagnostics.. Tropical medicine and infectious disease. 2026

items.title: Point of Care Testing and Recombinase Polymerase Amplification.
items.citation: Weidmann M, El Wahed AA. Point of Care Testing and Recombinase Polymerase Amplification.. Journal of clinical laboratory analysis. 2026

items.title: Development of loop-mediated isothermal amplification and recombinase polymerase amplification combined with lateral flow dipstick assay for the rapid detection of Salmon gill poxvirus.
items.summary: This study addressed the need for rapid field diagnostics for Salmon gill poxvirus, a pathogen capable of causing high mortality in Atlantic salmon hatcheries where early intervention is critical. Researchers developed and evaluated two isothermal amplification methods, loop-mediated isothermal amplification and recombinase polymerase amplification, each paired with a lateral flow device to enable visual detection of the virus from gill mucus samples. Both assays showed high analytical specificity and no cross-reactivity with common salmon gill pathogens, and both agreed well with a reference real-time PCR method when tested on purified DNA. However, the recombinase polymerase amplification approach was consistently inhibited by crude gill mucus, making it poorly suited for direct field use, whereas the loop-mediated isothermal amplification assay performed robustly on unprocessed mucus samples without prior nucleic acid extraction. The loop-mediated isothermal amplification combined with lateral flow detection delivered visual results within minutes, demonstrating strong potential as a practical, non-invasive tool for early outbreak detection and improved management of this virus in salmon aquaculture.
items.citation: Sun B, Weli SC, Dale OB et al.. Development of loop-mediated isothermal amplification and recombinase polymerase amplification combined with lateral flow dipstick assay for the rapid detection of Salmon gill poxvirus.. Journal of virological methods. 2026

items.title: Numerical study of the ITER divertor plasma with the B2-EIRENE code package
items.summary: The abstract is too thin to summarize, as it contains only bibliographic information about a technical report and no scientific content describing the study's methods, objectives, or findings.
items.citation: V. Kotov. Numerical study of the ITER divertor plasma with the B2-EIRENE code package. Dokumentenrepositorium der RUB (Ruhr University Bochum). 2026

items.title: The analysis of natural gemstones and their synthetic counterparts using analytical spectroscopy methods
items.summary: This study examined whether Raman spectroscopy could reliably differentiate natural gemstones from their laboratory-grown synthetic counterparts, focusing on ruby, sapphire, emerald, and spinel. The researchers evaluated both a laboratory Raman spectrometer equipped with two different laser wavelengths and a portable Raman system, applying these instruments to identify gems produced by various manufacturing methods. The laboratory instrument successfully distinguished natural from synthetic gemstones, determined geographic origin among gems of the same color, and demonstrated that emerald analysis required the shorter wavelength laser. The portable system could differentiate between broad stone types but lacked the sensitivity needed to separate natural from synthetic specimens. Repeated measurements confirmed the reliability of the technique, with Raman band positions consistently falling within an acceptable margin of reference values from the literature.
items.citation: Raabell Shah. The analysis of natural gemstones and their synthetic counterparts using analytical spectroscopy methods. Research Output (Edinburgh Napier University). 2026

items.title: Viral metagenomics of synanthropic urban bats: A surveillance strategy for uncovering potentially zoonotic viruses
items.summary: This study developed a framework for detecting bat-borne viruses with zoonotic potential by integrating viral metagenomics into an existing rabies passive surveillance program in Brazil. Using an algorithmic selection process, researchers chose representative bat specimens from a large collection across São Paulo state and subjected paired lung and intestine samples to nanopore metagenomic sequencing. The analysis identified viral contigs spanning multiple viral families of public health concern, including members of Arenaviridae, Coronaviridae, and Paramyxoviridae. A particularly notable finding was the discovery of a previously unknown filovirus in bats from the Americas, demonstrating the framework's capacity to uncover novel pathogens. The approach was validated by multisectoral One Health experts as a scalable, cost-effective model suitable for national expansion and adaptable to the constraints of low- and middle-income countries.
items.citation: Juliana Amorim Conselheiro, Filipe Romero Rebello Moreira, Gisely Toledo Barone et al.. Viral metagenomics of synanthropic urban bats: A surveillance strategy for uncovering potentially zoonotic viruses. One Health. 2026

items.title: Hantavirus Emergence in a Changing World: Virology, Pathogenesis, Surveillance, and One Health Preparedness
items.summary: This review examines hantaviruses, rodent-borne pathogens responsible for hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, in the context of accelerating global environmental change. The authors synthesize current knowledge spanning virology, epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical presentation, diagnostics, and surveillance, with particular attention to how climate variability, urbanization, and land-use transformation alter rodent reservoir dynamics and increase spillover risk to humans. The review identifies significant surveillance and diagnostic gaps in tropical and Caribbean regions where hantavirus circulation is likely underrecognized. Advances in molecular diagnostics, genomic surveillance, vaccine development, monoclonal antibody therapies, and climate-based early warning systems are highlighted as promising tools for improving outbreak detection and response. The authors conclude that integrated One Health surveillance combining human, animal, and environmental monitoring, alongside strengthened laboratory capacity and regional collaboration, is essential for reducing the global burden of hantavirus disease and preparing for future zoonotic threats.
items.citation: Maria E. Ramos‐Niño, Nicolette Chiem, Prakash V. A. K. Ramdass. Hantavirus Emergence in a Changing World: Virology, Pathogenesis, Surveillance, and One Health Preparedness. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Human Metapneumovirus (HMPV): Advances in Diagnosis, Molecular Epidemiology, and Clinical Impact of an Underrecognized Respiratory Virus
items.summary: Human metapneumovirus is a respiratory pathogen that disproportionately affects immunocompromised individuals, the elderly, and young children, though evidence now indicates that healthy adults are also at risk for serious disease. First identified in the early twenty-first century, the virus causes a spectrum of illness ranging from mild upper respiratory infections to severe pneumonia. This review synthesizes current literature on the epidemiology, molecular virology, and clinical characteristics of the virus, highlighting its substantial contribution to respiratory morbidity across populations. The authors emphasize that HMPV remains underrecognized and underappreciated as a public health threat, and they call for improved diagnostic tools and stronger public health measures to address the burden it imposes.
items.citation: ‏Helal F. Hetta, Rehab Ahmed, Abdul Haseeb et al.. Human Metapneumovirus (HMPV): Advances in Diagnosis, Molecular Epidemiology, and Clinical Impact of an Underrecognized Respiratory Virus. Diagnostics. 2026

items.title: Flashing with colours: Photometric indicators of an early interaction in type II supernovae
items.summary: This study examined early-time photometric and spectroscopic properties of Type II supernovae to investigate signatures of interaction between the exploding star and surrounding circumstellar material. Using a combined sample of dozens of Type II supernovae observed with high cadence and precision in multiple optical bands, the researchers categorized events based on the presence or absence of transient narrow emission features from highly ionised elements — known as "flash features" — detected in spectra taken within days of explosion. They found that supernovae displaying these flash features tend to be more luminous at peak brightness, show longer rise times in the blue band, and are systematically bluer than non-flash events, with distinct color distributions persisting for weeks after explosion. Notably, the shape of color-curve evolution, particularly breaks in the color curves within the first month and the change in slopes across those breaks, provides a clear photometric distinction between flash and non-flash supernovae. The results suggest that photometric observations alone, without early spectroscopy, may be sufficient to identify supernovae undergoing interaction with dense circumstellar material.
items.citation: A. Mendez-Llorca, G. Folatelli, C. P. Gutierrez et al.. Flashing with colours: Photometric indicators of an early interaction in type II supernovae. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Experimental Demonstration of a Balanced Travelling Wave Parametric Amplifier
items.summary: This paper studied a balanced architecture for superconducting travelling-wave parametric amplifiers (TWPAs) designed to address a fundamental limitation of three-wave-mixing operation, namely spectral ambiguity arising from the generation of an idler tone at an image frequency. The researchers constructed a balanced amplifier system by connecting two kinetic-inductance TWPAs between a pair of hybrid couplers, arranging the signal and pump to enter and exit through the sum and difference ports respectively, thereby spatially separating the amplified signal from the pump and idler outputs. Through experimental demonstration, they showed that this configuration doubles the instantaneous image-rejected bandwidth compared to a single TWPA, while achieving substantial signal gain across nearly an octave of bandwidth, strong pump rejection, and meaningful image rejection across the operating band. The balanced architecture resolves sideband degeneracy without requiring complex filtering, making it a practical solution for broadband parametric amplification in applications such as qubit readout arrays, spectrometers, and radiometers where wide, unambiguous bandwidth is essential.
items.citation: Nikita Klimovich, Peter K. Day, Henry G. Leduc et al.. Experimental Demonstration of a Balanced Travelling Wave Parametric Amplifier. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Effects of Spanwise Curvature on Hypersonic Boundary Layer Transition in Görtler-driven Flows
items.summary: This study examined how spanwise convex curvature affects hypersonic boundary layer transition on streamwise-concave surfaces, where Görtler instability driven by centrifugal forces typically governs the path to turbulence. Using direct numerical simulation alongside Mach 7 wind tunnel experiments on doubly curved geometries with systematically increasing spanwise convexity, the researchers isolated the three-dimensional curvature effects on an otherwise centrifugally unstable flow. They found that increasing spanwise curvature thins the boundary layer, reducing the effective Görtler number and suppressing the centrifugal amplification of streamwise vortices, which delays transition and pushes secondary instability and turbulent breakdown further downstream. Acoustic instabilities, including the second Mack mode, shift to higher frequencies and become more prominent near breakdown as spanwise curvature increases, but remain subdominant and do not supplant the Görtler-sinuous secondary instability as the principal transition mechanism. Numerical and experimental results agreed in their trends, collectively demonstrating that spanwise convex curvature stabilises hypersonic Görtler-dominated boundary layers while leaving the qualitative transition pathway unchanged.
items.citation: Andrew Welter, Ngoc Cuong Nguyen, Nicholas Webber et al.. Effects of Spanwise Curvature on Hypersonic Boundary Layer Transition in Görtler-driven Flows. arXiv. 2026

items.title: LagNet: Lag-Structured Operators for Long-Term Time Series Forecasting
items.summary: The paper investigates long-term time series forecasting by examining the structural form of the history-to-future mapping operator rather than focusing solely on input representations or model architectures. Through analysis of sensitivity matrices across different model families, the authors identify recurring diagonal patterns corresponding to relative temporal lags, motivating a framework built around lag-structured temporal operators. The core component, called LagLayer, constructs a Toeplitz matrix by tying history-to-future connections that share the same relative lag, augmented with scaling coefficients to allow flexible relaxation of strict parameter sharing. Stacking these layers with nonlinear activations and multiple feature maps produces the full LagNet architecture, which can also serve as a drop-in replacement for temporal linear layers in existing models. Experiments on standard benchmarks show LagNet is competitive with strong baselines, and additional diagnostics and limited-data evaluations indicate that the lag-structured design offers improved sample efficiency over conventional linear layers.
items.citation: Zhenan Yu, Guangxin Jiang, Jiuyun Jiang et al.. LagNet: Lag-Structured Operators for Long-Term Time Series Forecasting. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Escaping Parameter Space: Tight Generalization Bounds via Representation Quality
items.summary: This paper derives a generalization bound for deterministic neural networks that operates in representation space rather than parameter space, using the quality of last-hidden-layer embeddings as evaluated by a parameter-free k-nearest-neighbor classifier. The bound avoids traditional complexity measures such as weight norms, KL divergences, and compression schemes, instead decomposing additively into three independently measurable empirical quantities: local class geometry, decoder-network agreement, and training stability. Applied to standard benchmarks, the bound achieves tight, non-vacuous certificates both for networks trained from scratch and for frozen pretrained representations, including on large-scale datasets where previous approaches have failed. The authors use the framework as a diagnostic tool, demonstrating that deliberately disrupting local class geometry in representation space eliminates generalization while leaving memorization intact, establishing class geometry as a causally relevant mechanism for generalization. They also show that learned representations are substantially more robust to weight noise than linear readouts, offering an explanation for why parameter-space certificates tend to be loose.
items.citation: Niclas Göring, Shuofeng Zhang, Branton DeMoss et al.. Escaping Parameter Space: Tight Generalization Bounds via Representation Quality. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Hectospec Spectroscopic Census of Kinematic Members in the Orion Nebula Cluster
items.summary: This paper presents a large-scale spectroscopic survey of the Orion Nebula Cluster aimed at comprehensively characterizing its stellar membership and physical properties. Using low-resolution optical spectroscopy from MMT/Hectospec, the researchers derived spectral types, youth indicators, and accretion diagnostics for over a thousand stars in the cluster region, which were then combined with kinematic membership analysis based on Gaia astrometry to identify confirmed pre-main-sequence members. Infrared photometry from the Spitzer Space Telescope was incorporated to construct a census of protoplanetary disks, while stellar masses, ages, and extinctions were estimated using a code that combines photometric and spectroscopic data with stellar evolutionary models via a Monte Carlo approach. The study ultimately identifies hundreds of bona fide T Tauri stars associated with the cluster and assembles a homogeneous catalog providing spectroscopic characterizations, membership constraints, disk diagnostics, and self-consistent stellar parameters. This catalog is presented as a robust foundation for future investigations into the cluster's kinematic structure, age distribution, and protoplanetary disk population.
items.citation: Jesús Hernández, Ezequiel Manzo-Martínez, Lucía Adame et al.. A Hectospec Spectroscopic Census of Kinematic Members in the Orion Nebula Cluster. arXiv. 2026

items.title: From sepsis biomarker discovery to regulated in vitro diagnostics: evidence, certification status and implementation gaps
items.citation: Plata-Menchaca E, Hernández-Jiménez E. From sepsis biomarker discovery to regulated in vitro diagnostics: evidence, certification status and implementation gaps. Frontiers in medical technology. 2026

items.title: Mechanism-informed diagnostic accuracy of blood biomarkers for sepsis-associated encephalopathy: a systematic review and Bayesian diagnostic network meta-analysis.
items.summary: This systematic review and Bayesian diagnostic network meta-analysis investigated the diagnostic accuracy of blood biomarkers for sepsis-associated encephalopathy, a severe form of acute brain dysfunction complicating sepsis. The authors searched multiple international databases and applied a mechanism-informed framework organizing candidate biomarkers along an immune activation, blood-brain barrier dysfunction, glial response, and neuronal injury axis, synthesizing evidence from studies with extractable diagnostic data and accounting for heterogeneity in case definitions and biomarker sampling timing. Pooled analyses indicated that blood-brain barrier and glial markers such as GFAP and S100β demonstrated more balanced diagnostic discrimination than classic neuronal injury markers, while Bayesian comparative ranking placed upstream immune and alarmin candidates alongside day-three S100β among the highest-ranked biomarkers. However, several top-ranked candidates were supported by only single studies, and few studies evaluated whether biomarkers provide diagnostic value beyond established clinical predictors such as illness severity scores or sedation-related confounders. The authors conclude that findings are hypothesis-generating and call for prospective, head-to-head validation studies using standardized phenotyping and anchor-based sampling protocols to determine whether mechanism-staged biomarker panels offer incremental clinical utility.
items.citation: Zhang Q, Zhu R, Li Y et al.. Mechanism-informed diagnostic accuracy of blood biomarkers for sepsis-associated encephalopathy: a systematic review and Bayesian diagnostic network meta-analysis.. Frontiers in molecular neuroscience. 2026

items.title: Dynamic Changes of Neutrophil Nuclear Membrane CD63 as a Potential Biomarker for Early Adjunctive Diagnosis and Prognostic Evaluation of Sepsis in Critically Ill Patients: A Prospective Cohort Study.
items.summary: This prospective cohort study investigated whether neutrophil nuclear membrane CD63 (nmCD63), a marker of targeted nuclear degranulation during neutrophil extracellular trap formation, could serve as an early biomarker for sepsis diagnosis and prognosis in critically ill patients. The researchers developed a flow cytometry assay to quantify nmCD63 and validated it across two centers using a derivation cohort and an independent external validation cohort, establishing diagnostic cutoffs and combined models without recalibration between cohorts. They found that nmCD63 levels rose progressively with disease severity and outperformed conventional biomarkers such as C-reactive protein and procalcitonin in distinguishing non-infectious systemic inflammation from infection. When combined with organ failure scoring, nmCD63 achieved strong discriminatory performance for identifying sepsis in infected patients. Crucially, dynamic changes in nmCD63 preceded shifts in all conventional biomarkers, and trajectory analysis over seven days allowed reliable prognostic stratification, supporting its dual clinical utility for early sepsis diagnosis and outcome prediction.
items.citation: Gao X, Zhang M, Li L et al.. Dynamic Changes of Neutrophil Nuclear Membrane CD63 as a Potential Biomarker for Early Adjunctive Diagnosis and Prognostic Evaluation of Sepsis in Critically Ill Patients: A Prospective Cohort Study.. MedComm. 2026

items.title: Clinical utility of combined serum IL-6, PCT, and SAA assays for early diagnosis and severity stratification of neonatal sepsis.
items.summary: This study investigated whether combining three serum biomarkers—interleukin-6, procalcitonin, and serum amyloid A—could improve early diagnosis and severity stratification of neonatal sepsis compared to using any single marker alone. Neonates admitted to an intensive care unit were grouped into confirmed sepsis, suspected sepsis, and non-infective controls, with sepsis cases further divided by severity, and all biomarkers were measured at admission before antibiotic treatment. All three markers were significantly elevated in confirmed sepsis relative to the other groups and were also higher in severe compared to mild or moderate cases. The combined three-biomarker panel achieved a diagnostic accuracy substantially greater than any individual marker, with high sensitivity and specificity. The authors conclude that simultaneous measurement of these three biomarkers provides a rapid and reliable complement to blood culture for early neonatal sepsis diagnosis and severity grading in intensive care settings.
items.citation: Jiang Y, Yang J, Yang S. Clinical utility of combined serum IL-6, PCT, and SAA assays for early diagnosis and severity stratification of neonatal sepsis.. Frontiers in medicine. 2026

items.title: Interpretable admission-stage machine learning for early Sepsis-3 identification in the emergency department.
items.summary: The study aimed to develop and evaluate interpretable machine learning models for identifying Sepsis-3-defined sepsis at the time of emergency department admission, comparing their performance against conventional biomarkers and the Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome criteria. Using a prospective cohort of adult emergency department patients with suspected community-onset sepsis, the researchers applied feature selection and trained four models—penalized logistic regression, Explainable Boosting Machine, Extreme Gradient Boosting, and Light Gradient Boosting Machine—on routinely available demographic, physiological, and laboratory variables. All four machine learning models achieved moderate discriminative performance, with no statistically significant differences among them, while outperforming conventional biomarkers and SIRS criteria to varying degrees. Age, procalcitonin, oxygen saturation, respiratory rate, and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio emerged as the most influential predictors across models. The authors conclude that interpretable machine learning offers clinically relevant sensitivity and transparent predictor effects for early sepsis identification, though external validation is needed before clinical deployment.
items.citation: Cantaş Türkiş F, Varol B. Interpretable admission-stage machine learning for early Sepsis-3 identification in the emergency department.. Frontiers in medicine. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic accuracy of procalcitonin for identifying paediatric sepsis: A retrospective study in a Malaysian tertiary hospital.
items.summary: This retrospective study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of serum procalcitonin (PCT) as a biomarker for identifying sepsis in children presenting to a Malaysian tertiary referral hospital. Children aged one month to eighteen years who underwent PCT testing for suspected infection were classified as having sepsis or non-sepsis using established paediatric consensus criteria, with PCT performance compared against C-reactive protein and total white cell count using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis. PCT concentrations were significantly elevated in the sepsis group, and at an optimal cut-off the biomarker demonstrated moderate sensitivity and specificity, with an area under the curve indicating moderate overall diagnostic accuracy. PCT showed a moderate positive correlation with C-reactive protein but no meaningful correlation with total white cell count. The authors conclude that PCT may serve as a useful adjunctive tool in the early evaluation of paediatric sepsis but should not be used in isolation, requiring integration with clinical assessment and microbiological investigations.
items.citation: Razak SMA, Taib MNA, Abdul Jalil K et al.. Diagnostic accuracy of procalcitonin for identifying paediatric sepsis: A retrospective study in a Malaysian tertiary hospital.. The Medical journal of Malaysia. 2026

items.title: Gut microbial-derived metabolites: key players in kidney disease and renal fibrosis
items.summary: This review examines the relationship between gut microbial-derived metabolites and kidney disease, focusing on how disruptions in gut microbiota composition contribute to renal injury and fibrosis. The authors synthesize current evidence showing that kidney disease creates a bidirectional cycle in which renal injury promotes intestinal barrier dysfunction and microbial dysbiosis, which in turn reduces beneficial short-chain fatty acids while allowing uremic toxins to accumulate. These metabolic shifts influence kidney pathology through multiple signaling pathways, with tryptophan metabolites identified as particularly important mediators of gut-kidney communication. The review covers the implications of these mechanisms across several conditions including acute kidney injury, chronic kidney disease, diabetic kidney disease, and immune-mediated nephropathies. The authors also evaluate therapeutic strategies targeting gut microbiota dysbiosis, including natural products, prebiotics, probiotics, and renal replacement therapy, with the goal of informing more precise treatment approaches.
items.citation: Wan-Ying Zhang, Yu-Lu Zhang, Qing-Qing Yu et al.. Gut microbial-derived metabolites: key players in kidney disease and renal fibrosis. International Journal of Biological Sciences. 2026

items.title: A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression
items.summary: This systematic review examined how different forms of exercise influence the expression of Toll-like receptors, a family of immune cell receptors central to inflammatory signalling and implicated in the chronic low-grade inflammation associated with sedentary lifestyles and non-communicable diseases. The authors searched multiple databases and included studies in which exercise was the sole intervention in human participants, categorising findings by exercise type and duration across acute and chronic modalities. Acute resistance exercise appeared to upregulate TLR expression, while acute aerobic exercise showed a more neutral or downregulatory effect, particularly in healthy individuals. Chronic resistance and combined training programmes predominantly led to unchanged or decreased TLR levels, whereas chronic aerobic training produced mixed results with most measurements showing no change in expression. The authors conclude that exercise modulates TLR signalling in a manner dependent on exercise characteristics, but highlight substantial heterogeneity across study designs and call for further research to clarify the mechanisms and pathophysiological implications involved.
items.citation: Kasper Favere, Matthias Bosman, Peter Delputte et al.. A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Federated Learning in Multimodal Healthcare Diagnostics: Privacy-Preserving AI for Biomedical Imaging, Electronic Health Records, Wearables, and Clinical Decision Support
items.summary: This review paper examines the application of federated learning as a privacy-preserving approach to training artificial intelligence models across diverse healthcare data modalities, including biomedical imaging, electronic health records, wearable sensor outputs, and clinical decision support systems. The authors conducted a literature review spanning multiple clinical domains such as chronic disease management, elder care, and diagnostic imaging, synthesizing how federated learning enables multi-institutional AI model training without transferring raw patient data by sharing only model updates between collaborating sites. The paper clarifies that while federated learning reduces direct data exposure and improves alignment with privacy regulations, it does not automatically guarantee confidentiality, as vulnerabilities such as gradient leakage, model inversion, and membership inference attacks still pose meaningful risks. The review identifies persistent barriers to real-world implementation, including system heterogeneity across institutions, data imbalance, communication bottlenecks, and concerns about algorithmic fairness. Based on this synthesis, the authors provide actionable recommendations for regulators, developers, and healthcare systems aimed at advancing safe, equitable, and geographically distributed federated learning deployments in medicine.
items.venue: Archives of Computational Methods in Engineering
items.citation: Shon G. Nemane, Vaishnavi M. Sarad, Dhiraj P. Tulaskar et al.. Federated Learning in Multimodal Healthcare Diagnostics: Privacy-Preserving AI for Biomedical Imaging, Electronic Health Records, Wearables, and Clinical Decision Support. Archives of Computational Methods in Engineering. 2026

items.title: Pseudomonas aeruginosa: associated pathogenesis, epidemiology, resistance mechanisms, host response and emerging treatment strategies
items.summary: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a critical-priority pathogen responsible for a substantial proportion of healthcare-associated infections globally, with particularly high mortality in intensive care settings and a dominant role in chronic lung disease such as cystic fibrosis. This review examines the organism's pathogenic mechanisms, epidemiology, resistance landscape, and interactions with the host immune system. Key virulence features discussed include biofilm formation, which dramatically increases antimicrobial tolerance, as well as quorum sensing, phenazine and rhamnolipid production, and the toxin pyocyanin, which damages host tissues through multiple cellular mechanisms. During chronic infection, host defences including epithelial barriers, mucociliary clearance, and immune cell responses become progressively less effective, permitting persistent bacterial colonisation and inflammation. Rising rates of multidrug and carbapenem resistance are driving investigation of alternative therapeutic strategies such as anti-virulence agents, biofilm-disrupting enzymes, nanoparticles, bacteriophage therapy, and host-directed immunomodulatory approaches.
items.citation: Sheeba Sawant, Safura Shaikh, Timothy Baldwin et al.. Pseudomonas aeruginosa: associated pathogenesis, epidemiology, resistance mechanisms, host response and emerging treatment strategies. Archives of Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Stimuli-responsive nanocarriers for precision targeted and controlled antimicrobial drug delivery in drug-resistant infections
items.summary: This review paper examined stimuli-responsive nanocarriers as a strategy for targeted antimicrobial drug delivery in the context of drug-resistant infections. The authors analyzed how infected tissues present distinct microenvironmental characteristics — including acidic pH, elevated reactive oxygen species, enzymatic activity, hypoxia, and inflammatory signaling — that can serve as triggers for controlled drug release, contrasting these with the non-specific systemic distribution of conventional antibiotics. The review systematically covered the mechanistic principles underlying pH-, enzyme-, redox-, and multi-stimuli-responsive nanocarrier systems, detailing how physicochemical transformations upon trigger activation govern drug retention, penetration, and release specifically within resistant infection sites. The authors compared these platforms against passive nanocarriers and free antibiotics, arguing that infection-synchronized delivery can enhance antimicrobial efficacy, reduce off-target toxicity, and lessen resistance-selective pressure by addressing barriers such as biofilm tolerance, intracellular pathogen persistence, and efflux-mediated drug extrusion. The review also critically evaluated translational obstacles including microenvironmental heterogeneity, trigger variability, manufacturing scalability, and regulatory complexity, concluding that stimuli-responsive nanocarriers represent a meaningful shift toward context-aware, site-selective antimicrobial intervention.
items.citation: Li Dai, Xiaoyan Sun. Stimuli-responsive nanocarriers for precision targeted and controlled antimicrobial drug delivery in drug-resistant infections. Frontiers in Microbiology. 2026

items.title: The Gut–Vagina Axis
items.summary: This review paper examines the gut–vagina axis, a concept describing bidirectional communication between the gut and vaginal microbiomes and its implications for female health. The authors synthesize current microbiome research to explore how these two distinct microbial communities interact through mechanisms including microbial migration, hormonal and immune regulation, and metabolite exchange. The review identifies the most promising features of this gut–vaginal relationship and discusses how disruptions or alterations in these interactions may influence microbial composition, immune responses, and hormonal balance at both local and systemic levels. The authors argue that understanding this bidirectional communication could have meaningful implications for female physiological health more broadly.
items.citation: Lorenzo Agoni, Elena Roselletti, Giovanni Marasco et al.. The Gut–Vagina Axis. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Flashing with colours: Photometric indicators of an early interaction in type II supernovae
items.summary: This paper investigated early-time photometric and spectroscopic properties of Type II supernovae to identify signatures of interaction between the explosion and dense circumstellar material surrounding the progenitor star. The researchers assembled a large sample of Type II supernovae, combining newly observed events with literature objects, and classified them based on the presence or absence of transient narrow emission lines from highly ionised elements — so-called "flash features" — detected in spectra taken within four days of explosion. They found that supernovae displaying flash features tend to be more luminous at peak, show longer rise times in the blue band, and appear systematically bluer than non-flash events, with these colour differences most pronounced around three weeks post-explosion and likely reflecting intrinsic physical differences rather than dust extinction. Crucially, the study identified that breaks in the colour-curve evolution occurring within the first month after explosion, combined with peak absolute magnitude, provide a powerful photometric diagnostic capable of distinguishing flash from non-flash supernovae. This result suggests that circumstellar interaction in Type II supernovae can be identified from photometry alone, without requiring early-time spectroscopy, which has important implications for large photometric surveys.
items.citation: A. Mendez-Llorca, G. Folatelli, C. P. Gutierrez et al.. Flashing with colours: Photometric indicators of an early interaction in type II supernovae. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Entering the Era of Circumplanetary Ring Detection with Direct Imaging
items.summary: This paper investigates how circumplanetary rings around exoplanets would affect reflected light observations from upcoming direct imaging missions, particularly the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. The researchers developed a hybrid forward model that combines ray casting to simulate mutual shadowing between planets and rings with empirical reflectance data from Cassini observations of Saturn's rings, applied to Jupiter-like planets hosting rings of varying sizes, inclinations, and obliquities. Their simulations demonstrate that rings can dramatically enhance planet-ring system brightness at favorable geometries, with Saturn-equivalent rings boosting peak flux substantially and more extended rings producing even greater contrast enhancements, though at certain geometries rings can actually suppress total brightness below that of a ringless planet. The flux contribution of rings was found to be highly sensitive to orbital geometry and obliquity, and multi-band photometry is identified as a useful diagnostic for detecting exorings. The authors conclude that unaccounted-for rings could bias inferred planetary properties from direct imaging data and must be considered in observation planning and interpretation, with an application to a known directly imaged planet serving as an observational test case.
items.citation: Samantha N. Hasler, Alexandra Z. Greenbaum, Geoffrey Bryden et al.. Entering the Era of Circumplanetary Ring Detection with Direct Imaging. arXiv. 2026

items.title: AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery
items.summary: This paper investigated whether large language model agents can automate the evaluation of reproducibility and analytical robustness in scientific research, addressing the high cost of manual verification. The researchers focused on published studies using a major U.S. cancer registry database, constructing a benchmark of published papers along with the data and resources needed to reproduce their findings. An AI agent was developed that successfully reproduced a substantial majority of atomic claims across these papers, and a separate agentic pipeline was built to test robustness by identifying analytical choices, proposing defensible alternatives, and rerunning analyses to assess their impact on conclusions. The pipeline flagged a notable fraction of fully reproduced findings as potentially sensitive to analytical choices, directing these for expert review. The work demonstrates that LLM agents can meaningfully assist scientific peer review by automating reproduction, systematically probing robustness, and prioritizing human attention toward findings most in need of scrutiny.
items.citation: Shicheng Liu, Krista Opsahl-Ong, Andrew Drozdov et al.. AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Demonstration of Logical Error Suppression in a Surface Code Memory on a Cloud-Accessible IBM Superconducting Processor
items.summary: This paper investigates quantum error correction using rotated surface-code memory implemented on a cloud-accessible superconducting processor, with the goal of demonstrating logical error suppression as code distance increases. The researchers optimized syndrome extraction circuits by combining short readout, fused measurement and reset, and an echo sequence applied to data qubits during ancilla readout, then compared performance against standard readout approaches across multiple placements on the processor. The optimized circuit substantially reduced logical error rates relative to the unoptimized baseline, with the improvement being more pronounced in one measurement basis than the other, highlighting the role of noise asymmetry. Increasing code distance from three to six produced clear reductions in per-round logical error rates and error-suppression factors above one under maximum-likelihood decoding, confirming that the hardware is operating below the fault-tolerance threshold, though long-lived temporal correlations observed in extended experiments suggest a persistent error component that limits scaling. The authors conclude that careful circuit compilation and hardware-level co-design are essential for translating surface-code theory into practical performance gains on current quantum cloud hardware.
items.citation: Shuwen Kan, Aaron Hoyt, Sean Garner et al.. Demonstration of Logical Error Suppression in a Surface Code Memory on a Cloud-Accessible IBM Superconducting Processor. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Leveraging verifiable structure in quantum circuits to find more efficient compilations with agentic AI
items.summary: This paper explores how AI agents can be used to find more efficient quantum circuit compilations when key subroutines possess classically verifiable structure. The central insight is that bottleneck subroutines composed of reversible classical logic, phasing operations, and measurement-based uncomputation can be efficiently simulated on classical inputs, enabling approximate circuit synthesis to be certified through fuzz testing under suitable assumptions on the input distribution. The authors demonstrate the flexibility of this approach across three application domains: computing the inverse square root function relevant to simulating the Coulomb operator in inertial confinement fusion modeling, decoding Reed-Solomon codes that bottleneck a quantum interferometry algorithm for polynomial intersection problems, and optimizing quantum look-up tables and Givens rotations central to chemistry simulation in second quantization. The paper provides reference implementations of these algorithms along with verification frameworks, and uses these as the basis for a Kaggle competition intended to accelerate AI-driven research into quantum circuit optimization.
items.citation: Tanuj Khattar, Nicholas C. Rubin, Craig Gidney et al.. Leveraging verifiable structure in quantum circuits to find more efficient compilations with agentic AI. arXiv. 2026

items.title: ENFR: Evidence Networks with Flow-Matched References for Amortized Simulation-Based Model Inference
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of computing the Bayesian evidence, the marginal likelihood of observed data under a model, which is a critical quantity for model comparison, goodness-of-fit testing, and detecting model misspecification in simulation-based inference settings. The authors introduce ENFR (Evidence Networks with Flow-matched References), a method that learns Bayes factors relative to a flow-matched reference distribution and then recovers absolute evidence values through amortized neural network training, building on an existing Evidence Network framework. A key theoretical contribution is a novel architecture with accompanying proof that jointly estimates the individual evidences for an entire set of competing models simultaneously. Across a range of scientific benchmark applications, ENFR outperforms flow-based baselines and other density estimation approaches in evidence estimation accuracy and computational efficiency. The work also highlights that using the evidence as a test statistic naturally induces a minimum-volume hypothesis test, making it a principled tool for assessing model fidelity before trusting downstream parameter inference.
items.citation: Kai Lehman, Jameson Dong, Carolina Cuesta-Lazaro et al.. ENFR: Evidence Networks with Flow-Matched References for Amortized Simulation-Based Model Inference. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Rapid Diagnostics for Antimicrobial Resistance: From Bench to Bedside
items.citation: Mugisha N, Fawaz L, Noureddine R et al.. Artificial Intelligence in Rapid Diagnostics for Antimicrobial Resistance: From Bench to Bedside. Health science reports. 2026

items.title: Integrated evaluation of rapid diagnostic testing, genotypic-phenotypic resistance profiling, and AI-Assisted prediction models for antimicrobial stewardship and clinical outcomes in a resource-limited setting.
items.summary: This prospective observational study examined whether combining rapid diagnostic testing, molecular resistance gene profiling, and an artificial intelligence prediction model could improve antimicrobial stewardship and patient outcomes in a resource-limited hospital setting. Adult patients with suspected bacterial infections were enrolled and evaluated using conventional antibiotic susceptibility testing alongside these integrated approaches, with outcomes tracked including time to effective therapy, antibiotic appropriateness, length of hospital stay, and mortality. The integrated approach dramatically shortened the time to pathogen identification and initiation of appropriate therapy compared to conventional methods alone, and substantially increased the rate of appropriate antibiotic prescribing while reducing broad-spectrum antibiotic use. Patients managed under the integrated approach experienced shorter hospital stays and lower mortality, and the AI model showed strong discriminatory performance in predicting antimicrobial resistance. The authors conclude that this combined diagnostic and predictive strategy represents a potentially cost-effective and scalable tool for combating antimicrobial resistance, particularly in settings with limited resources.
items.citation: Hammad M, Arif R, Fardoos S et al.. Integrated evaluation of rapid diagnostic testing, genotypic-phenotypic resistance profiling, and AI-Assisted prediction models for antimicrobial stewardship and clinical outcomes in a resource-limited setting.. PloS one. 2026

items.title: Recent Advances and Future Perspectives in the Detection of Carbapenem-Resistant <i>Acinetobacter Baumannii</i>.
items.summary: This review examines the detection of carbapenem-resistant *Acinetobacter baumannii*, a pathogen classified as a critical priority by the World Health Organization due to its multidrug resistance, nosocomial transmission, and limited treatment options. The authors surveyed a broad range of detection technologies, from conventional phenotypic and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to molecular amplification methods, mass spectrometry, whole-genome and metagenomic sequencing, AI-assisted diagnostics, and biosensor or CRISPR-integrated platforms. They found that while culture-based susceptibility testing remains the reference standard, its lengthy turnaround time limits early clinical decision-making, whereas molecular methods such as PCR and isothermal amplification approaches substantially reduce detection times and support point-of-care applications. Emerging genomic tools enable comprehensive resistance profiling and outbreak surveillance, and biosensor-based platforms offer sensitive and portable detection, though challenges around standardization, multiplexing, cost, and clinical validation persist. The review concludes that the field is transitioning toward integrated, automated, and clinically adaptable diagnostic platforms that must balance analytical performance, speed, cost, and suitability for point-of-care use.
items.citation: Ye Q, Liu Y, Zhang K et al.. Recent Advances and Future Perspectives in the Detection of Carbapenem-Resistant <i>Acinetobacter Baumannii</i>.. Infection and drug resistance. 2026

items.title: Concordance of AI-driven antimicrobial recommendations using rapid molecular versus phenotypic-optimized workflows for bloodstream infections: a prospective study in a resource-limited setting
items.summary: This prospective study evaluated an integrated diagnostic-therapeutic program for bloodstream infections that combined rapid molecular diagnostics with AI clinical decision support, followed by conventional culture-based phenotypic testing with AI optimization. Researchers analyzed consecutive monomicrobial bloodstream infection episodes processed through parallel workflows using two rapid molecular platforms alongside conventional culture with mass spectrometry identification and susceptibility testing, each paired with distinct AI recommendation tools. Molecular diagnostics substantially reduced diagnostic turnaround time compared to conventional methods, with bacterial identification and antimicrobial resistance detection showing high concordance between the two workflow approaches. Resistance detection discordance emerged as the sole independent predictor of therapeutic recommendation discordance, and while the molecular-AI pathway delivered appropriate therapy substantially earlier in the majority of cases without requiring adjustment, phenotypic-AI optimization ensured completely appropriate therapy across all cases. The authors conclude that combining rapid molecular-AI initial guidance with phenotypic-AI optimization supports implementation in antimicrobial stewardship programs, particularly in resource-limited settings.
items.citation: Torre JCGdl, Frenkel A, Chavez-Lencinas C et al.. Concordance of AI-driven antimicrobial recommendations using rapid molecular versus phenotypic-optimized workflows for bloodstream infections: a prospective study in a resource-limited setting. 2026

items.title: PMAxx dye-assisted colorimetric dual DNAzyme-LAMP (PD-cDDLAMP) for rapid phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing of <i>Escherichia coli</i>.
items.summary: This paper developed a rapid nucleic acid-based phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing method called PD-cDDLAMP to address the slow turnaround times of conventional approaches and the limited scope of genotypic methods. The technique uses a photoreactive DNA-crosslinking dye (PMAxx) that selectively binds to the DNA of membrane-compromised, antibiotic-susceptible bacteria, suppressing their nucleic acid amplification while leaving resistant bacteria unaffected, producing a simple colorimetric signal via a dual DNAzyme-LAMP readout system. By exploiting this selective suppression, the assay can reliably distinguish antibiotic-resistant ("signal-on") from antibiotic-susceptible ("signal-off") Escherichia coli after only thirty minutes of antibiotic exposure, far shorter than the hours required by existing LAMP-based phenotypic methods. Testing against ampicillin and tetracycline yielded high sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy, and the method was further validated in spiked milk samples, demonstrating applicability in complex matrices such as dairy farming environments. The authors conclude that PD-cDDLAMP's speed, minimal instrumentation requirements, and equipment-free readout make it a promising point-of-care tool for rapid antimicrobial susceptibility testing in clinical and on-site settings.
items.citation: Sewid AH, Ramos JH, Gelalcha BD et al.. PMAxx dye-assisted colorimetric dual DNAzyme-LAMP (PD-cDDLAMP) for rapid phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing of <i>Escherichia coli</i>.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: Antimicrobial stewardship challenges during the COVID-19 pandemic: implications of antibiotic overuse and antimicrobial resistance.
items.summary: This narrative review examined the relationship between the COVID-19 pandemic and antibiotic prescribing practices, with a focus on bacterial co-infections, antimicrobial resistance, and stewardship strategies. The authors conducted a systematic literature search across multiple major databases, selecting studies according to predefined criteria to synthesize evidence on prescribing patterns and their consequences. Despite relatively low rates of confirmed bacterial co-infections among COVID-19 patients, antibiotic use was disproportionately high, especially during the early pandemic period when diagnostic uncertainty complicated clinical decision-making. This excessive and inappropriate prescribing is thought to have contributed to the global burden of antimicrobial resistance. The review concludes that strengthening antimicrobial stewardship programmes, improving diagnostic accuracy through rapid molecular tools, promoting evidence-based prescribing, and adopting a One Health framework are essential complementary strategies to limit unnecessary antimicrobial exposure and mitigate long-term resistance consequences.
items.venue: Arhiv za higijenu rada i toksikologiju
items.citation: Špelić M, Krajinović V. Antimicrobial stewardship challenges during the COVID-19 pandemic: implications of antibiotic overuse and antimicrobial resistance.. Arhiv za higijenu rada i toksikologiju. 2026

items.title: Accelerating scientific discovery with Co-Scientist
items.summary: This paper introduces Co-Scientist, a multi-agent AI system built on Gemini that is designed to augment scientific discovery by generating, critiquing, and refining research hypotheses through structured scientific reasoning. The system employs an asynchronous task execution framework for flexible compute scaling and a tournament evolution process that enables self-improving hypothesis generation, with automated evaluations demonstrating that hypothesis quality improves as test-time compute increases.
