Although designed as a general-purpose tool, the system was validated in three biomedical domains: drug repurposing, novel-target discovery, and understanding mechanisms of antimicrobial resistance. Most notably, Co-Scientist identified new drug-repurposing candidates and synergistic combination therapies for acute myeloid leukaemia that were subsequently confirmed through laboratory experiments. These real-world validations support the claim that AI systems of this type have genuine potential to accelerate the pace of scientific discovery.
items.citation: Juraj Gottweis, Wei‐Hung Weng, Alexander Daryin et al.. Accelerating scientific discovery with Co-Scientist. Nature. 2026

items.title: Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications
items.summary: This review examines how the integration of multiomics technologies and artificial intelligence is reshaping precision drug discovery and clinical translation. The paper synthesizes how approaches spanning genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics generate deep molecular insights into disease pathogenesis, while deep learning architectures decode the resulting complex biological datasets to identify patterns and build predictive models. The authors analyze the combined application of these technologies across the drug development pipeline, including target identification, drug repositioning, de novo compound discovery, virtual screening, pharmacokinetic modeling, and safety assessment. Case studies in oncology, neurodegenerative diseases, and cardiovascular conditions are used to illustrate the practical potential of this convergence, though the review also acknowledges persistent challenges such as harmonizing disparate data streams, ensuring reproducibility, and mitigating algorithmic biases. The authors conclude that the fusion of multiomics with artificial intelligence represents a foundational shift toward more precise therapeutic interventions and a new era of bench-to-clinic translational medicine.
items.citation: Yuqing Liu, Kun Zhu, Weijun Peng et al.. Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Soil microbes are the tiny bioengineers running Earth’s underground factory
items.summary: This paper synthesizes current research on soil microbial communities, focusing on how their diversity connects to ecosystem function. The authors developed a function-centred framework that identifies four conserved functional axes — secondary metabolism, nutrient cycling, community interactions, and stress tolerance — that together govern key soil processes. They propose that soil operates as a self-organizing system in which microbial interactions produce emergent ecosystem-level behaviours, though the expression of these functions is strongly context dependent. The framework is intended to support predictive, ecology-informed strategies for managing soil systems in the service of sustainable agriculture, environmental remediation, and climate mitigation.
items.citation: Suzanne Hassan-Dalléac, Wafa Guiga, Antonia Suau. Soil microbes are the tiny bioengineers running Earth’s underground factory. Communications Earth & Environment. 2026

items.title: Arc mediates intercellular tau transmission via extracellular vesicles
items.summary: The paper investigated the mechanisms by which misfolded tau protein spreads between cells in neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal dementia. The researchers focused on the neuronal gene Arc, examining its role in packaging tau into extracellular vesicles using transgenic mouse models, including crosses with Arc knockout animals, as well as human brain tissue. They found that Arc is essential for loading tau into extracellular vesicles through a pathway involving the I-BAR protein IRSp53, and that Arc protein directly binds tau to form a complex detectable in both mouse and human brain. When Arc was absent, extracellular vesicles contained substantially less tau and were unable to seed tau aggregation, while tau instead accumulated intracellularly in neurons, correlating with accelerated hippocampal neuron loss. The authors conclude that Arc-dependent packaging of tau into extracellular vesicles serves a dual function: facilitating the clearance of tau from within neurons and enabling its intercellular transmission.
items.citation: Mitali Tyagi, Eric de Hoog, Matthew Grega et al.. Arc mediates intercellular tau transmission via extracellular vesicles. Cell. 2026

items.title: Synthesis and multilevel evaluation of benzimidazole-based anticancer compounds: DNA/serum albumin interaction, and in-depth theoretical insights
items.summary: Two novel benzimidazole-based compounds were synthesized and evaluated for their potential as anticancer agents against multiple cancer cell lines, including lung, breast, and liver cancers, alongside a healthy cell line. The study employed a broad multilevel approach encompassing cytotoxicity assays, gene expression analysis of apoptotic and oxidative stress markers, cellular senescence assessment, DNA and serum albumin binding studies using fluorescence spectroscopy, and computational analyses including density functional theory calculations and molecular docking. One compound showed notably potent cytotoxic activity against breast and liver cancer cell lines, while both compounds downregulated anti-apoptotic genes and upregulated pro-apoptotic genes in breast cancer cells, accompanied by elevated oxidative stress and induction of cellular senescence. Fluorescence spectroscopy revealed strong intercalative binding of both compounds to DNA, with high binding constants, and moderate affinity toward serum albumin, suggesting favorable transport properties with limited nonspecific protein interaction. Collectively, the experimental and theoretical findings support these benzimidazole derivatives as promising candidates for further development as anticancer agents.
items.citation: Sevgi Kundu, Senem Akkoç, Yalçın Erzurumlu et al.. Synthesis and multilevel evaluation of benzimidazole-based anticancer compounds: DNA/serum albumin interaction, and in-depth theoretical insights. Molecular and Cellular Biochemistry. 2026

items.title: Enhanced Electrochemiluminescence by Nanocatalyst-Supported Nanochannel–Surfactant Micelle Assembly for Ultrasensitive Detection of Rifampicin
items.summary: This paper developed a new electrochemiluminescence sensing platform aimed at ultrasensitive detection of the antibiotic rifampicin, addressing limitations in existing approaches related to poor enrichment of ECL components at electrode interfaces and insufficient catalytic enhancement of co-reactants. The platform combined a nitrogen-doped graphene quantum dot and molybdenum disulfide nanosheet composite deposited on an electrode to catalyze oxygen reduction, with a vertically ordered mesoporous silica film filled with surfactant micelles grown atop this layer to simultaneously enrich luminol, dissolved oxygen, and rifampicin through hydrophobic interactions. This layered architecture produced a strong luminol–dissolved oxygen ECL signal, while rifampicin selectively quenched the signal by consuming superoxide anion radicals, enabling quantitative detection. The mesoporous silica film also provided a molecular sieving effect that improved selectivity and stability against interfering species. The resulting sensor achieved very high sensitivity, a wide linear detection range spanning several orders of magnitude, and an exceptionally low detection limit, and was successfully applied to rifampicin determination in eye drops and seawater samples.
items.citation: Jiahui Lin, Zhongping Mao, Fei Yan. Enhanced Electrochemiluminescence by Nanocatalyst-Supported Nanochannel–Surfactant Micelle Assembly for Ultrasensitive Detection of Rifampicin. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: Flashing with colours: Photometric indicators of an early interaction in type II supernovae
items.summary: This paper examined early-time optical observations of type II supernovae to investigate whether photometric data alone can reveal evidence of interaction between the supernova ejecta and dense circumstellar material. The researchers compiled a large sample of supernovae using new high-cadence, high-precision multiband photometry from the POISE collaboration combined with previously published events, classifying each supernova based on whether early spectra showed transient narrow emission lines ("flash features") from highly ionised elements. They found that supernovae displaying these flash features tend to be more luminous at peak, show longer rise times in the blue band, and are systematically bluer than non-flash events, with these colour differences most apparent around three weeks after explosion. A key finding is that breaks in the colour-curve evolution within the first month after explosion, combined with the rate of colour change across the break and peak absolute magnitude, provide a strong diagnostic capable of distinguishing flash from non-flash supernovae. This suggests that photometric monitoring alone, without early spectroscopic follow-up, may be sufficient to identify supernovae undergoing circumstellar interaction.
items.citation: A. Mendez-Llorca, G. Folatelli, C. P. Gutierrez et al.. Flashing with colours: Photometric indicators of an early interaction in type II supernovae. arXiv. 2026

items.title: ModeCast: One-Shot Prediction of Linear MHD Eigenmodes and Growth Rates in Tokamaks
items.summary: ModeCast is a machine learning surrogate model designed to predict the linear magnetohydrodynamic stability of tokamak plasmas, a critical step in fusion reactor design that is computationally prohibitive with conventional solvers. The model was trained on a large dataset of simulations spanning thousands of plasma equilibria, covering multiple toroidal mode numbers, and was built to incorporate linear-phase physics directly into its architecture, objective function, and inputs. ModeCast performs inference many orders of magnitude faster than the reference solver on a single GPU while correctly identifying all unstable cases in held-out test data and accurately reproducing spatial field structures such as magnetic island topology and resistivity-dependent trends. The model also demonstrates promising generalization outside its training distribution, where lightweight retraining of a small subnetwork on a handful of simulations substantially reduces prediction error for growth rates. Because ModeCast is differentiable and outputs full spatial fields, the authors propose it could eventually assimilate experimental measurements to bridge the gap between simulation and real fusion devices.
items.citation: Alex Higginbottom, Zara Z. Ercan, Abetharan Antony et al.. ModeCast: One-Shot Prediction of Linear MHD Eigenmodes and Growth Rates in Tokamaks. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Large Language Model LLM Approach to COVID-19 Fake News Detection
items.summary: This study investigated the use of large language models and transformer-based transfer learning approaches for detecting fake news related to COVID-19 on social media. The researchers applied seven pretrained models, including BERT variants, GPT-2, XLNet, and T5, to a labeled dataset of tweets classified as real or fake, and additionally tested six late-fusion ensemble optimization techniques to improve classification performance. Models were evaluated using standard classification metrics alongside confusion matrix visualizations. Among individual models, GPT-2 achieved the highest performance across accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, while the Nelder-Mead fusion method yielded the best result among the ensemble approaches. The findings demonstrate the effectiveness of large language models for automated COVID-19 misinformation detection, with the authors identifying multiclass classification, multilingual data, and real-time detection as promising future directions.
items.citation: Muhammad Arif, Samah Fodeh-Jarad, Elyas Irankhah et al.. A Large Language Model LLM Approach to COVID-19 Fake News Detection. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Rapid mixing within a phase for Ising models
items.summary: This paper investigates how quickly Glauber dynamics mixes for Ising models restricted to configurations with a large majority of positive spins, a setting corresponding to sampling within a single thermodynamic phase. The authors derive functional inequalities—specifically Poincaré and modified logarithmic Sobolev inequalities—for these conditioned measures by combining a sparse spectral condition on the interaction matrix with magnetization drift and entropy-weighted drift conditions. These tools are then applied to several concrete models: they establish near-linear-time approximate posterior sampling for the Z₂ synchronization problem at sufficiently high signal-to-noise ratio starting from a spectral initialization, prove rapid phase ordering for ferromagnetic Ising models on random regular graphs at lower temperatures than previously known, and show near-linear mixing for the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model at any fixed inverse temperature when the external field is large enough. The work thus provides a unified framework for proving rapid mixing within a phase across a variety of disordered and structured spin systems by exploiting drift conditions that keep the dynamics confined to a magnetization-rich region.
items.citation: Vasyl Paliy, Youngtak Sohn. Rapid mixing within a phase for Ising models. arXiv. 2026

items.title: MTEdit: Packed Trajectories Beat Rollouts for Multi-Turn Image Editing
items.summary: This paper addresses the problem of multi-turn image editing, where an image is progressively modified according to a sequence of instructions to support human-AI collaborative creation. The key challenge tackled is that conventional approaches using sequential rollouts accumulate errors and cause visual-quality drift across editing turns during training data construction. To overcome this, the authors developed MTEdit, a large-scale dataset built using a packed trajectory canvas generation pipeline that jointly renders multiple editing states within a single visual context, reducing drift and covering both step-wise and context-aware editing scenarios. They also introduced MTEdit-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating instruction following, content consistency, resistance to visual-quality drift, and use of historical context across turns. Fine-tuning an existing model on MTEdit yielded the best performance among evaluated open-source models on MTEdit-Bench, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed data construction approach.
items.citation: Houyuan Chen, Fanzhou Wang, Xiangyu Fan et al.. MTEdit: Packed Trajectories Beat Rollouts for Multi-Turn Image Editing. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Neural Operators Reveal Scale-Dependent Limits on Recovering Greenland Ice Loss from Sea Level Fingerprints
items.summary: This paper investigates how well the spatial distribution of Greenland Ice Sheet mass loss can be recovered from sea level fingerprints—the characteristic patterns of sea surface height change caused by shifting ice mass. To tackle this ill-conditioned inverse problem, the authors developed a physics-informed neural operator constrained by a neural-operator emulator of the forward sea level equation, allowing systematic, scale-resolved analysis across ensembles of synthetic ice loss scenarios. They found that broad patterns of ice loss can be recovered, but distinct ice loss configurations can produce nearly indistinguishable fingerprints, meaning fine-scale structure is strongly dependent on prior assumptions about ice change geometry. Inversion accuracy varies with the spatial wavelength and amplitude of ice mass change, and the authors derived an empirical error law that defines a scale-dependent ceiling on recoverable information, with sea surface height observations near Greenland carrying the most diagnostic power. Applying their framework to observed sea surface height trends from recent decades recovers the large-scale Greenland fingerprint, while residuals correlate with basin-scale bathymetry, pointing to unresolved sterodynamic variability and highlighting where additional independent observations or ice sheet constraints would most improve ice loss inference.
items.citation: Xiyuan Bao, Sophie Coulson, Natasha Valencic et al.. Neural Operators Reveal Scale-Dependent Limits on Recovering Greenland Ice Loss from Sea Level Fingerprints. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Translational Barriers and AI-Driven Challenges of Microfluidics-Enabled Wearables and Implantable Systems in Personalized Medicine.
items.summary: This review paper examines the trajectory of wearable and implantable microfluidic systems from laboratory prototypes toward clinical deployment, focusing on their capacity for continuous, minimally invasive monitoring of biomarkers in biofluids such as sweat, saliva, tears, and interstitial fluid. Rather than addressing materials or fabrication in isolation, the authors construct a unified framework spanning foundational biomaterials, advanced fabrication techniques, and performance benchmarking of both diagnostic and closed-loop theranostic platforms. The review systematically evaluates how microfluidic transport, multiplexed molecular analytics, and autonomous therapeutic integration together enable a shift from passive health tracking to adaptive intervention. A central focus is the role of artificial intelligence in enabling sensor self-calibration, multiplexed molecular decoding, and on-device autonomous decision-making. The authors conclude that socio-technical barriers—particularly biofluid data heterogeneity and population baseline disparities that introduce algorithmic bias—must be addressed alongside robust hardware interfaces, standardized validation benchmarks, and alignment with regulatory frameworks to achieve equitable clinical translation.
items.citation: Huang K, Fong CY, Huang X et al.. Translational Barriers and AI-Driven Challenges of Microfluidics-Enabled Wearables and Implantable Systems in Personalized Medicine.. Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany). 2026

items.title: Molecular point-of-care: technological evolution, clinical applications, and future perspectives
items.citation: Zhang D, Cui X, Zhang R et al.. Molecular point-of-care: technological evolution, clinical applications, and future perspectives. Frontiers in bioengineering and biotechnology. 2026

items.title: Recent advances in microfluidic-based biosensors for nucleic acid detection: From amplification strategies to point-of-care diagnostic devices.
items.summary: This review examines recent advances in microfluidic-based biosensors designed for nucleic acid detection, with a focus on their application in point-of-care diagnostics for both infectious and non-infectious diseases. The authors critically assess how microfluidic integration addresses key limitations of conventional centralized molecular diagnostics, including high cost, long analysis times, and restricted accessibility in resource-limited settings. The review covers a range of nucleic acid amplification strategies, including thermocyclic approaches such as polymerase chain reaction and various isothermal amplification techniques, evaluating their compatibility with miniaturized microfluidic platforms. Emerging amplification and detection technologies, device integration strategies, and comparative analytical performance are also discussed. The authors highlight the remaining technological and practical challenges that must be overcome to successfully translate laboratory-based microfluidic nucleic acid detection systems into reliable, user-friendly point-of-care diagnostic devices.
items.citation: Kulkarni MB, Vineela, Mandal N et al.. Recent advances in microfluidic-based biosensors for nucleic acid detection: From amplification strategies to point-of-care diagnostic devices.. SLAS technology. 2026

items.title: Machine learning–empowered smartphone platforms for sustainable point-of-care bacterial detection
items.citation: Rzgar Sirwan Raza, Shilan Arif Fatah, Sameera Sh. Mohammed Ameen et al.. Machine learning–empowered smartphone platforms for sustainable point-of-care bacterial detection. Talanta. 2026

items.title: Soil microbes are the tiny bioengineers running Earth’s underground factory
items.summary: This paper synthesizes research on soil microbial communities with the goal of clarifying how microbial diversity translates into ecosystem-level functions. The authors developed a function-centred framework that identifies four conserved functional axes — secondary metabolism, nutrient cycling, community interactions, and stress tolerance — as the core processes governing soil ecosystem outcomes. Drawing on studies across ecological, agricultural, and environmental contexts, they find that these functional axes collectively influence plant productivity, climate regulation, and pollutant transformation, though their expression varies strongly with context. The authors propose that soil operates as a self-organizing system in which microbial interactions produce emergent ecosystem behaviour beyond what individual organisms accomplish. This framework is offered as a foundation for predictive, ecology-informed strategies to manage soils for sustainable agriculture, environmental remediation, and climate mitigation.
items.citation: Suzanne Hassan-Dalléac, Wafa Guiga, Antonia Suau. Soil microbes are the tiny bioengineers running Earth’s underground factory. Communications Earth & Environment. 2026

items.title: Interaction-aware dexterous robot for minimally invasive transcanal inner ear interventions
items.summary: This paper addressed the challenge of delivering therapeutic and diagnostic interventions to the inner ear, where anatomical constraints make access extremely difficult with existing tools. The researchers developed a miniaturized dual-segment continuum robot that combines catheter, endoscopic, and instrumental functions within a low-aspect-ratio design, driven by antagonistic cables and built around a transition-free backbone of saddle-shaped joints. The robot achieves tight bending radii and programmable configurations to navigate complex anatomy, while a centrally embedded microneedle serves as the end-effector with high positioning accuracy, and Fiber Bragg grating sensors on the needle enable real-time measurement of tool-tissue interaction forces. The system was validated in cadaver and live animal models, demonstrating atraumatic transcanal access to the round window membrane for targeted drug delivery and microsampling. The authors conclude that this robotic platform offers a practical approach to early diagnosis and precision treatment of inner ear diseases, with potential to extend care to underserved populations.
items.citation: Haiming Li, Peiyuan Gao, Haoyue Tan et al.. Interaction-aware dexterous robot for minimally invasive transcanal inner ear interventions. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: Machine Learning-Guided Synthetic Microbial Communities Enable Functional and Sustainable Degradation of Persistent Environmental Pollutants
items.summary: This paper developed a machine learning-guided framework called GENIA for the rational design of synthetic microbial communities capable of degrading multiple persistent environmental pollutants simultaneously. The researchers used a microfluidic high-throughput cultivation platform to isolate and screen thousands of bacterial strains from pollutant-enriched environments, then performed whole-genome sequencing on prioritized candidates to identify metabolic traits relevant to pollutant degradation. Genomic profiles were encoded into graph representations and processed through a pipeline combining graph neural networks, pathway complementarity modeling, and functional redundancy minimization to predict optimal community assemblies. The resulting nine-member synthetic community was tested against lignin, atrazine, and PFAS as proof-of-concept target pollutants, achieving high removal efficiencies for all three compounds under simulated environmental conditions, representing a substantial improvement over existing single-strain or naturally occurring consortium approaches. The authors conclude that GENIA provides a scalable and generalizable framework for engineering ecologically coherent microbial consortia for complex environmental bioremediation applications.
items.citation: Esaú De la Vega-Camarillo, Jorge Arreola‐Vargas, Sanjay Antony‐Babu et al.. Machine Learning-Guided Synthetic Microbial Communities Enable Functional and Sustainable Degradation of Persistent Environmental Pollutants. Environmental Science & Technology. 2026

items.title: Regulatory Challenges and Opportunities for Cell‐Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Pharmaceutical Development: A European and Global Perspective
items.summary: This paper examines the regulatory landscape governing cell-derived extracellular vesicles as emerging therapeutic and diagnostic agents, with a focus on inconsistencies between major jurisdictions. The authors analyze how existing medicinal product frameworks in the European Union, the United States, Japan, and other regions classify and oversee these products, noting that the acellular nature of extracellular vesicles does not map cleanly onto established regulatory categories such as advanced therapy medicinal products or biological products. A key finding is that this cross-regional heterogeneity creates practical challenges around product classification, quality attribute definition, potency assessment, and comparability during clinical development. The authors argue that extracellular vesicle products can and should be accommodated within existing medicinal product frameworks, provided that regulatory tools are applied consistently and ambiguous zones around classification criteria and critical quality attributes are resolved through ongoing dialogue. Rather than proposing new normative frameworks, the review synthesizes the current state of knowledge to support regulatory harmonization efforts among international agencies and scientific societies.
items.citation: Tania Limongi, Paola Milla, Barbara Stella et al.. Regulatory Challenges and Opportunities for Cell‐Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Pharmaceutical Development: A European and Global Perspective. Journal of Extracellular Vesicles. 2026

items.title: From selection to design: Reshaping aptamer discovery with artificial intelligence
items.summary: This review examines how artificial intelligence is transforming the discovery and design of nucleic acid aptamers, which are synthetic oligonucleotide ligands that function analogously to antibodies in molecular recognition. The authors argue that classical aptamer discovery methods such as SELEX are fundamentally limited by their stochastic, trial-and-error nature, making clinical translation slow and unreliable. The review categorizes emerging AI approaches into predictive frameworks that learn sequence-structure-function relationships from noisy experimental data and generative models—including variational autoencoders, diffusion models, and inverse folding approaches—that enable the rational design of aptamers targeting specific molecular geometries. High-throughput SELEX is reframed not merely as a selection tool but as a data-generation engine that feeds these computational frameworks, with translational applications highlighted in AI-designed biosensors and chemically optimized therapeutics. The authors also identify persistent challenges around data sparsity and model interpretability, and propose a roadmap toward closed-loop design-test-refine ecosystems that iteratively couple computational design with experimental validation.
items.citation: Xin Yang, Shijian Ding, Meishen Ren et al.. From selection to design: Reshaping aptamer discovery with artificial intelligence. Chemical Engineering Journal. 2026

items.title: Flashing with colours: Photometric indicators of an early interaction in type II supernovae
items.summary: This paper investigated whether photometric observations alone can identify Type II supernovae interacting with dense circumstellar material, a phenomenon typically diagnosed through early spectroscopic detection of narrow emission lines from highly ionised elements known as "flash features." The researchers combined new optical photometry and spectroscopy for a sample of previously unpublished Type II supernovae observed by the POISE collaboration with a literature sample, yielding a total dataset of dozens of events with high-cadence, high-precision multi-band light curves. By categorising supernovae based on the presence or absence of flash spectroscopic features, they compared key photometric properties including rise times, peak absolute magnitudes, and colour evolution between the two groups. They found that flash supernovae are on average more luminous at peak, tend to exhibit longer rise times in the blue band, and are generally bluer than non-flash events, with these colour differences likely reflecting intrinsic physical differences rather than dust extinction. Crucially, the study demonstrates that colour-curve breaks occurring within roughly a month of explosion, combined with peak absolute magnitude, provide a strong photometric diagnostic capable of identifying circumstellar material interaction even without early spectroscopic observations.
items.citation: A. Mendez-Llorca, G. Folatelli, C. P. Gutierrez et al.. Flashing with colours: Photometric indicators of an early interaction in type II supernovae. arXiv. 2026

items.title: ModeCast: One-Shot Prediction of Linear MHD Eigenmodes and Growth Rates in Tokamaks
items.summary: This paper introduces ModeCast, a machine learning surrogate model designed to predict linear magnetohydrodynamic instabilities in tokamak plasmas, which pose a major challenge for fusion reactor design because conventional simulation tools are computationally prohibitive at scale. The model was trained on a large dataset of JOREK simulations spanning thousands of plasma equilibria and multiple toroidal mode numbers, incorporating linear-phase physics directly into its architecture, training objective, and inputs to improve data efficiency. ModeCast returns complete spatial eigenmode structures and growth rates in a single forward pass, achieving inference speeds more than four orders of magnitude faster than the reference solver while correctly identifying all unstable cases in held-out test data. The predicted fields faithfully reproduce physically meaningful features such as magnetic island topology and resistivity-dependent trends, and the model generalizes to out-of-distribution conditions through lightweight fine-tuning on just a handful of simulations. Because ModeCast is differentiable and outputs full spatial fields, the authors suggest it could eventually assimilate experimental measurements and serve as a bridge between simulations and real fusion devices.
items.citation: Alex Higginbottom, Zara Z. Ercan, Abetharan Antony et al.. ModeCast: One-Shot Prediction of Linear MHD Eigenmodes and Growth Rates in Tokamaks. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Demonstration of Logical Error Suppression in a Surface Code Memory on a Cloud-Accessible IBM Superconducting Processor
items.summary: This paper investigates whether logical error suppression consistent with quantum error correction theory can be demonstrated on a commercially accessible superconducting quantum processor. The researchers implemented rotated surface-code memory experiments on an IBM Nighthawk processor accessed via cloud, exploring how circuit-level optimizations affect logical error rates. Their key optimizations included combining short readout, fused measurement and reset, and an echo pulse on data qubits during ancilla readout, which together substantially reduced per-round logical error rates compared to a standard unoptimized baseline. Scaling the code distance in one basis while holding the other fixed produced clear logical error suppression, with error-suppression factors above unity under maximum-likelihood decoding, demonstrating that the physical noise is below threshold. However, the team also identified limitations including performance variation across processor placements, weakening of the distance advantage at longer circuit depths, and long-lived temporal correlations suggestive of a persistent error component, motivating closer codesign between hardware and error-correction circuits.
items.citation: Shuwen Kan, Aaron Hoyt, Sean Garner et al.. Demonstration of Logical Error Suppression in a Surface Code Memory on a Cloud-Accessible IBM Superconducting Processor. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Self-Building Labs
items.summary: This paper introduces the self-building laboratory, a system designed to address the flexibility bottleneck in automated scientific research. Unlike existing self-driving laboratories that can only execute the specific experimental procedures they were engineered for, the self-building laboratory autonomously designs, configures, and operates its own experimental setup starting from a high-level scientific goal and whatever physical resources are already available. The system constructs the necessary components end-to-end, including lab layout, digital twin models, robot skills, and experimental workflows, and can scale from a single workstation to multi-robot configurations. The approach was validated through a real-world quantum-dot synthesis experiment, demonstrating its capacity to handle genuine scientific tasks. By shifting human researchers from manual programming and device configuration to simply specifying scientific objectives, the system aims to make laboratory automation substantially more accessible and scalable.
items.citation: Jiaru Bai, Yuchi Zhao, Han Hao et al.. Self-Building Labs. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Engineering nonrelativistic spin splitting in semiconductors by altermagnetic proximity
items.summary: This paper investigates how altermagnetic properties can be transferred to conventional semiconductors through proximity effects, circumventing the challenge of finding single materials that simultaneously exhibit altermagnetic symmetry, semiconducting character, and weak spin-orbit coupling. The authors developed an analytical theory describing a semiconductor coupled to a gapped altermagnet, showing that virtual tunneling processes transfer momentum-dependent, nonrelativistic spin splitting from the altermagnet into the semiconductor. A key finding is that the induced nonrelativistic altermagnetic splitting and the relativistic Rashba splitting depend differently on band alignment, because virtual processes involving the altermagnet's valence and conduction bands reinforce the altermagnetic contribution while contributing with opposite signs to the Rashba coupling. This distinction enables electrostatic tuning to a regime where the Rashba splitting vanishes while a substantial altermagnetic spin splitting remains, effectively decoupling the two types of spin interactions. Exact diagonalization of the full heterostructure model confirms the analytical results and establishes that this mechanism is robust beyond the perturbative limit, suggesting altermagnetic proximity as a general strategy for engineering nonrelativistic spin-split states in established semiconductor platforms.
items.citation: Sing Lam Wong, Marcel Franz. Engineering nonrelativistic spin splitting in semiconductors by altermagnetic proximity. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Limits from nonlinear loss of spin-orbit-torque control of magnon transport
items.summary: This paper investigated how spin-orbit torque can be used to control magnon transport in magnetic insulator devices, and what ultimately limits this control. Using three-terminal devices made from low-damping lithium aluminum ferrite thin films with a platinum gate electrode, the researchers measured the nonlocal magnon signal as a function of applied gate current. They found that the magnon signal initially increases as the gate current compensates magnon damping, but then saturates and decreases beyond a critical current density. Brillouin light scattering microscopy revealed that this turnover corresponds to the onset of a spatially localized auto-oscillation mode beneath the gate, which exhibits a continuous frequency redshift indicative of large-amplitude nonlinear dynamics and suppresses the propagating magnon population. Micromagnetic simulations confirmed that this nonmonotonic behavior arises from amplitude-dependent nonlinear damping associated with these auto-oscillations, rather than from saturation of spin injection, establishing nonlinear damping as the fundamental limit to magnon current modulation in magnetic insulators.
items.citation: Lerato Takana, Katya Mikhailova, Charles Zheng et al.. Limits from nonlinear loss of spin-orbit-torque control of magnon transport. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Nanozyme-based biosensors for pathogenic microorganism detection: a mini-review
items.citation: Yang T, Ling Y, Zhang E et al.. Nanozyme-based biosensors for pathogenic microorganism detection: a mini-review. Frontiers in microbiology. 2026

items.title: Advancements in biosensor Technologies for Pathogen Detection: Innovations and comparison with conventional diagnostic approaches.
items.summary: This review paper examines the state of biosensor technologies for detecting pathogens across clinical, food safety, and environmental monitoring contexts, comparing them against established conventional diagnostic methods. The authors surveyed electrochemical, optical, nanoparticle, microfluidic, and paper-based biosensor platforms, analyzing their underlying sensing principles, design strategies, applications, and respective strengths and limitations. Conventional approaches such as culture-based methods, ELISA, and PCR, while analytically proven, are noted to be constrained by lengthy processing times, complex instrumentation, and the requirement for trained personnel. Biosensors are presented as advantageous alternatives owing to their portability, sensitivity, capacity for multiplexing, and suitability for point-of-care use, with advances in nanomaterials, biorecognition strategies, and signal-transduction mechanisms further expanding their detection capabilities. Nevertheless, the review identifies persistent practical challenges including sensor stability, reproducibility, fabrication complexity, scalability, and the need for rigorous validation as barriers to widespread real-world implementation.
items.citation: Singhal P, Misra S, Prakash A et al.. Advancements in biosensor Technologies for Pathogen Detection: Innovations and comparison with conventional diagnostic approaches.. Journal of microbiological methods. 2026

items.title: Development of a NiCoFe-LDH/Ketjenblack-enhanced electrochemical antibacterial peptide biosensor for Aeromonas hydrophila detection in seawater samples.
items.summary: This paper developed an electrochemical biosensor for detecting the fish pathogen Aeromonas hydrophila in aquaculture settings, addressing the need for rapid and sensitive diagnostic tools to protect animal health and reduce economic losses. The biosensor was constructed by modifying a screen-printed carbon electrode with a nanocomposite of ternary NiCoFe layered double hydroxide combined with Ketjenblack carbon, synthesized via one-pot precipitation, and functionalized with an antibacterial peptide as the biorecognition element. The nanocomposite was characterized as exhibiting a high-activity nanosheet structure with efficient electron transfer properties, and the peptide layer was validated through electrochemical characterization and affinity studies. Under optimized room-temperature conditions, the sensor achieved detection across a broad bacterial concentration range, an exceptionally low limit of detection, high reproducibility with minimal cross-reactivity toward other bacteria, and near-complete recovery when tested in spiked seawater samples. The authors report this as the first electrochemical antibacterial peptide-based biosensor for A. hydrophila to be evaluated in seawater, suggesting its potential utility for real aquaculture monitoring.
items.citation: Kızılkurtlu AA, Arancı K, Gülyüz S et al.. Development of a NiCoFe-LDH/Ketjenblack-enhanced electrochemical antibacterial peptide biosensor for Aeromonas hydrophila detection in seawater samples.. Mikrochimica acta. 2026

items.title: Automated machine learning framework for interpreting paper-based biosensing of pathogens.
items.summary: This paper investigated how machine learning could be used to automatically interpret images from paper-based colorimetric biosensors designed to detect microbial pathogens, addressing the limitation that current interpretation relies on manual analysis and study-specific decision thresholds. The researchers developed and compared several machine learning approaches, including conventional normalized intensity extraction, region-of-interest descriptors, and convolutional neural networks, evaluating their performance both within individual studies and across different biosensor studies targeting distinct pathogens. While all approaches performed well within a single study, classification performance degraded when decision thresholds were applied across studies due to systematic shifts between experimental contexts. To overcome this, the authors introduced a color-space normalization method that characterizes each biosensor signal relative to paired positive and negative controls rather than relying on single-channel intensity alone, which stabilized decision boundaries across studies. This cross-study normalization approach outperformed the other methods in cross-study validation and was demonstrated on an independent dataset, supporting its potential to enable more consistent, automated interpretation of paper-based biosensor results.
items.citation: Park S, Yang Z, He Z. Automated machine learning framework for interpreting paper-based biosensing of pathogens.. Environmental research. 2026

items.title: Self-Cleaning Electrochemical Biosensor Based on MCOF@Ag for Simultaneous Pathogen Detection and Photocatalytic Inactivation.
items.summary: This paper developed a dual-function electrochemical biosensor capable of both detecting and inactivating bacterial pathogens using a single electrode material. The researchers synthesized silver nanoparticle-decorated metal-covalent organic framework composites with a nanoflower-like structure, which enhanced electron transfer and both electrochemical and photocatalytic performance. By functionalizing the electrode with aptamers specific to Staphylococcus aureus, the biosensor achieved highly sensitive quantification of the bacterium across a broad concentration range with a detection limit of one colony-forming unit per milliliter. Beyond detection, the electrode leveraged its photocatalytic activity under visible light to generate reactive oxygen species, achieving near-complete inactivation of captured bacteria within minutes, after which the electrode could be regenerated and reused. The study demonstrates that a single metal-covalent organic framework-based platform can integrate ultrasensitive electrochemical biosensing with photocatalytic antibacterial functionality, offering a promising strategy for infectious disease prevention and control.
items.citation: Bai Y, Xiao L, Cai L et al.. Self-Cleaning Electrochemical Biosensor Based on MCOF@Ag for Simultaneous Pathogen Detection and Photocatalytic Inactivation.. Analytical chemistry. 2026

items.title: One-step MCDA-CRISPR/Cas12b platform for point-of-care testing of Shewanella algae.
items.summary: The paper investigated the detection of *Shewanella algae*, an emerging marine zoonotic pathogen associated with high mortality, for which existing diagnostic methods are inadequate in terms of specificity, speed, and simplicity. The researchers developed a one-pot, isothermal detection platform called MCTOS, which combines Multiple Cross Displacement Amplification with CRISPR/Cas12b-based signal readout, targeting a *S. algae*-specific gene identified through pan-genome analysis of hundreds of *Shewanella* genomes. The assay operates at a constant temperature and completes within one hour, with results readable by either real-time fluorescence or a lateral flow biosensor. MCTOS achieved a low limit of detection, showed no cross-reactivity against non-target templates, and demonstrated near-perfect specificity and high sensitivity when evaluated against clinical isolates and field samples. The authors conclude that MCTOS offers a simpler, more sensitive alternative to existing one-pot CRISPR and loop-mediated isothermal amplification methods, making it suitable for point-of-care diagnostics and epidemiological surveillance across a range of laboratory settings.
items.citation: Wang X, Dong L, Zhang S et al.. One-step MCDA-CRISPR/Cas12b platform for point-of-care testing of Shewanella algae.. Talanta. 2026

items.title: Synergistic Multicomponent Nucleopeptide-Based Hydrogels: Harnessing DNA-Base Pairing and Electrostatic Complementarities
items.summary: This study investigated how combining peptides functionalized with DNA nucleobases (nucleopeptides) into multicomponent systems affects the properties of low-molecular-weight hydrogels. The researchers synthesized a series of nucleopeptides derived from two complementary tetrapeptide sequences — one negatively charged and one positively charged at physiological pH — each functionalized with one of the four DNA nucleobases introduced via a peptide nucleic acid moiety. By systematically mixing these components and exploiting both electrostatic complementarity and nucleobase-pairing interactions, they examined how these forces collectively influence gelation time, sol-gel transition temperature, stiffness, stress resistance, and fibrillar network morphology. The results demonstrated that careful selection of complementary components allows fine-tuning of hydrogel mechanical and physicochemical properties, though unexpected behaviors also emerged, highlighting the complexity of these bioinspired multicomponent systems. Overall, the findings underscore the potential of nucleopeptide-based multicomponent hydrogels as a versatile platform for developing high-performance supramolecular materials with biomedical and biotechnological applications.
items.citation: Tristan Giraud, Marine Koch, Paul Hoschtettler et al.. Synergistic Multicomponent Nucleopeptide-Based Hydrogels: Harnessing DNA-Base Pairing and Electrostatic Complementarities. ACS Materials Au. 2026

items.title: Self-amplifying RNA (saRNA) and circular RNA (circRNA) vaccines: Progress, evidence gaps, and translational pathways for durable and scalable immunization
items.summary: This review examines two emerging RNA vaccine platforms — self-amplifying RNA and circular RNA — as alternatives to conventional non-replicating mRNA vaccines. Self-amplifying RNA uses an encoded replicase to amplify intracellular RNA templates, achieving high antigen expression at lower doses, while circular RNA relies on a covalently closed structure that resists enzymatic degradation and enables sustained, cap-independent translation. The authors synthesize clinical, animal, and mechanistic evidence across both platforms, noting a pronounced asymmetry in maturity, as self-amplifying RNA has advanced through human trials including late-phase COVID-19 vaccine evaluations and regulatory authorization, whereas circular RNA remains predominantly preclinical. To structure cross-platform comparison, the review proposes a framework organized around durability, dose-sparing, and deployability, while identifying major barriers including delivery system design, innate immune sensing, and manufacturing standardization. The authors conclude by mapping translational pathways needed to move both modalities toward scalable and durable immunization strategies.
items.citation: Ugwu Okechukwu Paul-Chima, Michael Ben Okon, Ogenyi Fabian C. et al.. Self-amplifying RNA (saRNA) and circular RNA (circRNA) vaccines: Progress, evidence gaps, and translational pathways for durable and scalable immunization. Human Vaccines & Immunotherapeutics. 2026

items.title: Federated Learning in Multimodal Healthcare Diagnostics: Privacy-Preserving AI for Biomedical Imaging, Electronic Health Records, Wearables, and Clinical Decision Support
items.summary: This review paper examines the application of federated learning to multimodal healthcare diagnostics, addressing the fundamental tension between leveraging diverse clinical data and protecting patient privacy. The authors surveyed the literature across multiple healthcare domains, including biomedical imaging modalities such as MRI, CT, ultrasound, and histopathology, as well as electronic health records, wearable physiological signals, chronic disease management, elder care, and clinical decision support systems. Federated learning is presented as a promising solution because it enables collaborative AI model training across institutions by sharing only model updates rather than raw patient data, thereby reducing direct data exposure and improving alignment with privacy regulations. However, the review emphasizes that privacy is not inherently guaranteed by this approach, as vulnerabilities such as gradient leakage, model inversion, and membership inference attacks still pose significant risks requiring additional safeguards. The authors also identify persistent implementation challenges including system heterogeneity, data imbalance, communication bottlenecks, and fairness concerns, and conclude with actionable guidance for regulators, developers, and healthcare systems seeking to advance safe and equitable federated learning deployment in medicine.
items.venue: Archives of Computational Methods in Engineering
items.citation: Shon G. Nemane, Vaishnavi M. Sarad, Dhiraj P. Tulaskar et al.. Federated Learning in Multimodal Healthcare Diagnostics: Privacy-Preserving AI for Biomedical Imaging, Electronic Health Records, Wearables, and Clinical Decision Support. Archives of Computational Methods in Engineering. 2026

items.title: CRISPR-Cas systems as next-generation antimicrobials: a systemic review of mechanisms, delivery strategies, and translational challenges
items.summary: This systematic review examined the use of CRISPR-Cas systems as alternative antimicrobial strategies against multidrug-resistant bacteria, which pose a growing global threat as conventional antibiotics lose effectiveness. The authors synthesized preclinical and experimental evidence on different CRISPR effector types, their antibacterial mechanisms, delivery platforms, and therapeutic outcomes across studies targeting resistant bacterial infections. The review found that CRISPR-Cas systems can effectively kill or resensitize resistant bacteria through mechanisms such as chromosomal double-strand break induction, resistance plasmid elimination, and RNA-targeted cleavage, with Cas9 being the most commonly used effector. Among delivery strategies evaluated, phage-mediated delivery showed the most consistent efficacy, and one CRISPR-enhanced engineered bacteriophage cocktail has progressed to clinical evaluation. Despite promising results, the authors conclude that significant barriers—including limited bacterial host range, physiological instability, escape mutations, and insufficient long-term safety data—must be overcome through optimized delivery systems, multiplex targeting, and clearer regulatory frameworks before clinical translation can be achieved.
items.citation: Maha S.I. Wizrah. CRISPR-Cas systems as next-generation antimicrobials: a systemic review of mechanisms, delivery strategies, and translational challenges. Frontiers in Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Targeting biofilm-driven antibiotic resistance: emerging mechanisms and next-generation therapeutic interventions
items.summary: This review examines how microbial biofilms contribute to antimicrobial resistance and the emerging therapeutic strategies designed to overcome this challenge. Biofilms enhance antibiotic tolerance through multiple mechanisms, including restricted drug penetration, antibiotic degradation, and facilitation of horizontal gene transfer, making infections in both community and healthcare settings extremely difficult to treat. The authors synthesize current understanding of these resistance mechanisms, emphasizing that the absence of approved anti-biofilm therapeutics represents a critical gap in the clinical arsenal. The review highlights a range of next-generation interventions under investigation, including nanotechnology, antimicrobial peptides, bacteriophage-derived enzymes, quorum-sensing inhibitors, CRISPR-based tools, microbiome engineering, and artificial intelligence-driven drug discovery. The authors argue that a multi-platform therapeutic approach combining these strategies offers the most promising path toward improving outcomes in biofilm-associated, treatment-resistant infections.
items.citation: Abdulkarim Mbaraka, Ritu Raj Meena, Ekta Menghani et al.. Targeting biofilm-driven antibiotic resistance: emerging mechanisms and next-generation therapeutic interventions. Frontiers in Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Traditional fermented food microbial ecosystems oriented towards industrial standards: multi-dimensional characterization and artificial regulation
items.summary: This review examined the microbial ecosystems underlying traditional fermented foods, which are shaped by complex interactions among microorganisms, substrates, and environmental conditions, but are prone to inconsistency that hinders industrial standardization. The authors surveyed how multi-omics approaches can comprehensively characterize microbial composition, community dynamics, metabolite profiles, and phage activity within these systems. They also summarized intervention strategies—including the use of functional starter strains, synthetic microbial communities, bacteriophage manipulation, and physicochemical modulation—aimed at bringing greater control to spontaneous fermentation processes. The review concludes by outlining future directions and challenges involved in transitioning traditional fermentation from empirical, artisanal practice to predictable and scalable industrial production.
items.citation: M T Wu, Jiayao Wang, Yu Wang et al.. Traditional fermented food microbial ecosystems oriented towards industrial standards: multi-dimensional characterization and artificial regulation. npj Science of Food. 2026

items.title: Bad Diagnosis: Analyzing Consent and Data Collection Practices of Mobile Medical Apps
items.summary: This paper investigated the consent practices and data collection behaviors of over ten thousand mobile health applications available on the Google Play Store, a domain that handles highly sensitive personal and medical information. The researchers developed a principled framework to distinguish genuine health apps from general wellness tools, then applied static code analysis alongside automated privacy policy examination to detect permission misuse and consent violations at scale. Their findings reveal pervasive problems throughout the mHealth ecosystem, including the majority of apps requesting permissions—such as location, camera, and microphone access—with no functional justification based on their stated purposes. Most critically, nearly all apps failed to present users with any consent form, directly contravening regulations like the GDPR, and even those apps that did provide consent mechanisms frequently exhibited gaps between the consent obtained and the personal data actually collected. The authors conclude that these results demonstrate an urgent need for stronger regulatory enforcement and planned to release their dataset and tools to support ongoing monitoring of the space.
items.citation: Ethan Myers, Lorenzo De Carli, Shantanu Sharma et al.. Bad Diagnosis: Analyzing Consent and Data Collection Practices of Mobile Medical Apps. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Entering the Era of Circumplanetary Ring Detection with Direct Imaging
items.summary: This paper investigated how circumplanetary rings around exoplanets would affect reflected light observations from upcoming direct imaging missions, particularly the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. The researchers developed a hybrid forward model combining ray casting to simulate planet-ring mutual shadowing with empirical reflectance data from Cassini observations of Saturn's rings, applied to Jupiter-like planets with rings of varying size, inclination, and obliquity. They found that rings can substantially enhance planetary flux ratios at favorable geometries, with Saturn-equivalent rings boosting peak flux significantly and more extended rings producing even larger contrast enhancements, though certain geometries can instead suppress total system brightness below that of a ringless planet. The study also identified multi-band photometry as a useful diagnostic for detecting exorings, and applied the model to a known directly imaged planet candidate as an observational test case. The authors conclude that unaccounted-for rings could bias inferences about planetary properties from direct imaging data, making proper treatment of exorings essential for observation planning and interpretation.
items.citation: Samantha N. Hasler, Alexandra Z. Greenbaum, Geoffrey Bryden et al.. Entering the Era of Circumplanetary Ring Detection with Direct Imaging. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Detecting Exoplanetary Rings with Roman CGI Reflected Light Phase Curve Observations
items.summary: This paper investigates whether Saturn-like ring systems around giant exoplanets could be detected using the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope's Coronagraph Instrument through reflected light observations. The authors developed an analytical framework for modeling reflected-light phase curves of both ringed and ringless planets, finding that rings can outshine their host planets by one to two orders of magnitude or more, making them potentially far easier to detect than the planets themselves. A key diagnostic is that ring systems produce a distinctive phase-curve morphology with four extrema rather than the two expected for ringless planets, allowing rings to be distinguished from the planet's intrinsic signal across multiple observing epochs. Simulations of a specific candidate target with a Saturn-like ring configuration demonstrate that such systems would be detectable and could expand the number of viable targets beyond those previously considered too faint. The authors conclude that this instrument may provide the first observational constraints on the prevalence of rings around mature giant exoplanets, while also cautioning that unrecognized rings could lead to misinterpretation of planetary properties if not properly accounted for.
items.citation: Elizabeth Lane, Mary Anne Limbach, Logan Pearce et al.. Detecting Exoplanetary Rings with Roman CGI Reflected Light Phase Curve Observations. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Lyapunov Exponents in Power Systems: A Survey of Theory and Applications in Stability, Control, Forecasting, and Protection
items.summary: This survey examines how Lyapunov exponents, which measure the average exponential rate at which nearby trajectories in phase space converge or diverge, have been applied to power system problems over roughly three decades. The paper reviews a large body of literature spanning early demonstrations of chaos in simplified machine models through to recent machine-learning-augmented approaches used in grids dominated by inverter-based resources. The review is organized around four principal domains: stability analysis and real-time monitoring, chaos characterization and control, forecasting and predictability analysis, and protection together with fault diagnosis and condition monitoring. For each domain, the authors trace methodological evolution, compare model-based and data-driven estimation strategies, and assess validation gaps and benchmark practices. The paper concludes by identifying open research problems in each area, positioning Lyapunov exponents as a unifying diagnostic and predictive tool across diverse power system challenges.
items.citation: Mohammad Almomani, Venkataramana Ajjarapu. Lyapunov Exponents in Power Systems: A Survey of Theory and Applications in Stability, Control, Forecasting, and Protection. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Large Language Model LLM Approach to COVID-19 Fake News Detection
items.summary: This study investigated the use of transformer-based large language models for automatically detecting COVID-19-related fake news on social media. The researchers applied seven pretrained models, including BERT, GPT-2, and T5 variants, to a labeled dataset of tweets classified as real or fake, then evaluated six late-fusion ensemble optimization strategies to further boost classification performance. Models were assessed using standard classification metrics and confusion matrix visualizations. GPT-2 achieved the strongest individual performance, while among ensemble approaches the Nelder-Mead fusion method yielded the highest accuracy. The authors conclude that large language models offer substantial promise for pandemic misinformation detection and identify multilingual, multiclass, and real-time extensions as priorities for future work.
items.citation: Muhammad Arif, Samah Fodeh-Jarad, Elyas Irankhah et al.. A Large Language Model LLM Approach to COVID-19 Fake News Detection. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Enforcing Code Reasoning in Agentic Scaffold for More Effective Issue Resolution
items.summary: This paper investigates how reasoning about code occurs within ReAct-based programming agents and whether it contributes to successful software issue resolution. The researchers analyzed thousands of issue-resolution trajectories across multiple agent scaffolds, programming languages, and benchmarks, identifying distinct forms of code reasoning and finding that its presence correlates with higher resolution rates and increases with task complexity. However, they found that code reasoning in existing agents is largely unguided, leading to problems such as superficial fault localization, failure to refine nearly correct patches, and inadequate test generation. To address these gaps, the authors developed DeskCheck, a scaffold that systematically enforces code reasoning by simulating execution paths for root-cause localization, evaluating candidate patches, auditing solutions against requirements, and reasoning about corner cases before generating tests. DeskCheck demonstrated statistically significant improvements in resolution rates over baseline agents across benchmark instances, with only modest additional per-instance cost, supporting the conclusion that systematic code reasoning is an effective strategy for improving programming agents.
items.citation: Changshu Liu, Ji young Kim, Alireza Ghazanfari et al.. Enforcing Code Reasoning in Agentic Scaffold for More Effective Issue Resolution. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Trends of nucleic acid – based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases
items.summary: This review paper examines the landscape of nucleic acid-based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases, motivated by the global need for decentralized, rapid, and accessible testing. The authors systematically organized their analysis around three core operational steps: nucleic acid extraction, amplification, and detection. For extraction, they evaluated approaches including magnetic bead-based, paper-based, and integrated microfluidic methods, emphasizing designs that are simplified, rugged, and equipment-free. For amplification, they surveyed established and modified techniques such as PCR, NASBA, RPA, and LAMP, highlighting adaptations that enable rapid, low-power, and portable operation. On the detection side, the review covers a spectrum from colorimetric and fluorescent lateral flow assays to advanced biosensor platforms exploiting CRISPR/Cas systems and toehold switch principles, concluding that these newer approaches offer highly sensitive and programmable nucleic acid recognition suited to point-of-care settings.
items.citation: Hossam Hatem, Mohamed Mysara, Raghda Ramadan. Trends of nucleic acid – based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases. Journal of Biological Engineering. 2026

items.title: Development and validation of a multiplex TaqMan real-time quantitative PCR assay for the simultaneous detection of six major bacterial respiratory pathogens in goats.
items.summary: This study developed and validated a multiplex real-time quantitative PCR system for the simultaneous detection of six major bacterial and mycoplasmal pathogens responsible for respiratory disease in goats. Two triplex TaqMan panels were designed, one targeting three Mycoplasma species and one targeting two bacterial species and a Streptococcus subspecies, with performance evaluated for specificity, sensitivity, and reproducibility using plasmid standards and non-target organisms. Both panels demonstrated high analytical specificity with no cross-reactivity against non-target pathogens, low detection limits, and excellent reproducibility as reflected by low coefficients of variation within and between assays. When applied to field-collected goat nasal swab samples, the assay detected at least one target pathogen in more than half of samples, and nearly a quarter of samples harbored co-infections with two or more pathogens, highlighting the prevalence of mixed infections. The authors conclude that this multiplex approach offers a rapid and reliable diagnostic tool suited for both clinical investigation and epidemiological surveillance of caprine respiratory disease.
items.citation: Fu M, Liu Y, Zhang Z et al.. Development and validation of a multiplex TaqMan real-time quantitative PCR assay for the simultaneous detection of six major bacterial respiratory pathogens in goats.. Frontiers in veterinary science. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic accuracy of rapid integrated molecular testing for major respiratory viral infections: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.citation: Liu C, Yu D. Diagnostic accuracy of rapid integrated molecular testing for major respiratory viral infections: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Frontiers in medicine. 2026

items.title: Development and Initial Analytical Evaluation of a Multiplex PCR-Based Targeted NGS Assay for Expanded Viral Detection in Clinical Respiratory Specimens.
items.summary: This study developed an in-house multiplex PCR-based targeted next-generation sequencing method designed to detect a broad panel of viruses simultaneously in clinical respiratory specimens, addressing the limitation of conventional PCR assays that require prior etiological hypotheses and can only test for a restricted number of pathogens at once. The researchers constructed a panel targeting a large set of viruses, established bioinformatics pipelines for data processing, and evaluated the method's analytical sensitivity using positive control samples as well as its performance across a large collection of nasopharyngeal and oropharyngeal swabs previously characterized by standard PCR. The method achieved acceptable limits of detection for the majority of experimentally evaluated viral targets, and when applied to clinical specimens it showed strong concordance with existing PCR results while additionally identifying other viruses in a notable subset of PCR-positive cases and detecting viruses in many specimens that were PCR-negative. The approach also uncovered coinfections and provided viral typing information not available from standard testing, though a substantial proportion of additional detections involved viruses such as Epstein-Barr virus and cytomegalovirus, which require careful clinical interpretation in the respiratory context. The authors conclude that while the method shows promise as a complementary diagnostic tool for respiratory infections, further optimization, validation, and standardization of interpretive criteria are needed before broader clinical implementation.
items.citation: Nadtoka MI, Bukharina AY, Roev GV et al.. Development and Initial Analytical Evaluation of a Multiplex PCR-Based Targeted NGS Assay for Expanded Viral Detection in Clinical Respiratory Specimens.. Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland). 2026
