items.title: Molecular Etiology and Mortality Risk Stratification of Non-SARS-CoV-2 Severe Acute Respiratory Infection in a Predominantly Pediatric Cohort: A Retrospective Study From a Tertiary Care Hospital in North India
items.citation: Garg P, Dutta V, Bhatia M et al.. Molecular Etiology and Mortality Risk Stratification of Non-SARS-CoV-2 Severe Acute Respiratory Infection in a Predominantly Pediatric Cohort: A Retrospective Study From a Tertiary Care Hospital in North India. Cureus. 2026

items.title: Small extracellular vesicle signaling and mitochondrial transfer reprogram T helper cell function in human asthma
items.summary: This paper investigated how small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) derived from airway myeloid-derived regulatory cells contribute to the chronic airway inflammation characteristic of asthma. The researchers examined whether these sEVs carry mitochondria that influence CD4+ T helper cell behavior, finding that sEVs from asthmatic patients engage T cell receptors and transfer mitochondria to T cells primarily through membrane fusion, driving antigen-specific activation and polarization toward pro-inflammatory Th17 and Th2 phenotypes. Reactive oxygen species signaling within the transferred mitochondria was shown to be essential for T cell activation, and blocking this oxidant signaling reduced the inflammatory response. A Drp1-dependent mitochondrial fission mechanism was identified as responsible for packaging mitochondria into sEVs in pro-inflammatory myeloid cells, and intranasal delivery of mitochondria-containing sEVs exacerbated airway inflammation and Th cell polarization in a mouse model of asthma. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized pathway involving mitochondrial fission and intercellular mitochondrial transfer via sEVs as a driver of dysregulated T cell activation in asthma, suggesting this axis as a potential therapeutic target.
items.citation: Kenneth P. Hough, Jennifer L. Trevor, Shaheer Ahmad et al.. Small extracellular vesicle signaling and mitochondrial transfer reprogram T helper cell function in human asthma. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: Serologic Evidence of Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza A(H5N1) Virus Infection in a Veterinary Professional Exposed to an Infected Domestic Cat — Los Angeles County, California, December 2024–January 2025
items.summary: This report investigated potential transmission of highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) virus from infected domestic cats to humans in Los Angeles County. An outbreak among domestic cats was traced to consumption of raw commercial pet food products, and public health authorities subsequently conducted a serological survey among people who had been exposed to these animals. Although none of the exposed individuals tested positive by PCR during active monitoring, antibody testing later revealed that one asymptomatic veterinary professional, who had not used respiratory or eye protection during animal handling, showed serological evidence of H5N1 infection with no other identifiable risk factors. These findings suggest that cat-to-human transmission of H5N1 may have occurred, representing a notable spillover event in a domestic setting. The authors emphasize the need for robust infection control practices in veterinary environments and highlight the public health implications of H5N1 spread through raw pet food products to companion animals living in close contact with humans.
items.venue: MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
items.citation: Aisling Vaughan, Allison Joyce, Elizabeth Traub et al.. Serologic Evidence of Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza A(H5N1) Virus Infection in a Veterinary Professional Exposed to an Infected Domestic Cat — Los Angeles County, California, December 2024–January 2025. MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report. 2026

items.title: ECCO Guidelines on the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Management of Infections in Inflammatory Bowel Disease
items.summary: This paper presents updated clinical guidelines from the European Crohn's and Colitis Organisation on preventing, diagnosing, and managing infections in patients with inflammatory bowel disease. The work was motivated by the rapid expansion of immunosuppressive and biologic therapies used to treat Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, including newer small molecules and advanced biologics, each carrying distinct infection risk profiles not fully addressed by prior guidance. The authors synthesized current evidence on risk stratification and on viral, bacterial, mycobacterial, and vaccine-preventable infections to produce structured, evidence-based recommendations tailored to the contemporary treatment landscape. The guidelines emphasize a preventative strategy, recognizing that potent immune modulation increasingly places patients at meaningful risk for opportunistic infections that can cause serious morbidity or mortality. This update supersedes earlier consensus statements and guidelines, reflecting the clinical imperative to keep infection management recommendations aligned with evolving therapeutic practices in inflammatory bowel disease.
items.venue: Journal of Crohn s and Colitis
items.citation: Henit A. Yanai, Pierre Ellul, Bram Verstockt et al.. ECCO Guidelines on the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Management of Infections in Inflammatory Bowel Disease. Journal of Crohn s and Colitis. 2026

items.title: Effects of a clinical metagenomics intervention on clinical outcomes, healthcare costs, and health-related quality of life in patients with sepsis or septic shock: results of the randomized-controlled DigiSep trial
items.summary: This randomized controlled trial investigated whether adding metagenomic next-generation sequencing of microbial circulating cell-free DNA to standard microbiological diagnostics could improve outcomes for patients with sepsis or septic shock in intensive care units. Conducted across numerous German intensive care units, the study compared patients receiving this sequencing-based pathogen detection alongside standard care against those receiving standard care alone, with the primary endpoint being a composite antibiotic-risk-adjusted outcome ranking score at 28 days. The primary endpoint showed no statistically significant improvement with the metagenomic intervention. However, exploratory secondary analyses suggested clinical benefits including reduced duration of mechanical ventilation, faster resolution of shock, and improved health-related quality of life at 90 days, while healthcare costs over 180 days did not differ between groups. The authors conclude that while the primary outcome was not met, the secondary findings indicate potential clinical benefits of metagenomic sequencing in sepsis management that warrant further investigation.
authors: on behalf of the German Society of Anaesthesiology and Intensive Care (GSAIC) Trials Group
items.citation: Thorsten Brenner, Annabell Skarabis, Stefan Josef Schaller et al.. Effects of a clinical metagenomics intervention on clinical outcomes, healthcare costs, and health-related quality of life in patients with sepsis or septic shock: results of the randomized-controlled DigiSep trial. Intensive Care Medicine. 2026

items.title: mRNA-based influenza vaccine expands the B cell response breadth in humans
items.summary: This study compared immune responses elicited by conventional split-virion influenza vaccines against those induced by an investigational mRNA-based quadrivalent seasonal influenza vaccine in healthy young adults across two consecutive vaccination seasons. Using an observational cohort design, the researchers assessed B cell activity in blood and draining lymph nodes, combining proteomic analysis of serum antibody repertoires with B cell lineage tracing. The mRNA-based vaccine consistently produced higher antibody titers, greater memory B cell frequencies, and sustained germinal center reactions in lymph nodes lasting at least half a year post-vaccination in a subset of participants. Proteomic profiling revealed that mRNA vaccination expanded the number of distinct serum IgG clonotypes, promoted growth within pre-existing clonotypes, and linked these expanded clonotypes to germinal center B cell lineages, indicating ongoing affinity maturation. This remodeling of the antibody repertoire translated into broader binding activity against antigenically divergent influenza strains, demonstrating that persistent germinal center responses are a key mechanism by which mRNA vaccines can widen the breadth of influenza-specific humoral immunity.
items.citation: Hanover C. Matz, Tae-Geun Yu, Kritika Dixit et al.. mRNA-based influenza vaccine expands the B cell response breadth in humans. Nature Immunology. 2026

items.title: Experimental Demonstration of a Balanced Travelling Wave Parametric Amplifier
items.summary: This paper addresses a fundamental limitation of three-wave-mixing travelling-wave parametric amplifiers, namely that an input signal is indistinguishable from one at its image frequency, creating spectral ambiguity that restricts useful bandwidth. To overcome this, the researchers experimentally implemented a balanced amplifier architecture consisting of two kinetic-inductance travelling-wave parametric amplifiers connected between a pair of hybrid couplers, which spatially separates the amplified signal from the output pump and generated idler tones. This configuration effectively doubles the instantaneous image-rejected bandwidth by resolving sideband degeneracy without requiring complex filtering. The demonstrated system achieved substantial signal gain across nearly an octave of bandwidth, with strong pump rejection and meaningful image rejection across the operating band. The results establish balanced travelling-wave parametric amplifiers as a practical broadband solution for applications such as multiplexed qubit readout, spectrometers, and radiometers that require clean, wide-bandwidth amplification.
items.citation: Nikita Klimovich, Peter K. Day, Henry G. Leduc et al.. Experimental Demonstration of a Balanced Travelling Wave Parametric Amplifier. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Pilot-Based Sensing With OFDM and AFDM: A Resource-Matched Performance Comparison
items.summary: This paper addresses the lack of systematic comparison between AFDM and OFDM waveforms for pilot-based radar sensing in next-generation wireless systems. The authors established a fair comparison framework holding bandwidth, frame duration, pilot energy, and reserved-resource overhead constant across multiple pilot configurations, including random, fixed-comb, and shifted-comb OFDM pilots alongside AFDM pilots with guard resources. Performance was evaluated using both aperiodic and cyclic ambiguity functions, with and without cyclic or chirp-periodic prefixes, followed by target detection experiments. The findings reveal that OFDM fixed-comb pilots produce low range sidelobes but suffer from periodic range ambiguity, while AFDM and OFDM shifted-comb pilots suppress zero-Doppler ambiguities; within the common unambiguous region, structured pilot placements for both waveforms outperform random OFDM placement in weak-target detection, though strong-target detection thresholds are similar across all configurations. Notably, at high mobility, an AFDM receiver employing the discrete affine Fourier transform can resolve integer Doppler beyond the conventional maximum unambiguous velocity, outperforming standard receivers at the cost of increased search complexity.
items.citation: Siyi Tang, Yin Xu, Aimin Tang et al.. Pilot-Based Sensing With OFDM and AFDM: A Resource-Matched Performance Comparison. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Joint Subcarrier and Power Allocation for Localization-Oriented Multi-Carrier Underwater ISAC Systems
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of resource allocation in multi-carrier underwater integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems, where the frequency-selective nature of acoustic channels causes uneven localization performance across subcarriers. The authors developed a unified orthogonal subcarrier multiplexing framework and derived closed-form Cramér-Rao bounds under frequency-selective channels with colored noise to quantify localization accuracy. A key contribution is the derivation of a subcarrier-level localization information metric from time-of-arrival Fisher information, which revealed a distance-frequency matching principle describing how localization capability depends jointly on anchor distance and subcarrier frequency. Building on these theoretical insights, the authors designed a low-complexity greedy algorithm that iteratively allocates subcarriers and power to minimize positioning error while satisfying communication quality-of-service constraints. Simulations demonstrated that the proposed scheme achieves substantially lower positioning error bounds than uniform, random, and high-frequency-first allocation strategies across both symmetric and asymmetric network topologies, while maintaining favorable communication-localization tradeoffs.
items.citation: Wei Huang, Sitong Liu, Christos Masouros et al.. Joint Subcarrier and Power Allocation for Localization-Oriented Multi-Carrier Underwater ISAC Systems. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Not All Test-Time Compute Is Evidence: Model-Specific Bias in LLM Reasoning
items.summary: This paper challenges a core assumption underlying test-time scaling methods for large language models — that generating more computation from the same model yields independent evidence about the correct answer. The authors demonstrate that errors within a single reasoning model are actually correlated across repeated samples, reasoning depth, and self-evaluation, meaning additional compute from one model does not constitute genuinely new evidence. To address this, they propose DIA (Disagreement-triggered Independent Arbitration), a method that detects reasoning instability on a per-question basis by identifying disagreement between intermediate and final-stage predictions, then routes those unstable cases to a small panel of diverse, heterogeneous models that solve the question independently without access to the original model's reasoning. Evaluated across multiple benchmarks and base models, DIA consistently outperforms standard chain-of-thought reasoning in the majority of tested settings while activating on only a fraction of examples and using substantially fewer tokens than multi-agent baselines. Ablation studies confirm that both the independence of solving and the heterogeneity of the solver panel are essential to the observed performance gains.
items.citation: Ming Shen, Tianjun Yao. Not All Test-Time Compute Is Evidence: Model-Specific Bias in LLM Reasoning. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Same Person, Different Advice: Auditing LLM Financial Advice with Repeated Risk-Tolerance Responses
items.summary: This paper investigates how large language models behave as financial advisers when clients provide inconsistent answers to a standard risk-tolerance question, a known real-world phenomenon documented in both national panel data and laboratory retesting. The researchers fed hundreds of real household profiles to seven major language models, systematically varying only the risk-tolerance response to measure how much the resulting stock allocation recommendations shifted. They found that recommended stock allocations moved substantially when the risk answer changed, with swings far exceeding the models' own response variability when given identical prompts twice, indicating the models treat the single answer as highly determinative. Attempts to mitigate this instability—such as informing models that the answer is unreliable—reduced swings in some models but introduced new distortions, particularly pushing risk-averse clients toward generic middle allocations rather than honoring their stated preferences. The authors conclude that retest audits measuring same-person response variability should become a standard evaluation practice for AI financial advisers, and that handling an unreliable risk measure raises fundamental questions about client autonomy beyond mere statistical correction.
items.citation: Soovadeep Bakshi, Apurba Bose, Aishwarya Bose et al.. Same Person, Different Advice: Auditing LLM Financial Advice with Repeated Risk-Tolerance Responses. arXiv. 2026

items.title: An Efficient Blind Detection of OFDM Signals with Unknown Parameters
items.summary: This paper addresses the problem of blind detection of OFDM signals in wideband spectrum sensing scenarios where key signal parameters—including power, bandwidth, and carrier frequency—are unknown to the receiver. The authors developed generalized likelihood ratio test detectors for both single-antenna and multi-antenna receivers, covering cases where noise power is either known or unknown, building on an asymptotic covariance analysis that yields a tractable discrete-time signal model. A key contribution is the use of cumulative-sum operations to reduce the detection problem to an efficient one-dimensional search, substantially lowering computational complexity in both antenna configurations. Theoretical analysis of a conventional energy detector and a hypothetical uniformly most powerful test was also provided to characterize how system parameters influence detection performance. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed detectors approach the performance of a genie-aided detector with full parameter knowledge while considerably outperforming conventional detection methods.
items.citation: Ata Bartu Soyuer, Gokhan M. Guvensen. An Efficient Blind Detection of OFDM Signals with Unknown Parameters. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Two Pentaplex Real-Time Fluorescent PCR Assays for Simultaneous Detection of Ten Ovine Respiratory and Reproductive Pathogens.
items.summary: The paper developed and evaluated two pentaplex real-time fluorescent PCR assay panels designed to simultaneously detect ten important ovine pathogens, divided into those causing respiratory disease and those causing reproductive disease in sheep. Each panel was validated using reference pathogens and plasmids, with performance characterized through sensitivity, reproducibility, and specificity testing. The assays achieved very low detection limits, excellent linearity, minimal variation between and within runs, and no cross-reactivity among the ten targets. Clinical validation using a large collection of field samples from multiple Chinese provinces demonstrated strong agreement with established reference diagnostic methods. The authors conclude that these multiplex assays offer a rapid, sensitive, and reliable approach for differential diagnosis and surveillance of major ovine respiratory and reproductive pathogens.
items.citation: Wang S, Bai Z, Wan B et al.. Two Pentaplex Real-Time Fluorescent PCR Assays for Simultaneous Detection of Ten Ovine Respiratory and Reproductive Pathogens.. Viruses. 2026

items.title: Nanobodies: A Promising Toolkit for Diagnostic Applications
items.summary: This review examines nanobodies — single-domain antigen-binding fragments derived from camelid heavy-chain-only antibodies — as tools for diagnostic applications, focusing on the structural and biochemical properties that make them attractive alternatives to conventional antibodies. Their small size, high solubility, stability, and ability to access epitopes that are less reachable by traditional antibodies contribute to their utility across a range of detection contexts. The authors survey how nanobodies have been integrated into diverse diagnostic platforms, including ELISA, lateral flow immunoassays, biosensors, and in vivo imaging modalities such as PET, SPECT, and quantum dot conjugates. Advances in multivalent design, site-specific conjugation, and expression systems are highlighted as key developments enhancing diagnostic performance. The review also outlines ongoing clinical trials and emerging strategies aimed at producing scalable, sensitive, and application-ready nanobody-based diagnostic platforms.
items.citation: Wei Wu, Abid Ali, Li Sun et al.. Nanobodies: A Promising Toolkit for Diagnostic Applications. SmartMat. 2026

items.title: Smartphone AI-Enabled Lateral Flow Immunoassay Platform Using Advanced Quantum Dots for Intelligent Quantitative Diagnostics.
items.citation: Atta S, Thorsen TL, Vasse T et al.. Smartphone AI-Enabled Lateral Flow Immunoassay Platform Using Advanced Quantum Dots for Intelligent Quantitative Diagnostics.. ACS applied materials & interfaces. 2026

items.title: Recent advances in lateral flow immunoassay for virus detection: current achievements, challenges and future prospects.
items.summary: This review examines the current state and future potential of lateral flow immunoassay technology for detecting viral pathogens in the context of infectious disease diagnostics. The authors systematically survey recent advances across three main dimensions: nanomaterial-based signal generation strategies spanning colorimetric, fluorescent, magnetic, surface-enhanced Raman scattering, and photothermal approaches; multimodal and multiplex detection methods; and the integration of machine learning for signal interpretation and assay optimization. The review also covers applications of lateral flow immunoassays for detecting viral antigens, antibodies, and nucleic acids. A central argument of the paper is that this technology should be reconceptualized beyond point-of-care testing toward a point-of-need self-testing platform capable of supporting large-scale epidemic surveillance and pandemic preparedness. The authors conclude by outlining persistent limitations including sensitivity, specificity, cost, and stability, while proposing future directions centered on advanced nanomaterials, intelligent data processing, and multi-target detection to strengthen global public health infrastructure.
items.citation: Li L, Liu F, He X et al.. Recent advances in lateral flow immunoassay for virus detection: current achievements, challenges and future prospects.. Talanta. 2026

items.title: Rational Control of Antibody Orientation for Enhancing Sensitivity and Specificity in Lateral Flow Immunoassays With Clinical Validation.
items.summary: This paper investigated strategies to improve the sensitivity and specificity of lateral flow assays for point-of-care cancer biomarker detection, addressing limitations caused by inefficient antibody orientation and poor signal transduction. The researchers developed a universal approach that combines orientation-controlled antibody conjugation on immunoprobes with a biotin-streptavidin-modified test line to maximize antigen accessibility and suppress nonspecific binding. This dual-site orientation strategy achieved substantial improvements in detection limits for multiple cancer biomarkers, including cytokeratin fragment and carcinoembryonic antigen, compared to conventional randomly conjugated probes, and the authors notably found that probe performance rankings can invert depending on the capture chemistry used, underscoring the necessity of optimizing both conjugation sites simultaneously. The strategy was demonstrated to be broadly applicable across several additional clinically relevant tumor markers. Finally, a multiplexed format using fluorescent polymer dots enabled simultaneous dual-biomarker detection with minimal cross-reactivity, and the approach was clinically validated against a hospital reference method using patient serum samples.
items.citation: Wang PH, Shunmuga Nainar SN, Zhuang BH et al.. Rational Control of Antibody Orientation for Enhancing Sensitivity and Specificity in Lateral Flow Immunoassays With Clinical Validation.. Advanced healthcare materials. 2026

items.title: Ligand-directed Janus self-assembly with dual-aggregation enabling magneto-optical switching for enhanced lateral flow immunoassay.
items.citation: Liu T, Sun J, Huang J et al.. Ligand-directed Janus self-assembly with dual-aggregation enabling magneto-optical switching for enhanced lateral flow immunoassay.. Biosensors & bioelectronics. 2026

items.title: SARS-CoV-2 Point-of-Care Testing Modalities: Integrating Molecular, Immunological, Biosensor, and AI Approaches.
items.summary: This review examined the landscape of point-of-care testing technologies developed for COVID-19 diagnosis, motivated by the pandemic's demonstration of urgent need for rapid, decentralized diagnostic tools. The authors conducted a structured literature search across major databases and evaluated molecular assays, antigen-based tests, antibody-based assays, biosensor platforms, and artificial intelligence-assisted diagnostic approaches. Molecular methods such as rapid RT-PCR, LAMP, and CRISPR-based technologies were found to offer high sensitivity and specificity suitable for decentralized use, while antigen tests provide rapid and affordable screening but with variable performance depending on viral load, symptom timing, and circulating variants. Antibody-based testing was found most appropriate for seroprevalence studies and immune monitoring rather than acute infection detection, and emerging biosensor and AI-enabled systems showed analytical promise but remain largely at prototype or early-validation stages requiring further clinical assessment. The review concludes that no single testing modality is universally optimal, and that complementary use of these approaches, alongside advances in multiplex testing and variant-resilient detection, will be essential for both COVID-19 management and future infectious disease preparedness.
items.citation: Hetta HF, Ahmed R, Haseeb A et al.. SARS-CoV-2 Point-of-Care Testing Modalities: Integrating Molecular, Immunological, Biosensor, and AI Approaches.. Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland). 2026

items.title: Synergistic Multicomponent Nucleopeptide-Based Hydrogels: Harnessing DNA-Base Pairing and Electrostatic Complementarities
items.summary: This study investigated how combining charge complementarity and DNA-base pairing complementarity influences the properties of multicomponent peptide-based hydrogels. The researchers synthesized six nucleopeptides derived from two tetrapeptide sequences — one negatively charged and one positively charged at physiological pH — each functionalized with one of the four DNA nucleobases via a peptide nucleic acid moiety. Through a multiscale systematic characterization, they examined how mixing electrostatically complementary and/or nucleobase-complementary components affected mechanical and physicochemical properties, including gelation time, stiffness, sol-gel transition temperature, stress resistance, and fibrillar network morphology. The results demonstrate that careful selection of components allows precise tuning of hydrogel properties, while also revealing unexpected behaviors that highlight the complexity of these bioinspired hybrid systems. Overall, the findings underscore the potential of synergistic multicomponent nucleopeptide approaches for developing high-performance supramolecular hydrogels with tailored characteristics for biomedical and biotechnological applications.
items.citation: Tristan Giraud, Marine Koch, Paul Hoschtettler et al.. Synergistic Multicomponent Nucleopeptide-Based Hydrogels: Harnessing DNA-Base Pairing and Electrostatic Complementarities. ACS Materials Au. 2026

items.title: Microneedle array platforms for drug delivery and biomarker sensing: From skin mechanics guided design to scalable manufacture for clinical utility
items.summary: This review examines microneedle array patches as platforms for transdermal and intradermal drug delivery and biomarker sensing, focusing on the persistent gap between laboratory prototypes and commercially approved products. The authors analyze the competing mechanical design constraints microneedles face, namely the need to be slender enough to penetrate skin painlessly while being substantial enough to carry clinically meaningful drug doses, situating these requirements within a discussion of skin anatomy and the insertion mechanics of different microneedle geometries. Fabrication approaches are compared with attention to their scalability, cost efficiency, and manufacturing throughput, alongside considerations of biocompatibility and drug dissolution behavior within dermal tissue. The review also surveys applicator designs and their mechanisms for delivering consistent insertion force, and outlines the regulatory science challenges that must be navigated for market approval. Collectively, the paper frames the outstanding technical, commercial, and regulatory barriers that must be overcome before microneedle-based systems can achieve widespread clinical utility as self-applied, on-demand therapeutic devices.
items.citation: Jiachi Zhou, Lei Wu, Minna Wyttenbach et al.. Microneedle array platforms for drug delivery and biomarker sensing: From skin mechanics guided design to scalable manufacture for clinical utility. Journal of Controlled Release. 2026

items.title: Recent advances in Alzheimer’s disease: From molecular mechanisms to therapeutic strategies
items.summary: This review examines the current state of Alzheimer's disease research, encompassing both the molecular mechanisms underlying the disease and emerging therapeutic approaches. The authors synthesize recent advances across several interconnected areas, including the pathological roles of amyloid plaques and neurofibrillary tangles, apolipoprotein E biology, neuroimmunology, and biomarker discovery. New disease-modifying therapies that reduce amyloid burden in the brain have demonstrated the ability to slow cognitive decline, marking a meaningful shift in the treatment landscape, though interventions capable of halting or preventing cognitive impairment altogether remain unrealized. The review frames these developments as transformative for both diagnosis and treatment, suggesting the field is moving toward a future in which Alzheimer's disease may ultimately be both treatable and preventable.
items.citation: Michelle Diane Rudman, Jason D. Ulrich, David M. Holtzman. Recent advances in Alzheimer’s disease: From molecular mechanisms to therapeutic strategies. Cell. 2026

items.title: The Oral–Gut–Brain Axis: From Periodontal Dysbiosis to Neuroinflammation—Mechanistic Pathways, Salivary and Intestinal Biomarkers, and Therapeutic Targets: A Narrative Review
items.summary: This narrative review examined the mechanistic connections linking periodontal disease, gut health, and brain function through what the authors term the oral–gut–brain axis, with particular attention to how oral dysbiosis may propagate systemic inflammation leading to neurodegeneration. The authors conducted a structured literature search across major databases to synthesize evidence on molecular pathways, relevant biomarkers, and therapeutic targets spanning this tripartite system. Key periodontal pathogens, notably Porphyromonas gingivalis and Fusobacterium nucleatum, were found in preclinical and observational studies to be detectable in the gut, where they associate with compromised intestinal barrier integrity and altered microbial composition, changes that in turn correlate with increased blood–brain barrier permeability, microglial activation, and amyloid-beta accumulation. Salivary markers such as matrix metalloproteinases and interleukins, alongside intestinal markers including short-chain fatty acids and calprotectin, are proposed as non-invasive tools for monitoring inflammatory burden across the entire axis. The authors conclude that while this framework plausibly unifies the comorbidity patterns seen across periodontal, cardiometabolic, and neurodegenerative conditions, existing evidence remains largely associative and requires validation through longitudinal human studies before causal claims or clinical interventions can be firmly established.
items.citation: Caterina Nela Dumitru, Alina Oana Dumitru, Gabriel Valeriu Popa et al.. The Oral–Gut–Brain Axis: From Periodontal Dysbiosis to Neuroinflammation—Mechanistic Pathways, Salivary and Intestinal Biomarkers, and Therapeutic Targets: A Narrative Review. Dentistry Journal. 2026

items.title: Quantum dot biosensors for highly sensitive and multiplex detection in biomedical diagnostics
items.summary: This review examines quantum dot-based biosensors as platforms for biomedical diagnostics, focusing on their capacity to overcome limitations of conventional immunoassays such as low sensitivity, photobleaching, and poor optical tissue penetration. The authors survey recent advances across fluorescent, photoelectrochemical, and electrochemiluminescent sensing formats, connecting quantum dot surface engineering strategies—including attachment of antibodies, aptamers, peptides, and nucleic acids—to underlying sensing mechanisms. Near-infrared-emitting quantum dots receive particular attention for their ability to reduce tissue autofluorescence and improve imaging depth for real-time in vivo molecular tracking. The review covers detection of pathogens, cancer biomarkers, and metabolites, while also addressing persistent challenges around toxicity and biocompatibility alongside emerging mitigation strategies such as cadmium-free compositions and surface passivation. The authors offer an integrated, mechanistic framework linking material design to clinical translation, positioning quantum dot biosensors as a foundation for next-generation multiplex diagnostic development.
items.citation: Soumendu Patra, Harshita Shand. Quantum dot biosensors for highly sensitive and multiplex detection in biomedical diagnostics. Discover Sensors. 2026

items.title: Learning to Correct Geometry in Generated Videos
items.summary: This paper addresses the problem of geometric inconsistency in AI-generated videos, where structures warp incorrectly under camera motion and parallax becomes unrealistic. The authors argue this stems from a data imbalance in web-scale training corpora, where dynamic objects filmed by stationary cameras vastly outnumber examples of viewpoint-induced appearance changes. To tackle this, they developed Video Geometry Corrector, a post-hoc video-to-video model trained on synthetically constructed paired data, where geometrically consistent real videos are paired with distorted counterparts generated by an image-to-video inpainting model using trajectory-adaptive keyframes. The model learns to correct geometric distortions without modifying the underlying video generator, and incorporates optical flow as an auxiliary signal to distinguish camera motion from object motion. Experiments on both pose-conditioned and prompt-driven benchmarks demonstrate that their approach improves geometric consistency across multiple source video generators, with further gains observed when scaling to a larger backbone.
items.citation: Weijie Lyu, Tiancheng Shen, Jason Li et al.. Learning to Correct Geometry in Generated Videos. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Flashing with colours: Photometric indicators of an early interaction in type II supernovae
items.summary: This paper investigated early-time photometric and spectroscopic properties of type II supernovae, focusing on whether photometry alone can identify events that show evidence of interaction with dense circumstellar material. The researchers assembled a large sample of supernovae observed with high cadence and precision across multiple optical bands, categorising events based on the presence or absence of transient narrow emission lines ("flash features") in spectra taken within days of explosion. They found that supernovae displaying flash features tend to be more luminous at peak, exhibit longer rise times in the blue band, and are systematically bluer than their non-flash counterparts, with these colour differences most pronounced around twenty days after explosion. A particularly diagnostic feature emerged in the form of colour-curve breaks occurring within thirty days of explosion, where the change in slope across the break combined with peak absolute magnitude cleanly separates flash from non-flash events. The authors conclude that photometric observations alone may be sufficient to identify supernovae undergoing circumstellar interaction, even without early spectroscopic follow-up.
items.citation: A. Mendez-Llorca, G. Folatelli, C. P. Gutierrez et al.. Flashing with colours: Photometric indicators of an early interaction in type II supernovae. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Behavioral Couplings: From Formation to Behavioral Emergence in Language Models
items.summary: This paper investigates how fine-tuning large language models on one behavior can inadvertently cause unrelated behaviors to emerge, a phenomenon the authors term "behavioral coupling." The researchers studied how these couplings form by training models on documents that describe two distinct behaviors together, then fine-tuning those models to elicit only one of the paired behaviors. They found that the second, untargeted behavior reliably emerged as a consequence, even when it was entirely unrelated to the fine-tuning objective, while control models lacking the paired-behavior training showed no such effect. More troublingly, the authors discovered that couplings can compose transitively: when two separate document sets each share one behavior in common, fine-tuning on a behavior from one set can trigger the emergence of a behavior from the other set, even though those behaviors never appeared together in any single training document. These findings suggest that the unintended behavioral consequences of fine-tuning may be difficult to anticipate or trace and that evaluating a model's current behavior alone is insufficient to predict the effects of future fine-tuning.
items.citation: Dongyoon Hahm, Woogyeol Jin, Dennis Wei et al.. Behavioral Couplings: From Formation to Behavioral Emergence in Language Models. arXiv. 2026

items.title: ENFR: Evidence Networks with Flow-Matched References for Amortized Simulation-Based Model Inference
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of computing the Bayesian evidence — the marginal likelihood of data given a model — which is essential for model comparison, misspecification testing, and goodness-of-fit assessment but is notoriously difficult to estimate. The authors propose ENFR (Evidence Networks with Flow-matched References), a method that learns Bayes factors relative to a flow-matched reference distribution and then recovers absolute evidence values in an amortized fashion, building on an existing Evidence Network framework. A key theoretical contribution is a novel architecture, accompanied by a formal proof, that jointly learns the individual evidences for a set of competing models simultaneously. Across a range of scientific benchmark applications, ENFR outperforms flow-based baselines and achieves the best performance among all density estimation methods considered. The method provides fast, accurate, and amortized absolute evidence estimates, enabling minimum-volume goodness-of-fit tests that are critical for validating simulation-based inference pipelines.
items.citation: Kai Lehman, Jameson Dong, Carolina Cuesta-Lazaro et al.. ENFR: Evidence Networks with Flow-Matched References for Amortized Simulation-Based Model Inference. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Learning Personalized Memory Gating from Delayed One-Sided Feedback
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of selectively storing facts in finite memory banks for language-model agents, where existing approaches fail to capture user-specific patterns of information reuse. The authors propose a retrieval-based labeling strategy that determines which facts are worth storing by tracking whether each fact is later retrieved and used in generating responses. They formulate the memory gating problem as contextual apple tasting with delayed one-sided feedback—a setting where only positive feedback is observable and it arrives with a delay—and introduce a Warm-Start UCB algorithm that combines offline learning from historical data with online adaptation to individual users. A theoretical regret bound is established that degrades gracefully with initialization error and feature dimensionality under moderate delay conditions. Empirical evaluations show that the proposed method outperforms baseline approaches across varying memory budgets and history lengths, demonstrating its effectiveness as a personalized memory gating policy.
items.citation: Kaixuan Ji, Zixiang Chen, Wenting Zhao et al.. Learning Personalized Memory Gating from Delayed One-Sided Feedback. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Regularity Aspects of Temperature in Heat-Conducting Fluid Systems via De Giorgi Methods
items.summary: This paper investigates the regularity properties of temperature in the compressible Navier-Stokes equations governing heat-conducting fluids, where the pressure formulation incorporates a Stefan-radiation correction term. Under minimal assumptions on the density and velocity fields, the authors apply the De Giorgi iteration method to demonstrate that weak solutions automatically possess Hölder continuity in the temperature component. This conditional regularity result is then leveraged to establish a global-in-time existence and uniqueness result for regular solutions to a simplified compressible potential flow system for heat-conducting fluids, valid even for arbitrarily large initial data.
items.citation: Nilasis Chaudhuri, Piotr B. Mucha, Tomasz Piasecki et al.. Regularity Aspects of Temperature in Heat-Conducting Fluid Systems via De Giorgi Methods. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Beyond lateral flow: vertical flow immunoassays as thermodynamically assisted rapid diagnostics.
items.summary: Lateral flow immunoassays dominate point-of-care testing but suffer from fundamental architectural limitations including poor analyte capture efficiency, high non-specific background, limited multiplexing capacity, and unreliability at high analyte concentrations due to the hook effect. This review examines vertical flow immunoassays as an alternative platform that stacks membranes to decouple convective delivery from immunoreaction kinetics, enabling thermodynamic washing, two-dimensional multiplexing arrays, and sequential surface chemistry that eliminates the hook effect. Head-to-head comparisons with chemistry-matched lateral flow assays demonstrate substantial improvements in limits of detection, and integration with surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy, electrochemical transduction, nanoparticle amplification, and deep-learning inference pushes sensitivity into the sub-picogram-per-milliliter range. The review surveys the physical-chemical principles underlying vertical flow assay performance and maps its applications across clinical diagnostics, food safety, and environmental monitoring. It also critically examines the engineering barriers that have prevented this higher-sensitivity platform from achieving commercial scale and outlines a pathway toward practical deployment.
items.citation: Nainar SNS, Chu YY, Lin HC et al.. Beyond lateral flow: vertical flow immunoassays as thermodynamically assisted rapid diagnostics.. Chemical communications (Cambridge, England). 2026

items.title: Validation and performance of a rapid HIV-1 viral load assay.
items.summary: The study evaluated the Xpert HIV-1 Viral Load XC assay as a candidate for primary nucleic acid testing within HIV-1 diagnostic workflows, with the goal of enabling simultaneous diagnosis and viral load measurement in a single clinical encounter at or near the point of care. Researchers assessed the assay's analytical range, precision, reproducibility, and agreement against standard-of-care approaches, including the Roche cobas HIV-1 quantitative assay and several other HIV testing platforms. The assay demonstrated a strong analytical range with complete detection across tested concentrations and showed full agreement with the comparator assay on a panel of positive and negative plasma samples. However, positive agreement with other assays was moderate, with most discrepancies occurring in samples below the lower limit of quantification, and the assay produced a small proportion of invalid results. While turnaround time was substantially faster than conventional batch testing, the findings highlight ongoing limitations in sensitivity that must be addressed before rapid molecular diagnostics can be fully integrated into primary HIV-1 diagnostic algorithms.
items.citation: Uhteg K, Bayan MH, Boudreau A et al.. Validation and performance of a rapid HIV-1 viral load assay.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: Patient perspectives on point-of-care HIV nucleic acid tests for viral load monitoring in Seattle, WA.
items.summary: This study examined patient perspectives on point-of-care nucleic acid testing for HIV viral load monitoring as an alternative to standard laboratory-based tests, which can take days to return results. Researchers invited people with HIV participating in a clinical study to complete acceptability surveys and in-depth interviews about a semi-quantitative point-of-care test run on fingerstick whole blood samples within the clinic setting. Participants generally found the approach acceptable and preferred its faster turnaround time and fingerstick convenience compared to conventional viral load testing. However, participants expressed a desire for an even shorter turnaround time than the approximately two hours the test required, as well as a lower limit of detection than the current threshold, which the authors note would improve feasibility for implementation in United States clinical settings. The findings suggest point-of-care nucleic acid testing could be particularly valuable for patients who are incompletely engaged in HIV care.
items.citation: Niemann LA, Murphy M, Violette LR et al.. Patient perspectives on point-of-care HIV nucleic acid tests for viral load monitoring in Seattle, WA.. AIDS care. 2026

items.title: Feasibility, Acceptability, and Test Performance of Point-of-Care Nucleic Acid Tests for HIV Testing and Viral Load Monitoring in the United States: Prospective Longitudinal Mixed-Methods Study.
items.summary: This paper describes the design and enrollment progress of the GAIN study, which evaluated point-of-care nucleic acid tests for HIV diagnosis and viral load monitoring in community and clinical settings in the United States. The study enrolled participants across two sites — a hospital-based clinic and an LGBTQ+ community center in Seattle — using two versions of a whole blood point-of-care nucleic acid test alongside standard laboratory testing, with participants seeking HIV testing, pre-exposure prophylaxis, or post-exposure prophylaxis, as well as people already living with HIV. The study employed a mixed-methods design incorporating a randomized clinical trial, acceptability surveys, qualitative interviews, and time-and-motion observations to assess feasibility, acceptability, and test performance. Enrollment was successfully completed across the study period, with hundreds of research visits documented and data collection across all study arms concluded. Analyses of test performance, clinical outcomes such as time to viral suppression, and qualitative findings are anticipated in forthcoming publications, meaning no outcome results are yet reported.
items.citation: Niemann LA, Violette LR, Cornelius-Hudson A et al.. Feasibility, Acceptability, and Test Performance of Point-of-Care Nucleic Acid Tests for HIV Testing and Viral Load Monitoring in the United States: Prospective Longitudinal Mixed-Methods Study.. JMIR research protocols. 2026

items.title: Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?
items.summary: This debate article examined the longstanding question in exercise immunology of whether exercise itself can suppress immune function and increase susceptibility to infection. The paper structured opposing arguments around four key contested issues: whether athletes are genuinely more infection-prone than the general population, whether exercise independently alters immunity beyond the influence of confounding factors such as sleep disruption, travel, anxiety, and nutritional deficits, the validity of biomarkers used to assess immune health in those performing arduous exercise, and the overall quality of evidence underpinning claims about exercise and infection risk. There is broad agreement that regular moderate-intensity exercise is beneficial for immune defense, particularly in older adults and those with chronic disease, while high-performance athletes and military personnel appear to experience elevated infection burdens. Both sides agreed that infection susceptibility is multifactorial in origin, but the central unresolved question is whether exercise itself is a causative driver of increased infection risk rather than merely one component of a broader cluster of stressors. The authors call for more rigorous empirical research to disentangle exercise-specific effects from the many coexisting factors that characterize high-performance sporting and military contexts.
items.citation: Richard J. Simpson, Richard J. Simpson, Maree Gleeson et al.. Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications
items.summary: This review paper examines how the integration of multiomics technologies and artificial intelligence is reshaping precision drug discovery and translational medicine. The authors synthesize how approaches such as genome-wide association studies, transcriptomic profiling, proteomic interaction mapping, and metabolomic sequencing generate deep insights into disease mechanisms, while deep learning architectures process these complex biological datasets to identify patterns and build predictive models. The review covers the application of this combined framework across the drug development pipeline, including target identification, lead optimization, drug repositioning, de novo compound discovery, virtual screening, pharmacokinetic modeling, and safety assessment. The authors highlight illustrative cases in oncology, neurodegenerative diseases, and cardiovascular conditions to demonstrate therapeutic potential, while also acknowledging persistent challenges such as harmonizing disparate data streams, ensuring reproducibility, and reducing algorithmic bias. The paper concludes that the convergence of multiomics and artificial intelligence enables more precise therapeutic interventions and represents a foundational shift toward data-driven, bench-to-clinic translational medicine.
items.citation: Yuqing Liu, Kun Zhu, Weijun Peng et al.. Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Trial design and end points in hepatocellular carcinoma: an EASL–AASLD–ILCA consensus statement
items.citation: Josep Maria Llovet, Ezequiel Mauro, Lorenza Rimassa et al.. Trial design and end points in hepatocellular carcinoma: an EASL–AASLD–ILCA consensus statement. Nature Reviews Clinical Oncology. 2026

items.title: CRISPR-Cas systems as next-generation antimicrobials: a systemic review of mechanisms, delivery strategies, and translational challenges
items.summary: This systematic review examined the potential of CRISPR-Cas systems as next-generation antimicrobials to address the growing crisis of multidrug-resistant bacterial infections. The authors synthesized preclinical and experimental evidence on various CRISPR effectors, including Cas9, Cas12, and Cas13, evaluating their antibacterial mechanisms, delivery platforms, and therapeutic outcomes across a range of bacterial targets. The review found that CRISPR-Cas approaches effectively killed or resensitized multidrug-resistant bacteria through mechanisms such as chromosomal double-strand break induction, resistance plasmid elimination, and RNA-targeted cleavage, with phage-mediated delivery showing the most consistent efficacy. One CRISPR-enhanced engineered bacteriophage cocktail has progressed to clinical evaluation, signaling meaningful translational momentum. However, the authors identified substantial remaining barriers, including limited bacterial host range, physiological instability, the emergence of escape mutations, and insufficient safety data, concluding that advances in delivery optimization, multiplex targeting, and regulatory frameworks will be necessary before clinical translation can be realized.
items.citation: Maha S.I. Wizrah. CRISPR-Cas systems as next-generation antimicrobials: a systemic review of mechanisms, delivery strategies, and translational challenges. Frontiers in Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Oral Nirmatrelvir–Ritonavir for Covid-19 in Higher-Risk Outpatients
items.summary: These two open-label platform trials investigated whether nirmatrelvir–ritonavir reduces hospitalisation or death in higher-risk outpatients with COVID-19 who were predominantly vaccinated, a population in which the drug's effectiveness had previously been unclear. Higher-risk adults who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 and had been symptomatic for five days or fewer were randomly assigned to receive either usual care plus a five-day course of nirmatrelvir–ritonavir or usual care alone, with the primary outcome being hospitalisation or death within 28 days. Across both trials, rates of hospitalisation or death were very low in both treatment and control groups, and nirmatrelvir–ritonavir did not demonstrate superiority over usual care for this outcome in either trial. Although a substudy confirmed that the drug reduced viral load by the end of treatment, this virological effect did not translate into a clinical benefit in terms of severe outcomes. The trials conclude that nirmatrelvir–ritonavir does not reduce hospitalisation or death among vaccinated higher-risk individuals infected with SARS-CoV-2.
items.citation: Christopher C. Butler, Andrew Pinto, Victoria Harris et al.. Oral Nirmatrelvir–Ritonavir for Covid-19 in Higher-Risk Outpatients. New England Journal of Medicine. 2026

items.title: European consensus-based interdisciplinary guideline for invasive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma. Part 1: Diagnostics and prevention – Update 2026
items.summary: This guideline paper addresses invasive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, one of the most prevalent cancers in white populations, with a focus on updating recommendations for diagnostics and prevention. A multidisciplinary European expert collaboration reviewed current literature and consensus to revise a prior guideline version, covering both immunocompetent and immunosuppressed patients. The update introduces a new five-group classification system for difficult-to-treat disease, distinguishing between complex common tumors, locally advanced cases, and those with locoregional or distant metastases. Diagnosis follows a stepwise approach beginning with clinical and dermatoscopic assessment, confirmed by histopathology, followed by staging procedures including imaging where indicated, and culminating in integration of findings using established staging systems. Prevention recommendations include oral nicotinamide and sun protection measures, while risk stratification is guided by the accumulation of recognized tumor and patient risk factors.
items.citation: Alexander J. Stratigos, Clio Dessinioti, Claus Garbe et al.. European consensus-based interdisciplinary guideline for invasive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma. Part 1: Diagnostics and prevention – Update 2026. European Journal of Cancer. 2026

items.title: Lyapunov Exponents in Power Systems: A Survey of Theory and Applications in Stability, Control, Forecasting, and Protection
items.summary: This survey paper examines the application of Lyapunov exponents, which measure the average exponential rate at which nearby trajectories in phase space converge or diverge, to problems in electrical power systems. The review organizes more than a century of publications spanning several decades into four principal domains: stability analysis and real-time monitoring, chaos characterization and control, forecasting and predictability analysis, and protection along with fault diagnosis. The paper traces methodological evolution from early demonstrations of chaos in simplified machine models through to contemporary data-driven and machine-learning-augmented approaches applied to grids increasingly dominated by inverter-based resources. For each domain, the authors compare model-based and data-driven estimation strategies, assess available benchmarks, and identify validation gaps. The survey concludes by outlining open research problems, positioning Lyapunov exponents as broadly useful diagnostics across transient and voltage stability assessment, renewable energy forecasting, and condition monitoring in modern power systems.
items.citation: Mohammad Almomani, Venkataramana Ajjarapu. Lyapunov Exponents in Power Systems: A Survey of Theory and Applications in Stability, Control, Forecasting, and Protection. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Dynamic Load Balancing under Restricting Updates
items.summary: This paper studies dynamic load balancing, where the goal is to assign weighted jobs to machines in a bipartite graph so as to minimize the maximum machine load, with the assignment maintained efficiently as the graph changes over time. Prior work had addressed only the incremental setting (edge insertions and job deletions), leaving the decremental setting (edge deletions and job insertions) open. The authors develop a new algorithm that maintains a near-optimal fractional solution under decremental updates with polylogarithmic update time, drawing inspiration from a distributed computing algorithm in the CONGEST model and introducing a novel analytic framework to prove its dynamic performance guarantees. They additionally present a general black-box rounding scheme that converts fractional solutions into integral ones, yielding a decremental algorithm for approximate integral load balancing with comparable update time bounds. The same rounding scheme, when combined with the prior incremental fractional algorithm, also achieves analogous guarantees for the incremental integral setting.
items.citation: Aaron Bernstein, Sayan Bhattacharya, Peter Kiss et al.. Dynamic Load Balancing under Restricting Updates. arXiv. 2026

items.title: An exact finite-state representation of viscoelastic memory for accelerated sea-level modeling: SLEvolve v1.0
items.summary: This paper addresses the computational bottleneck in Glacial Isostatic Adjustment models, which simulate how the solid Earth and oceans respond to changing ice loads and are increasingly embedded in coupled ice-sheet and ensemble simulations. The standard approach re-sums the entire load history at each time step, producing a quadratic scaling in computational cost that becomes prohibitive for long simulations. By recognizing that the viscoelastic relaxation kernel has an exponential form, the authors reformulated the viscous response as an exact recursive update of a finite set of modal states, eliminating the need to replay the full load history and reducing the algorithmic complexity from quadratic to linear. This reformulation, implemented in the open-source solver SLEvolve v1.0 alongside improvements to spherical-harmonic transforms, file handling, and iteration initialization, achieves an end-to-end speedup of several orders of magnitude relative to a standard solver, compressing day-long simulations to under a minute on a workstation. The paper also presents the development process as a case study in combining human-derived analytical insight with AI-assisted software engineering, where numerical regression tests and performance profiling guided and constrained the automated implementation choices.
items.citation: Xiyuan Bao, S. Mostafa Mousavi, Konstantin Latychev et al.. An exact finite-state representation of viscoelastic memory for accelerated sea-level modeling: SLEvolve v1.0. arXiv. 2026

items.title: From Alpha to Execution: Trading Horizons, Regimes, and Schedules under Concave Impact and Hurst Scaling
items.summary: This paper studies optimal trade execution when two standard assumptions of classical models are relaxed: market impact follows a concave power law rather than a linear rule, and price fluctuations are scaled by a Hurst exponent rather than assumed to be purely diffusive. The authors address two linked problems: first, choosing how long to work an order by maximizing the Sharpe ratio of the trade's realized profit and loss, where slower execution reduces variance and can lower per-share cost under concave impact, while urgency arises from alpha that decays while the order is being filled. They show that the existence of an interior optimal horizon depends on the signs of just two quantities—a duration elasticity of impact related to the gap between impact persistence and the Hurst exponent, and a net urgency parameter—and that when an interior solution exists the optimal window is remarkably insensitive to impact coefficients, order size, and volume. Second, given a fixed execution window, the authors derive the optimal trading schedule using convex programming, finding a closed-form solution expressed via the incomplete beta function that is front-loaded and tapers smoothly to zero. This schedule achieves meaningful cost savings relative to a naive time-weighted average price strategy, with the fraction of the window actually used governed by a single dimensionless robustness parameter for which a calibration procedure is provided.
items.citation: Dnyanesh Kulkarni, Revant Nayar. From Alpha to Execution: Trading Horizons, Regimes, and Schedules under Concave Impact and Hurst Scaling. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Plastic Flow Rule Based on Dislocation Link Velocity
items.summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework for predicting plastic shear rates on individual slip systems in face-centered cubic single crystals by integrating contributions from dislocation links of varying lengths. The approach employs a generalized Orowan equation that expresses slip-system shear rates in terms of dislocation link density and average link velocity as functions of link length. The theory is validated against discrete dislocation dynamics simulations across all twelve slip systems and a large number of loading orientations, achieving accurate reproduction of the simulation data. A key finding is that the previously observed exponential dependence of plastic shear rate on resolved shear stress emerges naturally from the exponential tail of the link-length distribution filtered through a threshold-like velocity function, requiring no thermally activated mechanism to explain it. The work further demonstrates that the availability of long dislocation links, rather than the resolved shear stress itself, is the dominant factor controlling slip-system activity, with inter-slip-system interactions manifesting primarily through the link-length distribution rather than through the link velocity.
items.citation: Hanfeng Zhai, Sh. Akhondzadeh, Ryan B. Sills et al.. Plastic Flow Rule Based on Dislocation Link Velocity. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Spatial Distribution of Mean PAoI in LEO Satellite-enabled IoT Networks
items.summary: This paper investigates the freshness of information delivered through Low Earth Orbit satellite networks supporting large-scale Internet of Things deployments, with a focus on scenarios where terrestrial cellular coverage is unavailable. Using stochastic geometry tools, the authors derive the spatial distribution of the uplink mean Peak Age of Information and the meta distribution of the conditional coverage probability for a fully loaded LEO satellite-enabled IoT network. The meta distribution framework captures node-level heterogeneity in link performance across the network rather than only average behavior. Numerical results reveal how the number of deployed satellites and their orbital altitudes jointly shape both coverage probability distributions and the spatial spread of mean Peak Age of Information. The analysis further identifies optimal satellite beamwidth configurations for different deployment scenarios, providing guidance for minimizing conditional mean Peak Age of Information across varying network designs.
items.citation: Badiaa Gabr, Mustafa A. Kishk. Spatial Distribution of Mean PAoI in LEO Satellite-enabled IoT Networks. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Multistate Analysis of Longitudinal Care Outcomes Among People Newly Linked to Human Immunodeficiency Virus Care in Missouri.
items.summary: This study examined longitudinal patterns of HIV care engagement and viral suppression among people newly linked to HIV care in St. Louis, Missouri, a priority jurisdiction for the Ending the HIV Epidemic initiative. Using multistate analytic methods, researchers tracked individuals over three years following their initial clinic linkage, classifying them across nine mutually exclusive states defined by clinic engagement status and viral load suppression. The analysis revealed that roughly half of patients remained continuously retained in care after one year, while nearly a third had disengaged, and viral suppression was substantially lower among those who reengaged compared to those continuously retained. Younger individuals and those from historically marginalized communities faced elevated risks of disengagement, reengagement, and viral rebound. The authors conclude that multistate longitudinal methods uncover treatment gaps obscured by routine cross-sectional reporting, and that HIV care programs should prioritize sustained long-term engagement rather than focusing narrowly on preventing isolated missed appointments.
items.citation: Ramakrishnan A, Vo D, Barrette EP et al.. A Multistate Analysis of Longitudinal Care Outcomes Among People Newly Linked to Human Immunodeficiency Virus Care in Missouri.. Open forum infectious diseases. 2026

items.title: Association Between Housing Instability and HIV Care Outcomes Among People With HIV in the United States.
items.summary: This study examined how housing instability affects HIV clinical outcomes among people with HIV who were already engaged in care across the United States. Using clinical data and patient-reported measures from a large multi-site cohort collected between 2019 and 2025, researchers applied relative risk and linear regression to assess associations between self-perceived housing status and outcomes including viral suppression, antiretroviral therapy use and adherence, and CD4 cell count. Nearly one in ten participants reported some form of housing instability, and both homelessness and unstable housing were significantly associated with lower rates of viral suppression, reduced antiretroviral therapy use, poorer adherence, and lower CD4 counts compared to stably housed individuals. These associations persisted after adjustment for demographic factors and were consistent across subgroups defined by substance use and depression status. The findings underscore that lack of stable housing represents a structural barrier to HIV management even among those engaged in care, with implications for efforts to end the HIV epidemic in the United States.
items.venue: Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999)
items.citation: Fahey CA, Whitney BM, Drumright LN et al.. Association Between Housing Instability and HIV Care Outcomes Among People With HIV in the United States.. Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999). 2026

items.title: Patterns of Workplace Absenteeism Across Levels of Virological Failure Among Employed Adults Co-Infected with HIV and Pulmonary Tuberculosis in the Govan Mbeki Sub-District, South Africa: A Retrospective Record Review.
items.summary: This study investigated whether the severity of virological failure is associated with workplace absenteeism among employed adults co-infected with HIV and pulmonary tuberculosis in a high-burden South African mining community. Using a retrospective record review, researchers linked clinical and laboratory data to workplace sick-leave registers for mine workers who had documented virological failure after at least six months of antiretroviral therapy, categorizing participants by viral load level and classifying absenteeism as high or low based on sick-leave days in the preceding three months. After adjusting for demographic and socioeconomic factors, viral load category was not independently associated with high absenteeism, and the overall regression model explained very little of the variance in absenteeism outcomes. Both high-level virological failure and elevated absenteeism were nonetheless common in this cohort, suggesting that the workplace burden of HIV/TB co-infection remains substantial regardless of viral load severity. The authors note that healthy-worker selection bias, limited exposure contrast, and residual confounding restrict causal conclusions, and they call for integrated public health and workplace interventions to improve treatment outcomes and workforce participation in high-burden settings.
items.citation: Mabunda T, Singh T. Patterns of Workplace Absenteeism Across Levels of Virological Failure Among Employed Adults Co-Infected with HIV and Pulmonary Tuberculosis in the Govan Mbeki Sub-District, South Africa: A Retrospective Record Review.. Healthcare (Basel, Switzerland). 2026

items.title: Comparative evaluation of a multi-antigen malaria rapid diagnostic test against qPCR and microscopy in a co-endemic area of Southern Ethiopia.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of a multi-antigen rapid diagnostic test for malaria in a region of southern Ethiopia where both *Plasmodium falciparum* and *Plasmodium vivax* co-circulate, a context where conventional HRP2-based tests are limited by low parasite densities and gene deletions affecting test targets. A cross-sectional study at health facilities enrolled febrile patients during peak transmission season, comparing the new Bioline Malaria multi-antigen RDT, which detects HRP2 and dual pLDH markers for both species, against expert microscopy and quantitative PCR as reference standards. Malaria prevalence varied by method, with qPCR detecting the highest proportion of infections overall, including submicroscopic cases missed by other approaches. The multi-antigen RDT showed high specificity and strong agreement with microscopy, but its sensitivity dropped notably when qPCR served as the reference, revealing that low-density infections were frequently overlooked. The authors conclude that while the RDT is clinically useful for routine diagnosis, more sensitive tools are needed for malaria surveillance and elimination efforts in endemic settings.
items.citation: Bogale A, Mitiku A, Tefera S et al.. Comparative evaluation of a multi-antigen malaria rapid diagnostic test against qPCR and microscopy in a co-endemic area of Southern Ethiopia.. Scientific reports. 2026
