items.title: Real‐world comprehensive care of people living with schizophrenia: recommendations across different settings and clinical stages
items.summary: This paper addressed the challenge of providing comprehensive, real-world care for people living with schizophrenia-spectrum psychoses across diverse clinical contexts and resource environments. The authors conducted a critical review of the scientific literature and assembled a collaborative group of clinical academics from multiple countries, including those in the Global South, as well as experts with lived experience, to develop consensus recommendations. The resulting guidelines cover a broad range of care domains, including early detection, pharmacological and psychological treatments, psychosocial interventions, community and inpatient care, peer support, and population-level prevention. A central overarching recommendation is to implement evidence-based, culturally sensitive, and resource-appropriate care models that utilize task-sharing with non-professional health workers and traditional healers to address disparities between high- and low-resource settings. The authors also highlight that future digital solutions may improve care efficiency, but emphasize that meaningful progress depends on strengthening mental health funding, improving access, and addressing the social determinants of health.
items.citation: Paolo Fusar‐Poli, Toby Pillinger, Robert Ali McCutcheon et al.. Real‐world comprehensive care of people living with schizophrenia: recommendations across different settings and clinical stages. World Psychiatry. 2026

items.title: The spatial proteome of the Plasmodium falciparum schizont illuminates the composition and evolutionary trajectories of its organelles
items.summary: This paper investigated the subcellular organization of proteins in the malaria parasite *Plasmodium falciparum*, focusing on the invasive schizont stage of its erythrocytic life cycle. The researchers applied a spatial proteomics approach called hyperLOPIT, combined with supervised machine learning, to map the subcellular locations of thousands of parasite proteins across dozens of distinct cellular compartments, including sites within the infected host red blood cell. The resulting high-resolution maps assigned locations to a large number of previously uncharacterized proteins, substantially expanding knowledge of organelle composition in this parasite. By integrating comparative genomic analyses with the spatial data, the study also traced evolutionary trajectories that have shaped organelle development across *Plasmodium* species and revealed adaptive pressures relevant to disease management. Overall, the work provides a foundational resource for understanding the biology of malaria parasites and the unique cellular machinery that enables them to colonize erythrocytes.
items.citation: Scott A. Chisholm, Victor Flores, Alison Kemp et al.. The spatial proteome of the Plasmodium falciparum schizont illuminates the composition and evolutionary trajectories of its organelles. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: Clinical profile and genomic characterization of the 2026 Bundibugyo virus index case in Uganda
items.summary: This paper describes the clinical course and genomic characterization of an index case of Bundibugyo virus disease identified in Uganda in 2026. The patient was a male traveler from the Democratic Republic of the Congo who presented with prolonged gastrointestinal symptoms followed by rapid multiorgan deterioration, including acute kidney injury, hepatic dysfunction, pulmonary edema, and cardiac complications, ultimately dying within days of hospital admission. Posthumous testing confirmed orthoebolavirus RNA, and reverse transcription quantitative PCR identified the pathogen as Bundibugyo virus, with genomic sequencing achieving near-complete genome coverage. Phylogenetic analysis revealed that the virus represented a distinct lineage diverging roughly equally from the previously documented strains responsible for outbreaks in 2007–2008 and 2012, indicating approximately one percent sequence divergence from those earlier variants. The authors use this case to highlight the importance of fatality surveillance, private-sector clinical reporting, and rapid molecular-genomic diagnostics in enabling early detection and public health response for high-consequence viral hemorrhagic fevers in cross-border settings.
items.citation: Andrew Nsawotebba, Isaac Ssewanyana, Alisen Ayitewala et al.. Clinical profile and genomic characterization of the 2026 Bundibugyo virus index case in Uganda. Nature Medicine. 2026

items.title: Malnutrition and double burden of disease: the African dilemma of non-communicable disease
items.summary: This review examined the double burden of malnutrition in Africa, characterized by the simultaneous presence of undernutrition and overnutrition and their relationship to non-communicable diseases. The authors conducted a narrative review of peer-reviewed literature, institutional datasets, and global health reports spanning a quarter century to synthesize evidence on prevalence, biological mechanisms, and socio-environmental drivers of this dual burden. They found that high rates of stunting, wasting, and underweight persist across sub-Saharan Africa, while overweight and obesity are rising rapidly, particularly in urban areas, with both conditions converging through biological pathways involving early-life deprivation, micronutrient deficiencies, and obesity-driven inflammation. Socioeconomic inequality, food insecurity, and rapid urbanization further amplify the risk of non-communicable diseases across affected populations. The review concludes that addressing this challenge requires coordinated, context-specific, and multisectoral strategies—including community nutrition programs, food fortification, fiscal policies, and integration of nutrition and disease prevention across health, agriculture, and social protection systems.
items.citation: Daniel Omeodisemi Omokpariola, Cecilia Agbanu-Kumordzi, Gloria Omoefe et al.. Malnutrition and double burden of disease: the African dilemma of non-communicable disease. Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems. 2026

items.title: Energy constraint on human health
items.summary: This paper proposes a theoretical framework arguing that human health and disease are fundamentally shaped by evolved constraints on energy transformation within the body. The authors build on life history theory and cellular biology to contend that finite internal energy resources must be continuously reallocated among competing biological demands. They organize these demands into three categories — vital functions, stress responses, and growth, maintenance, and repair — and argue that these operate within a hierarchy in which more urgent vital and stress-related processes take priority, suppressing longevity-promoting maintenance and repair. The framework predicts that chronic prioritization of urgent energy demands at the expense of growth, maintenance, and repair underlies health deterioration and disease across the lifespan. The authors present this energy constraint model as a unifying conceptual tool for understanding health and disease dynamics from the level of organelles to the whole organism.
items.citation: Alexander Behnke, Evan D. Shaulson, Herman Pontzer et al.. Energy constraint on human health. Trends in Endocrinology and Metabolism. 2026

items.title: Flashing with colours: Photometric indicators of an early interaction in type II supernovae
items.summary: This paper investigated early-time photometric and spectroscopic properties of Type II supernovae to determine whether circumstellar material interaction, identified through "flash spectroscopy" features, leaves detectable signatures in photometry alone. The researchers assembled a large sample of Type II supernovae combining new observations from the POISE collaboration with published events, obtaining high-cadence, high-precision multi-band light curves and spectra taken within days of explosion. Supernovae were classified based on the presence or absence of transient narrow emission lines from highly ionised elements in early spectra, and their photometric properties were then compared between these two groups. Flash supernovae were found to be more luminous at peak, tend toward longer rise times in the blue band, and are systematically bluer than non-flash events at roughly three weeks post-explosion. Crucially, the study demonstrates that colour-curve breaks occurring within the first month after explosion, combined with peak absolute magnitude, provide a strong photometric diagnostic capable of identifying circumstellar material interaction even without early spectroscopic observations.
items.citation: A. Mendez-Llorca, G. Folatelli, C. P. Gutierrez et al.. Flashing with colours: Photometric indicators of an early interaction in type II supernovae. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Entering the Era of Circumplanetary Ring Detection with Direct Imaging
items.summary: This paper investigates how circumplanetary rings around exoplanets would affect reflected light observations from upcoming direct imaging missions. The researchers developed a hybrid forward model combining ray casting to compute planet-ring shadowing with empirical reflectance spectra derived from Cassini observations of Saturn's rings, applied to Jupiter-like planets hosting rings of varying size, inclination, and obliquity. Their simulations demonstrate that rings can substantially enhance the planet-to-star flux ratio at favorable geometries, with Saturn-equivalent rings boosting peak flux noticeably and more extended rings producing even greater contrast enhancements, while at certain geometries rings can actually suppress total system brightness below that of a ringless planet. The flux contribution of rings is shown to be highly sensitive to orbital geometry and obliquity, and multi-band photometry is proposed as a complementary diagnostic for detecting exorings. The authors conclude that unaccounted-for rings could bias inferred planetary properties from direct imaging data and must be considered in the planning and interpretation of observations with instruments such as the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope Coronagraph.
items.citation: Samantha N. Hasler, Alexandra Z. Greenbaum, Geoffrey Bryden et al.. Entering the Era of Circumplanetary Ring Detection with Direct Imaging. arXiv. 2026

items.title: AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery
items.summary: This paper investigated whether large language model agents can automate the reproduction and robustness evaluation of scientific findings, addressing the high cost of manual replication efforts. The researchers constructed a benchmark of published studies based on a major U.S. cancer registry database, pairing each paper with the data and resources needed to reproduce its results. An AI agent was developed and tested on this benchmark, successfully reproducing a substantial majority of atomic claims extracted from the papers while generating executable code as a baseline for further analysis. Beyond reproduction, the researchers built an agentic pipeline to probe analytical robustness by identifying key methodological choices embedded in each finding, proposing defensible alternatives, and re-running analyses to assess whether different choices would alter the conclusions. The pipeline flagged a notable fraction of fully reproduced findings as potentially sensitive to analytical choices, demonstrating that LLM agents can meaningfully support scientific review by automating reproduction, systematically testing robustness, and directing expert scrutiny toward consequential methodological decisions.
items.citation: Shicheng Liu, Krista Opsahl-Ong, Andrew Drozdov et al.. AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Demonstration of Logical Error Suppression in a Surface Code Memory on a Cloud-Accessible IBM Superconducting Processor
items.summary: This paper investigates quantum error correction using rotated surface-code memory implemented on a cloud-accessible superconducting processor, aiming to demonstrate that logical error rates can be suppressed by increasing code distance. The researchers systematically optimized the syndrome extraction circuit by combining short readout, fused measurement and reset, and an echo pulse on data qubits during ancilla readout, then benchmarked performance across different placements on the processor and over many rounds of error correction. The optimizations substantially reduced per-round logical error rates compared to a standard baseline, with the improvement being more pronounced in one measurement basis than the other due to noise asymmetry. Scaling from a smaller to a larger protected code distance achieved meaningful error suppression, yielding error-suppression factors above unity under maximum-likelihood decoding, though long-lived temporal correlations weakened the distance advantage at extended circuit depths. The authors conclude that careful circuit compilation and hardware-aware optimization are essential for realizing surface-code memory on current devices, and advocate for co-design of quantum processors and error-correction circuits to advance fault-tolerant quantum computing.
items.citation: Shuwen Kan, Aaron Hoyt, Sean Garner et al.. Demonstration of Logical Error Suppression in a Surface Code Memory on a Cloud-Accessible IBM Superconducting Processor. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Leveraging verifiable structure in quantum circuits to find more efficient compilations with agentic AI
items.summary: This paper explores a framework for using AI agents to improve the compilation of quantum circuits by exploiting classically verifiable structure in critical subroutines. When bottleneck subroutines consist of reversible classical logic, phasing operations, and measurement-based uncomputation, their correctness can be efficiently certified for classical inputs through a form of fuzz testing, enabling practical approximate circuit synthesis. The authors apply this paradigm to three distinct problems: computing an inverse square root relevant to simulating the Coulomb operator in inertial confinement fusion modeling, decoding Reed-Solomon codes that bottleneck a quantum interferometry algorithm for polynomial intersection, and optimizing quantum look-up tables and controlled Givens rotations central to quantum chemistry simulation in second quantization. Reference implementations of these algorithms are provided alongside a framework for constraining and verifying them, intended to seed a Kaggle competition aimed at accelerating AI-driven quantum circuit optimization research. The work thus generalizes a strategy previously applied to quantum cryptanalysis into a broader and flexible compilation paradigm with multiple high-value applications.
items.citation: Tanuj Khattar, Nicholas C. Rubin, Craig Gidney et al.. Leveraging verifiable structure in quantum circuits to find more efficient compilations with agentic AI. arXiv. 2026

items.title: ENFR: Evidence Networks with Flow-Matched References for Amortized Simulation-Based Model Inference
items.summary: The paper addresses the challenge of computing the Bayesian evidence, a quantity central to model comparison, goodness-of-fit testing, and detection of model misspecification, which remains notoriously difficult to estimate even when likelihoods are tractable. The authors propose ENFR (Evidence Networks with Flow-matched References), a method that builds on an existing Evidence Network framework by first learning Bayes factors relative to a flow-matched reference distribution, then recovering absolute evidence values from these ratios in an amortized fashion. They additionally introduce and formally prove an architecture capable of jointly learning the individual evidences of multiple competing models simultaneously. Benchmarks across several scientific applications show that ENFR outperforms flow-based baselines in evidence estimation and achieves the best performance among all density estimation methods evaluated. The work also frames the absolute evidence as a natural test statistic for minimum-volume hypothesis tests, providing a principled tool for assessing model fidelity in simulation-based inference pipelines.
items.citation: Kai Lehman, Jameson Dong, Carolina Cuesta-Lazaro et al.. ENFR: Evidence Networks with Flow-Matched References for Amortized Simulation-Based Model Inference. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Pulmonary Tuberculosis Detection with MiniDock MTB Using Swab Samples
items.summary: This prospective, cross-sectional study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy and usability of MiniDock MTB, a novel test designed to detect pulmonary tuberculosis at or near the point of care, across outpatient centers in seven countries spanning Africa and Asia. Participants aged twelve and older with presumptive pulmonary tuberculosis were tested using both sputum swabs and tongue swabs, with results benchmarked against sputum culture as the reference standard and compared to smear microscopy and the Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra assay. MiniDock MTB achieved sensitivity and specificity meeting World Health Organization targets for near-point-of-care tuberculosis diagnostics for both sample types, with sputum swab performance closely matching that of Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra and substantially outperforming smear microscopy for both sputum and tongue swabs. Usability assessments indicated the test was well received by operators, with scores classified as good usability and no adverse events attributable to the test. The authors conclude that MiniDock MTB represents a promising diagnostic tool suitable for deployment in peripheral health settings where improved tuberculosis case detection is urgently needed.
items.citation: Seda Yerlikaya, Masuzyo Chirwa, Bukola Ajide et al.. Pulmonary Tuberculosis Detection with MiniDock MTB Using Swab Samples. New England Journal of Medicine. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic performance and testing costs of pooled testing for molecular detection of tuberculosis in seven countries: a prospective, observational, diagnostic accuracy study.
items.summary: This study evaluated whether pooling multiple sputum specimens together for a single molecular test could serve as a cost-effective strategy for tuberculosis diagnosis in resource-limited settings. Conducted prospectively across seven countries spanning multiple continents, the research enrolled individuals with presumptive tuberculosis through both facility-based and community-based case finding, testing sputum in pools of two, three, or four specimens using Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra and comparing results against individual testing and culture as a reference standard. Pooled testing demonstrated slightly higher specificity than individual testing but modestly lower sensitivity, with agreement between pooled and individual results remaining high for specimens with medium to high bacterial loads but dropping notably for very low and trace detection grades. Critically, pooled testing required approximately half the number of diagnostic cartridges compared to testing each specimen individually, representing a substantial reduction in consumable costs. The authors conclude that this approach could meaningfully expand access to WHO-recommended molecular tuberculosis diagnostics in low to moderate prevalence settings without requiring additional laboratory infrastructure.
items.citation: Garg T, Sander M, Byrne RL et al.. Diagnostic performance and testing costs of pooled testing for molecular detection of tuberculosis in seven countries: a prospective, observational, diagnostic accuracy study.. The Lancet. Global health. 2027

items.title: Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.
items.summary: This paper reviews advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarker research over a five-year period, synthesizing evidence that has informed updated WHO policy guidance consolidating recommendations for detecting tuberculosis disease and drug resistance. Digital chest radiography supported by computer-aided detection has become a core screening and triage tool, while decentralised molecular diagnosis has expanded through multiple classes of nucleic acid amplification tests, including near point-of-care platforms and novel specimen types such as tongue swabs and pooled sputum. Molecular drug-resistance testing has progressed with newer rapid assays, and targeted next-generation sequencing is now endorsed for comprehensive drug-susceptibility testing at reference laboratory level, while urine lipoarabinomannan assays improve diagnostic yield in people with HIV but remain limited in broader application. Host blood transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic biomarkers show promise for prognosis and triage but none yet meet WHO target product profile criteria for a point-of-care test capable of reliably distinguishing infection from disease, including subclinical tuberculosis. The review concludes that substantial gaps in performance, implementation, and equity persist and identifies developmental priorities for closing them.
items.citation: Walzl G, McHugh TD, Chakaya J et al.. Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.. The Lancet. Microbe. 2027

items.title: The changing landscape of diagnosing HIV-associated tuberculosis.
items.summary: This narrative review examines how the diagnosis of HIV-associated tuberculosis has evolved from 1990 to the present, with a focus on the particular challenges posed by this co-infection. People with HIV present diagnostic difficulties because they tend to have lower bacillary loads in sputum, a higher proportion of extrapulmonary or disseminated disease, and nonspecific clinical features that overlap with other opportunistic infections, while disease progression is rapid in those with advanced immunosuppression. The review traces how reliance on smear microscopy—the sole rapid test available until 2011—resulted in both underdiagnosis and overdiagnosis due to its reduced sensitivity in this population, and how subsequent development of nucleic acid amplification tests and the urine lipoarabinomannan lateral flow assay, alongside the rollout of antiretroviral therapy, substantially reduced tuberculosis incidence and mortality. Despite these advances, no currently available rapid diagnostic test achieves ideal sensitivity, and only urine lipoarabinomannan detection combines affordability with point-of-care simplicity. The authors conclude that further development of accurate, affordable, and easy-to-deploy point-of-care diagnostics remains an urgent priority.
items.venue: South African medical journal = Suid-Afrikaanse tydskrif vir geneeskunde
items.citation: Maartens G. The changing landscape of diagnosing HIV-associated tuberculosis.. South African medical journal = Suid-Afrikaanse tydskrif vir geneeskunde. 2026

items.title: Development and validation of a blood-based diagnostic model for pulmonary tuberculosis combining GBP5 expression and routine laboratory indicators.
items.summary: This study addressed the challenge of diagnosing pulmonary tuberculosis rapidly and accurately without relying on sputum-based methods, given that conventional laboratory approaches suffer from poor sensitivity despite high specificity. Using a retrospective case-control design, the researchers enrolled patients with active tuberculosis and those with other pulmonary diseases, collecting data on GBP5 gene expression alongside routine blood laboratory indicators including white blood cell count, platelet count, and prothrombin time. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression identified these four variables as key predictors, which were then integrated into a diagnostic model constructed using the AdaBoost machine learning algorithm. The resulting model outperformed traditional diagnostic methods such as smear microscopy, mycobacterial culture, Xpert MTB/RIF, and IGRA in terms of area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, achieving consistent performance across both training and test sets. The authors conclude that this blood-based AdaBoost model shows promise as a rapid clinical diagnostic tool for active tuberculosis, though they acknowledge that validation in larger patient cohorts is necessary before clinical implementation.
items.citation: Zhao M, Hu Q, Wang Q et al.. Development and validation of a blood-based diagnostic model for pulmonary tuberculosis combining GBP5 expression and routine laboratory indicators.. Medicine. 2026

items.title: Near-point-of-care Diagnosis of Tuberculosis With LyocartE MTB Assay: a Multicenter Diagnostic Accuracy Study.
items.summary: The study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of the LyocartE assay, a near-point-of-care molecular test for tuberculosis, using both sputum and tongue swab specimens. In a multicenter prospective study conducted across three sites, consecutive individuals with presumptive tuberculosis were enrolled and tested with LyocartE alongside established comparators including Xpert Ultra, smear microscopy, and culture. When applied to sputum, LyocartE demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity against a composite microbiological reference standard, performing comparably to Xpert Ultra, while tongue swab testing also showed strong specificity with somewhat lower sensitivity. Diagnostic accuracy remained consistent across different specimen types, clinical presentations, and comorbidities, and LyocartE cycle threshold values correlated strongly with those from Xpert Ultra. The authors conclude that LyocartE offers rapid and accurate tuberculosis detection from non-invasive specimens, though further evaluation in asymptomatic and paucibacillary populations is needed.
items.venue: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
items.citation: Ma Z, Yu X, Yu Y et al.. Near-point-of-care Diagnosis of Tuberculosis With LyocartE MTB Assay: a Multicenter Diagnostic Accuracy Study.. Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America. 2026

items.title: Efficient differential expression analysis of large-scale single-cell transcriptomics data using Dreamlet
items.summary: The paper addresses the challenge of performing differential expression analysis on large-scale single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomics datasets spanning hundreds of subjects and millions of cells, which poses both statistical and computational difficulties. The authors developed an open-source R package called dreamlet that employs a pseudobulk approach based on precision-weighted linear mixed models to identify differentially expressed genes across cell clusters while accommodating complex study designs. The tool was designed specifically for large cohort data, achieving substantially faster runtimes and reduced memory usage compared to existing workflows while maintaining control of the false positive rate. Performance was benchmarked on previously published datasets and validated on a novel large-scale dataset of over a million single nuclei derived from postmortem brain tissue of Alzheimer's disease cases and matched controls. The authors claim dreamlet provides an efficient and statistically rigorous solution for differential expression analysis in large-scale single-cell transcriptomic studies of human disease.
items.citation: Gabriel E. Hoffman, Donghoon Lee, Jaroslav M. Bendl et al.. Efficient differential expression analysis of large-scale single-cell transcriptomics data using Dreamlet. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression
items.summary: This systematic review examined how different forms of exercise affect the expression of Toll-like receptors, a family of immune cell receptors that trigger inflammatory signalling and have been implicated in the chronic low-grade inflammation associated with sedentary lifestyles and non-communicable diseases. The authors searched multiple databases and included studies in which exercise was an isolated intervention in human participants, categorising findings by exercise type and duration across acute and chronic modalities. Acute resistance exercise tended to upregulate TLR expression, whereas acute aerobic exercise generally produced neutral or downregulatory responses, particularly in healthy individuals. Chronic resistance and combined training programmes were predominantly associated with unchanged or decreased TLR levels, while chronic aerobic training produced more mixed results with most measurements showing no change. The authors conclude that evidence supports an interaction between exercise and TLR signalling that depends on exercise characteristics, but highlight substantial heterogeneity across study designs and call for further research to clarify the underlying mechanisms and pathophysiological implications.
items.citation: Kasper Favere, Matthias Bosman, Peter Delputte et al.. A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Flashing with colours: Photometric indicators of an early interaction in type II supernovae
items.summary: This paper studied early-time photometric and spectroscopic properties of Type II supernovae to investigate signatures of interaction with circumstellar material. The researchers assembled a large sample of supernovae, combining newly observed events with published ones, and used near-daily cadence optical photometry alongside spectra taken within days of explosion to classify events based on the presence or absence of transient narrow emission features called "flash features," which indicate interaction with dense circumstellar material. They found that supernovae showing flash features tend to be more luminous at peak, exhibit longer rise times in the blue band, and are systematically bluer than non-flash events, with distinct colour distributions emerging within the first few weeks after explosion. Notably, breaks in the colour curves occurring within about a month of explosion provided a clear separation between flash and non-flash supernovae, and combining the slope change across these breaks with peak absolute magnitude yielded a strong diagnostic of circumstellar interaction. The study concludes that photometric observations alone may be sufficient to identify supernovae undergoing dense circumstellar material interaction, even without early spectroscopic follow-up.
items.citation: A. Mendez-Llorca, G. Folatelli, C. P. Gutierrez et al.. Flashing with colours: Photometric indicators of an early interaction in type II supernovae. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Entering the Era of Circumplanetary Ring Detection with Direct Imaging
items.summary: This paper investigates how circumplanetary rings around exoplanets would affect reflected light observations from upcoming direct imaging missions, particularly the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. The authors developed a hybrid forward model combining ray casting to handle mutual planet-ring shadowing with empirical reflectance spectra derived from Cassini observations of Saturn's rings, simulating Jupiter-like planets with icy rings of varying sizes, inclinations, and obliquities. They found that rings can substantially enhance planetary flux ratios at favorable geometries, with Saturn-equivalent rings boosting peak flux in the visible by a factor of several, while more extended rings produce even larger contrast enhancements, though at certain geometries rings can actually suppress total system brightness below that of a ringless planet. Multi-band observations are highlighted as a useful diagnostic for identifying exorings, and the model is applied to an actual directly imaged planet candidate as a test case. The study concludes that unaccounted-for rings could bias inferred planetary properties from direct imaging data, underscoring the need to incorporate ring effects into observation planning and interpretation.

items.title: AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery
items.summary: This paper investigated whether large language model agents can automate the reproduction of published scientific findings and assess their analytical robustness, addressing the high cost of manual replication efforts. The researchers developed a benchmark called SEER-Repro comprising published studies based on a major U.S. cancer registry, along with the data and resources needed to reproduce their results. An AI agent was then built to reproduce granular claims from these papers and to systematically test robustness by identifying underlying analytical choices, proposing defensible alternatives, and re-executing analyses to determine whether different choices altered the conclusions. The agent successfully reproduced the majority of atomic claims evaluated and identified potentially consequential analytical choices in a meaningful fraction of fully reproduced findings, flagging these for expert review. The authors conclude that LLM agents can meaningfully support scientific peer review by automating reproduction, stress-testing analytical decisions, and directing human expert attention to the findings most warranting scrutiny.
items.citation: Shicheng Liu, Krista Opsahl-Ong, Andrew Drozdov et al.. AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Demonstration of Logical Error Suppression in a Surface Code Memory on a Cloud-Accessible IBM Superconducting Processor
items.summary: This paper investigates quantum error correction using rotated surface-code memory implemented on a cloud-accessible superconducting processor, aiming to demonstrate logical error suppression as code distance increases. The researchers optimized the syndrome extraction circuit by combining short readout, fused measurement and reset, and an echo pulse on data qubits during ancilla readout, then benchmarked performance across multiple processor placements and up to many rounds of memory operation. The optimized circuit substantially reduced per-round logical error rates compared to standard readout, and increasing code distance produced clear error suppression with factors approaching two under maximum-likelihood decoding. However, the distance advantage weakened over longer experiments, accompanied by long-lived temporal correlations that suggest a persistent error component not fully captured by standard noise models. The work highlights how circuit compilation choices directly shape surface-code performance and motivates joint codesign of quantum processors and error correction circuits for fault-tolerant computing on current cloud hardware.

items.title: Leveraging verifiable structure in quantum circuits to find more efficient compilations with agentic AI

The key insight is that when critical circuit components consist of reversible classical logic, phasing operations, and measurement-based uncomputation, their correctness can be efficiently checked using classical simulation on sampled inputs, enabling a fuzz-testing approach to certify approximate circuit synthesis. Building on prior work in quantum cryptanalysis, the authors extend this paradigm to three new application domains: computing the inverse square root function relevant to Coulomb operator simulations for inertial confinement fusion modeling, decoding Reed-Solomon codes relevant to a quantum interferometry algorithm for polynomial intersection, and optimizing quantum look-up tables and Givens rotation circuits relevant to quantum chemistry simulation in second quantization. The authors describe reference implementations of these algorithms and propose a framework, including a Kaggle competition, intended to accelerate AI-driven research into quantum circuit optimization.
items.citation: Tanuj Khattar, Nicholas C. Rubin, Craig Gidney et al.. Leveraging verifiable structure in quantum circuits to find more efficient compilations with agentic AI. arXiv. 2026

items.title: ENFR: Evidence Networks with Flow-Matched References for Amortized Simulation-Based Model Inference
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of computing the Bayesian evidence, a quantity central to model comparison, goodness-of-fit testing, and detection of model misspecification, which is notoriously difficult to estimate even when the likelihood is tractable. The authors propose ENFR (Evidence Networks with Flow-Matched References), a method that combines evidence networks with flow-based generative models to obtain accurate, amortized estimates of the absolute evidence rather than only evidence ratios as in existing approaches. The method works by learning Bayes factors relative to a flow-matched reference distribution, from which the absolute evidence is then recovered, and the authors additionally introduce and prove an architecture capable of jointly learning the individual evidences of multiple models simultaneously. Across a range of scientific benchmark applications, ENFR outperforms flow-based baselines in evidence estimation and achieves the best performance among all density estimation methods evaluated. The absolute evidence estimates produced by the method enable minimum-volume hypothesis tests for model misspecification, which the authors argue are essential for validating simulation-based inference pipelines.
items.citation: Kai Lehman, Jameson Dong, Carolina Cuesta-Lazaro et al.. ENFR: Evidence Networks with Flow-Matched References for Amortized Simulation-Based Model Inference. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Current Data to Inform Point-of-Care Testing for Sexually Transmitted Infections in United States Healthcare Settings: A Narrative Review.
items.summary: This narrative review examined the current evidence base for point-of-care testing for sexually transmitted infections, including gonorrhea, chlamydia, trichomoniasis, and syphilis, across multiple United States healthcare settings. The authors reviewed literature from emergency departments, sexual health clinics, primary care and gynecology clinics, and urgent care centers, drawing on studies from other high-income countries where domestic data were limited, and stratified findings by clinical setting, patient priority group, and sex. They found some evidence for improved clinical outcomes, particularly among symptomatic women in emergency departments, but noted that most studies did not stratify results by priority population and predominantly evaluated longer-turnaround tests that often returned results after the patient had already left the visit. The review concludes that the evidence base remains insufficient to support widespread adoption and reimbursement decisions, with notable gaps around faster tests, workflow strategies to ensure results are actionable within the clinical encounter, and updated cost-effectiveness analyses specific to the United States context.
items.citation: Otsyina BE, Lorenz ZW, Widdice LE et al.. Current Data to Inform Point-of-Care Testing for Sexually Transmitted Infections in United States Healthcare Settings: A Narrative Review.. Sexually transmitted diseases. 2026

items.title: Interventions to Improve Care for Bacterial Sexually Transmitted Infections in Emergency Departments: A Narrative Review.
items.summary: This narrative review examined interventions designed to improve the diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up of bacterial sexually transmitted infections—specifically chlamydia, gonorrhea, and syphilis—within United States emergency department settings, which serve as critical access points for patients with limited routine sexual health care. The authors searched the published literature spanning several decades and identified studies meeting inclusion criteria for analysis. They found that universal screening substantially increased testing and case detection, electronic health record prompts enhanced screening uptake, and point-of-care testing improved same-day diagnosis and treatment while reducing unnecessary antibiotic prescribing. Patient-directed tools yielded more modest gains, whereas bundled interventions targeting multiple steps along the care pathway appeared to produce the greatest overall impact, though heterogeneity among interventions complicated direct comparisons. The authors conclude that future research should prioritize evaluating the implementation feasibility, sustainability, health equity implications, and cost-effectiveness of such interventions across diverse emergency department contexts.
items.citation: Andonian KS, Giri H, Goodman GR et al.. Interventions to Improve Care for Bacterial Sexually Transmitted Infections in Emergency Departments: A Narrative Review.. Sexually transmitted diseases. 2026

items.title: Community peer-led STI/HIV point-of-care testing and knowledge, attitude and practice (KAP) survey in men who have sex with men (MSM) attending an NGO-led clinic in the outskirts of Beirut (Lebanon).
items.summary: This pilot study examined the utility of point-of-care testing for HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis among men who have sex with men attending an NGO-led clinic in Beirut, Lebanon, alongside an assessment of their sexual health knowledge, attitudes, and practices. A cross-sectional design was used over four months, in which participants underwent STI and HIV testing and completed an anonymous questionnaire covering demographics, STI awareness, condom use, chemsex, sexual violence, and perceived stigma. The cohort was predominantly young, educated Lebanese and Syrian men, among whom a notable proportion were living with HIV, and high levels of STI awareness paradoxically coexisted with condomless sex and recreational drug use. HIV-related stigma and perceived community beliefs were identified as significant barriers to seeking testing. The authors conclude that integrating point-of-care testing into sexual health services enables same-day diagnosis, counselling, and linkage to care, making it a valuable tool for reaching this population.
items.citation: Abou Shahla W, Rossoni I, Padovese V. Community peer-led STI/HIV point-of-care testing and knowledge, attitude and practice (KAP) survey in men who have sex with men (MSM) attending an NGO-led clinic in the outskirts of Beirut (Lebanon).. Sexually transmitted infections. 2026

items.title: Flatline constructs : Gothic materialism and cybernetic theory-fiction
items.summary: This thesis examines the claim that cyberpunk fiction represents the supreme literary expression of postmodernism or late capitalism, subjecting that claim to sustained theoretical scrutiny by rethinking cyberpunk through three interlocking frameworks: cybernetics, the Gothic, and fiction. The author argues that postmodernism has been deeply preoccupied with cybernetic themes while cybernetics itself has been haunted by Gothic concerns, and that this convergence demands a materialist reconception of the Gothic drawn from Deleuze and Guattari's reading of Worringer rather than from conventional literary history. Central to this materialist Gothic is the theme of a nonorganic continuum and the breakdown of boundaries between the animate and the inanimate, which the thesis traces through key cyberpunk texts including Blade Runner, Videodrome, Neuromancer, and The Atrocity Exhibition. The thesis organizes its argument around the concept of the "flatline," derived from Gibson, which names both a state of undeath or unlife and a condition of radical immanence, and which is shown to be the point where Gothic and cybernetic concerns converge in what the author calls "imploded science fiction." Engaging with Baudrillard's suggestion that the era of cybernetic simulation dissolves the distinction between theory and fiction as separate genres, the thesis is structured around four aspects of the flatline: the flatlining of cybernetics and postmodernism, of the body, of reproduction, and of fiction itself within hyperreality.
items.venue: Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick)
items.citation: Mark Fisher. Flatline constructs : Gothic materialism and cybernetic theory-fiction. Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick). 2026

items.title: The many behind the few : the lives and emotions of Erks and WAAFs of RAF bomber command 1939-1945
items.summary: This thesis examines the lives and emotional experiences of the ground personnel — both men and women — who served in RAF Bomber Command during the Second World War, a group constituting the large majority of the service yet largely neglected in favour of histories focused on aircrew or bombing strategy. The research explores how a gendered hierarchy of trades was constructed within Bomber Command through interlocking discourses of class, gender, fear, heroism, and stoicism, as well as through specific features of RAF culture such as trade selection, pay, dialect, and perceived contribution to the command's mission. This hierarchy shaped experiences profoundly, with some personnel overburdened while others felt unable to contribute meaningfully, and it challenged the reductive stereotypes — the male "Erk" and the sexually promiscuous WAAF "chop girl" — through which ground personnel have typically been portrayed. The thesis also investigates emotional responses to serving in a community exposed to high aircrew losses, as well as the RAF medical services' treatment of those who suffered psychological breakdowns. By centring non-combatant personnel who occupied a liminal space between operational station and home front, the work contributes to the histories of the RAF, emotions, military medicine and psychiatry, and broader understandings of wartime work and citizenship.
items.venue: Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick)
items.citation: Dan Ellin. The many behind the few : the lives and emotions of Erks and WAAFs of RAF bomber command 1939-1945. Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick). 2026

items.title: APASL clinical practice guidelines on the management of chronic hepatitis B infection: a 2026 update
items.summary: These clinical practice guidelines address the ongoing and escalating burden of chronic hepatitis B infection in the Asia Pacific region, where the disease continues to cause significant morbidity and mortality through complications such as acute-on-chronic liver failure, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma. The Asia Pacific Association for the Study of the Liver assembled a Viral Elimination Taskforce comprising key opinion leaders from member countries to develop updated guidance, incorporating shifts in disease epidemiology, socioeconomic factors, and technological advancements. The resulting guidelines provide recommendations spanning thirteen major areas encompassing screening, vaccination, antiviral treatment, and hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance. The document is intended to support healthcare professionals, policymakers, and patients in making practical and cost-effective management decisions, with the overarching goal of reducing the disease burden attributable to chronic hepatitis B across the Asia Pacific region.
items.citation: Hong You, Rakhi Maiwall, Jing Chen et al.. APASL clinical practice guidelines on the management of chronic hepatitis B infection: a 2026 update. Hepatology International. 2026

items.title: Girls, gifts, and gender : an ethnography of the materiality of care in rural Mpumalanga, South Africa
items.summary: This ethnographic thesis examines how care for young people—both orphaned and non-orphaned—is organized, negotiated, and experienced in a rural South African community heavily affected by HIV/AIDS and economic inequality. Drawing on extended fieldwork with non-profit organizations serving orphans and vulnerable children, households, local government workers, faith-based leaders, and tourist-philanthropists, the study analyzes three interlocking gift-exchange relationships: children's labor exchanged for guardian care, girls' labor and sexual compliance exchanged for material support from men, and the local construction of "orphan" identities to attract charitable giving from visiting tourists. The research develops the concept of the "materiality of care" to theorize how Western and local understandings of childhood, orphanhood, and care interact on the ground when aid interventions arrive. The findings argue that care for young people must be understood within local cultural frameworks and within the broader political-economic and historical conditions that poverty and AIDS create across all children's lives, not just those formally classified as orphans. The thesis ultimately contributes to a critical body of scholarship challenging orphan-targeted interventions in sub-Saharan Africa for failing to account for the familial context of parentless children and the shared vulnerabilities of orphaned and non-orphaned youth alike.
items.venue: Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick)
items.citation: Annalise Weckesser. Girls, gifts, and gender : an ethnography of the materiality of care in rural Mpumalanga, South Africa. Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick). 2026

items.title: Moment closure approximations in epidemiology
items.summary: This thesis investigates moment closure approximations (MCAs) as deterministic methods for capturing spatial correlations in epidemiological models, going beyond traditional mean-field approaches that cannot account for local population structure. The work extends existing MCA techniques, which were largely developed for static regular lattices, to dynamic network models and continuous space models, thereby broadening their applicability in epidemiology and ecology. The research examines the accuracy of these approximations near critical points and during transient phases, and applies pair approximations to models of sexually transmitted diseases as well as to a continuous space epidemic model. By comparing processes on regular lattices with those on dynamic networks and in continuous space, the thesis explores how spatial structure and network dynamics influence epidemic behaviour. The overall conclusion is that MCAs remain a productive research framework and that extending them beyond static regular lattices yields meaningful insights into population-level disease dynamics.
items.venue: Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick)
items.citation: Christopher Thomas Bauch. Moment closure approximations in epidemiology. Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick). 2026

items.title: Hydrogels: current biomedical applications and future directions
items.summary: This review paper examines hydrogels as multifunctional biomedical materials, focusing on their design principles and expanding therapeutic applications. The authors systematically survey advances in polymer chemistry, crosslinking strategies, stimuli-responsive design, and fabrication technologies that have transformed hydrogels from simple soft materials into sophisticated biomedical systems. The review covers their current use across drug delivery, tissue engineering, biosensing, and organoid platforms, as well as their application in treating a wide range of diseases including wound healing, musculoskeletal injuries, cancer, neurological and cardiovascular diseases, autoimmune disorders, and reproductive system conditions. The authors argue that hydrogels are particularly well suited to overcome limitations of conventional therapies, such as poor targeting efficiency, narrow therapeutic windows, and inability to restore damaged tissue. The paper concludes by discussing prospects for clinical translation and offering perspectives intended to guide future development of hydrogel-based treatments.
items.citation: Haoming Wu, Guanghao Piao, Qiuqi Chen et al.. Hydrogels: current biomedical applications and future directions. Molecular Biomedicine. 2026

items.title: Flashing with colours: Photometric indicators of an early interaction in type II supernovae
items.summary: This paper investigated early-time photometric and spectroscopic properties of Type II supernovae to identify signatures of interaction with dense circumstellar material. The researchers compiled a large sample of supernovae, combining newly observed events from the POISE collaboration with previously published objects, obtaining high-cadence, high-precision optical photometry and classifying events based on whether their early spectra showed narrow emission lines from highly ionised elements, known as flash features. Flash supernovae were found to be more luminous at peak, tend to exhibit longer rise times in the blue band, and are systematically bluer than non-flash events, with these colour differences most pronounced around three weeks after explosion. A particularly notable finding is that breaks in colour curves within the first month post-explosion, combined with peak absolute magnitude, provide a strong diagnostic capable of distinguishing flash from non-flash supernovae. This suggests that photometric observations alone, without early spectroscopy, may be sufficient to identify supernovae undergoing circumstellar interaction.
items.citation: A. Mendez-Llorca, G. Folatelli, C. P. Gutierrez et al.. Flashing with colours: Photometric indicators of an early interaction in type II supernovae. arXiv. 2026

items.title: ENFR: Evidence Networks with Flow-Matched References for Amortized Simulation-Based Model Inference
items.summary: The paper addresses the problem of computing the Bayesian evidence — the marginal likelihood of observed data under a model — which is critical for model comparison, goodness-of-fit testing, and detecting model misspecification, yet is notoriously difficult to estimate. The authors propose ENFR (Evidence Networks with Flow-matched References), a method that learns Bayes factors relative to a flow-matched reference distribution and then recovers the absolute evidence through amortized neural inference, building on an existing Evidence Network framework. A key theoretical contribution is a novel architecture with a formal proof that enables joint learning of the individual evidences for a set of competing models simultaneously. The method is shown to outperform flow-based baselines and other density estimation approaches across a range of benchmark tasks drawn from diverse scientific applications. By providing fast, accurate, and amortized estimates of absolute evidence rather than mere evidence ratios, ENFR enables practical minimum-volume goodness-of-fit tests that are essential for validating the simulation models used in simulation-based parameter inference.

items.title: Clinical utility of nucleic acid amplification testing for detection of sexually transmitted infections in women with symptomatic bacterial vaginosis and vulvovaginal candidiasis identified by conventional versus molecular diagnoses.
items.summary: This study examined whether using molecular (NAAT-based) methods to diagnose bacterial vaginosis and vulvovaginal candidiasis improves the detection of co-occurring sexually transmitted infections compared to conventional laboratory or clinician-based vaginitis diagnosis. The researchers analyzed STI NAAT results for four pathogens across a large cohort of women with symptomatic vaginitis, comparing STI detection rates according to whether vaginitis was identified by healthcare provider clinical assessment, conventional laboratory methods, or molecular vaginitis testing. Women whose bacterial vaginosis was confirmed by NAAT had significantly higher rates of STI co-detection and a substantially elevated relative risk for any STI compared to those diagnosed by conventional methods, while a similar trend was observed for vulvovaginal candidiasis though it did not reach statistical significance. The findings indicate that an all-molecular approach—using a single specimen and single test platform to simultaneously assess vaginitis and STIs—yields superior STI case-finding compared to pairing STI NAATs with traditional clinician or laboratory vaginitis diagnoses. The authors conclude that combined molecular testing can improve risk stratification, align with STI screening guidelines, and streamline clinical workflows.
items.citation: Getman D, Seña AC, Nenninger A et al.. Clinical utility of nucleic acid amplification testing for detection of sexually transmitted infections in women with symptomatic bacterial vaginosis and vulvovaginal candidiasis identified by conventional versus molecular diagnoses.. Journal of clinical microbiology. 2026

items.title: Pre-exposure prophylaxis adherence and risks of HIV and sexually transmitted infection among adult men before vs during the COVID-19 pandemic.
items.summary: This study examined how the COVID-19 pandemic affected pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) adherence and rates of HIV and sexually transmitted infections among adult men who newly initiated PrEP. Using a retrospective cohort analysis of commercially insured individuals drawn from a large administrative claims database spanning 2018 to 2021, the researchers applied trajectory modeling to identify distinct patterns of PrEP adherence before and during the pandemic, then used weighted regression models to compare HIV incidence and STI rates between the two groups. Men who initiated PrEP during the pandemic showed worse adherence trajectories, with a substantially higher proportion falling into an early discontinuation category compared to those who initiated before the pandemic. Initiating PrEP during the pandemic was associated with a meaningfully elevated risk of HIV acquisition, while STI rates did not differ significantly between the two groups. The authors conclude that the pandemic disrupted HIV prevention through reduced PrEP adherence and increased HIV risk, underscoring the need for targeted strategies to sustain access to prevention services during public health emergencies.
items.venue: Journal of managed care & specialty pharmacy
items.citation: Unigwe IF, Jenjai C, Goodin AJ et al.. Pre-exposure prophylaxis adherence and risks of HIV and sexually transmitted infection among adult men before vs during the COVID-19 pandemic.. Journal of managed care & specialty pharmacy. 2026
