items.title: Molecular Diagnostics of Infectious Diseases.
items.summary: This review examines the current landscape of molecular diagnostic technologies applied to the detection and characterization of pathogens causing infectious diseases. The paper covers nucleic acid amplification approaches, including polymerase chain reaction variants optimized for speed, quantification, and point-of-care use, as well as isothermal amplification methods that operate without thermal cycling and are therefore well-suited to decentralized testing settings. CRISPR-based detection systems, which can be coupled with isothermal amplification to identify amplified nucleic acids at constant temperature, are also discussed as an emerging diagnostic modality. Next-generation sequencing is highlighted for its capacity to detect novel pathogens, diagnose complex infections, trace outbreak transmission routes, monitor pathogen evolution, and analyze microbiomes as potential disease biomarkers. The authors conclude that future advances in infectious disease molecular diagnostics will arise from integrating these complementary technologies into hybrid platforms that address the current limitations of individual methods.
items.citation: Takata M, Chikumi H, Yoshifuji A. Molecular Diagnostics of Infectious Diseases.. Yonago acta medica. 2026

items.title: Recent Advances in CRISPR/Cas Technologies for Biological Discovery, Therapeutics, and Diagnostics.
items.summary: This review examines the broad and expanding applications of CRISPR/Cas technology beyond its original role as a genome-editing tool. The authors survey recent advances across functional genomic screening, epigenome editing, therapeutic target discovery, and molecular diagnostics, with particular attention to newer approaches such as CRISPRi, CRISPRa, base editing, and prime editing. These innovations have deepened understanding of disease mechanisms and opened new avenues for therapeutic intervention in cancer immunotherapy, infectious disease, and neurological disorders. In diagnostics, CRISPR-based platforms leverage programmable nuclease activity to enable sensitive detection of pathogens, cancer biomarkers, and genetic disorders in both laboratory and point-of-care settings. The review concludes that continued development of novel effectors and engineered variants is driving the technology toward personalized medicine and precision diagnostics.
items.citation: Kim MS, Do HS, Jang HY et al.. Recent Advances in CRISPR/Cas Technologies for Biological Discovery, Therapeutics, and Diagnostics.. Biomolecules. 2026

items.title: Base-mismatched crRNA in CRISPR Enabled Universal One-pot Rapid Nucleic Acid Detection
items.summary: This paper investigated how to overcome the limitation of two-step workflows in CRISPR-Cas12a-based nucleic acid diagnostics, which require amplification and detection to be performed sequentially. The researchers introduced deliberate single-nucleotide mismatches into the seed region of the CRISPR RNA to suppress premature cis-cleavage activity, allowing recombinase polymerase amplification and CRISPR-Cas12a detection to occur simultaneously in a single tube without requiring PAM redesign or expensive modified reagents. Molecular dynamics simulations were used to guide selection of effective mismatches by identifying those producing moderate potential energy variation as correlating with improved detection performance. The strategy was validated against two bacterial pathogens, achieving sensitive and specific detection at very low copy numbers within half an hour, and was demonstrated to work in lyophilized form on battery-powered portable devices and in simulated field soil samples. The authors conclude that this universal, cost-effective approach can simplify RPA-CRISPR diagnostic workflows for infectious disease surveillance in resource-limited settings.
items.citation: Jianhao X, Xin W, Bing Y et al.. Base-mismatched crRNA in CRISPR Enabled Universal One-pot Rapid Nucleic Acid Detection. 2026

items.title: Synergistic Multicomponent Nucleopeptide-Based Hydrogels: Harnessing DNA-Base Pairing and Electrostatic Complementarities
items.summary: This study investigated hybrid molecules called nucleopeptides, which are short peptides functionalized with DNA nucleobases, as building blocks for multicomponent low-molecular-weight hydrogels. The researchers synthesized a series of six nucleopeptides derived from two complementary tetrapeptide sequences carrying opposite charges at physiological pH, each functionalized with one of the four DNA bases introduced via a peptide nucleic acid moiety. By systematically combining these components, they examined how both electrostatic complementarity between oppositely charged peptides and nucleobase-pairing complementarity influence the mechanical and physicochemical properties of the resulting hydrogels, including gelation time, stiffness, thermal stability, and fibrillar network morphology. The results demonstrated that deliberate selection of complementary components allows fine-tuning of hydrogel properties, with some combinations producing synergistic improvements in performance. Notably, the study also revealed unexpected behaviors, highlighting the complexity of these bioinspired multicomponent systems while affirming their potential for developing high-performance supramolecular hydrogels for biomedical and biotechnological applications.
items.citation: Tristan Giraud, Marine Koch, Paul Hoschtettler et al.. Synergistic Multicomponent Nucleopeptide-Based Hydrogels: Harnessing DNA-Base Pairing and Electrostatic Complementarities. ACS Materials Au. 2026

items.title: Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications
items.summary: This review examines how the integration of multiomics technologies and artificial intelligence is reshaping precision drug discovery and translational medicine. The authors synthesize current multiomics approaches—including genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic profiling—alongside advanced deep learning methodologies to assess their combined impact across the drug development pipeline. The review covers applications ranging from target identification and drug repositioning to de novo compound design, virtual screening, pharmacokinetic modeling, and safety assessment, with illustrative cases drawn from oncology, neurodegenerative diseases, and cardiovascular conditions. The authors argue that this convergence accelerates therapeutic innovation by enabling data-driven hypothesis generation and more precise clinical trial design, though they acknowledge persistent challenges including harmonization of heterogeneous data streams, reproducibility, and algorithmic bias. Overall, the paper presents a forward-looking perspective on how multiomics–AI integration marks a new era in bench-to-clinic translational medicine.
items.citation: Yuqing Liu, Kun Zhu, Weijun Peng et al.. Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: CRISPR-Cas systems as next-generation antimicrobials: a systemic review of mechanisms, delivery strategies, and translational challenges
items.summary: This systematic review evaluated the potential of CRISPR-Cas systems as antimicrobial agents against multidrug-resistant bacteria, which pose a growing global threat as conventional antibiotics lose effectiveness. The authors synthesized preclinical and experimental evidence on different CRISPR effectors, including Cas9, Cas12, and Cas13, examining how these tools kill bacteria or restore antibiotic sensitivity through mechanisms such as chromosomal double-strand break induction, resistance plasmid elimination, and RNA-targeted cleavage. Delivery strategies assessed included bacteriophages, conjugative plasmids, and nanoparticles, with phage-mediated delivery showing the most reliable efficacy across complex environments and animal models, and one CRISPR-enhanced phage cocktail has already progressed to clinical evaluation. The review found broad support for CRISPR-Cas antimicrobials as a precision approach to combating resistance, but identified substantial obstacles including limited bacterial host range, instability in physiological conditions, the emergence of escape mutations, and insufficient safety data. The authors conclude that advancing this field will require optimized delivery platforms, multiplex targeting strategies, and standardized regulatory frameworks to enable successful clinical translation.
items.citation: Maha S.I. Wizrah. CRISPR-Cas systems as next-generation antimicrobials: a systemic review of mechanisms, delivery strategies, and translational challenges. Frontiers in Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Targeting biofilm-driven antibiotic resistance: emerging mechanisms and next-generation therapeutic interventions
items.summary: This review paper examined the mechanisms by which microbial biofilms contribute to antimicrobial resistance and surveyed emerging therapeutic strategies to overcome this challenge. Biofilms dramatically enhance antibiotic tolerance through multiple mechanisms, including restricted drug penetration, enzymatic antibiotic degradation, and facilitation of horizontal gene transfer, making biofilm-associated infections exceptionally difficult to treat. The authors highlight that the current absence of approved anti-biofilm drugs represents a critical gap in the therapeutic arsenal, underscoring the urgency for new approaches. The review synthesizes recent advances in understanding biofilm-driven resistance and evaluates a diverse range of next-generation interventions, including nanotechnology, antimicrobial peptides, bacteriophage-derived enzymes, quorum-sensing inhibitors, CRISPR-based tools, microbiome engineering, and artificial intelligence-assisted drug discovery. The authors argue that a multi-platform therapeutic approach combining these strategies offers the greatest promise for redefining treatment outcomes in the context of resistant, biofilm-associated infections.
items.citation: Abdulkarim Mbaraka, Ritu Raj Meena, Ekta Menghani et al.. Targeting biofilm-driven antibiotic resistance: emerging mechanisms and next-generation therapeutic interventions. Frontiers in Microbiology. 2026

items.title: MXene quantum dot polymer nanocomposites as smart platforms for targeted drug delivery and multifunctional biomedical applications: an updated review
items.summary: This review examines MXene quantum dot polymer nanocomposites as multifunctional platforms for biomedical and technological applications, with particular emphasis on targeted drug delivery in cancer treatment. The authors survey how the exceptional electrical conductivity, flexibility, and biocompatibility of MXenes and their composites enable the development of smart microrobots capable of precise navigation and controlled therapeutic release. Combining MXenes with quantum dots in polymer matrices merges electrical, optical, and catalytic properties, broadening utility across drug delivery, tissue engineering, flexible electronics, and energy storage. Stimuli-responsive polymers incorporated into these systems allow controlled activation of embedded therapeutic agents, and the customizable surfaces of these nanocomposites facilitate co-delivery of multiple drugs for synergistic treatment effects. The review concludes that while these nanocomposites show considerable promise for driving biomedical and sustainable technology innovation, significant challenges related to scalable production, material stability, and clinical translation remain to be addressed.
items.citation: Mohammad Hossein Karami, Omid Moini Jazani. MXene quantum dot polymer nanocomposites as smart platforms for targeted drug delivery and multifunctional biomedical applications: an updated review. Discover Nano. 2026

items.title: Direct cell-to-cell transmission of retrotransposons
items.summary: The paper investigated how certain transposable elements spread between cells, a process previously thought to require the fusogenic Envelope protein characteristic of retroviruses. Focusing on long terminal repeat retrotransposons in the *Drosophila* ovary, the researchers used genetics, imaging, and electron microscopy to examine how these elements move from somatic cells into the germline despite lacking Envelope. They discovered that these retrotransposons encode a short transmembrane protein called sORF2, which has structural similarities to viral cell-cell fusogens and localizes to invasive somatic protrusions that carry retroviral capsids and make physical contact with the oocyte. Removing sORF2 abolished both protrusion formation and soma-to-germline capsid transmission, demonstrating its essential role in this process. The authors further found that sORF2-like proteins are broadly distributed among insect retrotransposons and appear in certain fish and bird viruses, revealing a noncanonical, Envelope-independent transmission mechanism shared across retrotransposons and non-enveloped viruses.
items.citation: Maya Voichek, Andreas Bernhard, Lea Lauterjung et al.. Direct cell-to-cell transmission of retrotransposons. Cell. 2026

items.title: Flashing with colours: Photometric indicators of an early interaction in type II supernovae
items.summary: This study examined early-time optical observations of Type II supernovae to investigate whether photometric data alone can distinguish events showing evidence of interaction with circumstellar material from those that do not. The researchers combined newly observed supernovae from the POISE collaboration with a literature sample to assemble a large dataset featuring high-cadence, high-precision multi-band photometry, categorizing events based on the presence or absence of transient narrow emission features ("flash features") in spectra taken within days of explosion. They characterized key photometric properties including rise times, peak luminosities, and color evolution across the two categories. Flash supernovae were found to be more luminous at peak, tend toward longer rise times in the blue band, and are systematically bluer than non-flash events at around twenty days post-explosion, with these color differences attributed to intrinsic physical differences rather than dust extinction. Crucially, the study demonstrates that color-curve breaks occurring within the first month after explosion, combined with peak absolute magnitude, serve as strong photometric diagnostics capable of identifying circumstellar material interaction even when early-time spectroscopy is unavailable.
items.citation: A. Mendez-Llorca, G. Folatelli, C. P. Gutierrez et al.. Flashing with colours: Photometric indicators of an early interaction in type II supernovae. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Bad Diagnosis: Analyzing Consent and Data Collection Practices of Mobile Medical Apps
items.summary: This paper investigated the consent and data collection practices of mobile health applications available on the Google Play Store, focusing on how these apps handle sensitive medical information. The researchers developed a framework combining static analysis and privacy policy examination, along with a rigorous definition to distinguish genuine health apps from general wellness programs, applied across a large corpus of apps. Their analysis revealed widespread permission misuse, with a majority of apps requesting access to location, camera, and microphone data despite no functional justification based on their stated purposes. Most critically, nearly all apps in the sample failed to provide users with a consent form, constituting direct violations of regulatory frameworks such as GDPR, and even those that did provide consent forms frequently exhibited gaps between what users consented to and what data was actually collected. The authors conclude that these findings expose a deeply problematic mHealth ecosystem and call for stronger enforcement of privacy regulations in this domain.
items.citation: Ethan Myers, Lorenzo De Carli, Shantanu Sharma et al.. Bad Diagnosis: Analyzing Consent and Data Collection Practices of Mobile Medical Apps. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Entering the Era of Circumplanetary Ring Detection with Direct Imaging
items.summary: This paper investigated how circumplanetary rings around exoplanets would affect reflected light observations from upcoming direct imaging missions, particularly the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. The researchers developed a hybrid forward model that combines ray casting to compute planet-ring shadowing with empirical reflectance spectra derived from Cassini observations of Saturn's rings, applied to Jupiter-like planets with varying ring sizes, inclinations, and obliquities. They found that rings can substantially enhance the flux ratio of a planet-star system at favorable geometries, with Saturn-equivalent rings boosting peak flux noticeably and more extended rings producing enhancements exceeding an order of magnitude, though certain geometries can also suppress total brightness below that of a ringless planet. The flux contribution of rings proved highly sensitive to obliquity and orbital position, and multi-band photometry was identified as a useful diagnostic for detecting exorings. The authors conclude that unaccounted-for rings could bias inferred planetary properties from direct imaging and must be considered in both observation planning and data interpretation.
items.citation: Samantha N. Hasler, Alexandra Z. Greenbaum, Geoffrey Bryden et al.. Entering the Era of Circumplanetary Ring Detection with Direct Imaging. arXiv. 2026

items.title: AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery
items.summary: This paper investigates whether large language model agents can automate the assessment of reproducibility and analytical robustness in scientific research, using published cancer epidemiology studies as a test case. The authors constructed a benchmark comprising published papers based on a major U.S. cancer registry, pairing each with the data and resources needed to reproduce their findings. An AI agent was developed that successfully reproduced a substantial majority of atomic claims extracted from these papers, and a separate agentic pipeline was built to identify the analytical choices underlying each finding, propose defensible alternatives, and rerun analyses to test whether different choices change the conclusions. The pipeline flagged a meaningful fraction of fully reproduced findings as potentially sensitive to analytical decisions, directing those cases toward expert review. The work demonstrates that LLM agents can meaningfully support scientific peer review by automating reproduction, systematically probing robustness, and prioritizing findings that warrant closer human scrutiny.
items.citation: Shicheng Liu, Krista Opsahl-Ong, Andrew Drozdov et al.. AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery. arXiv. 2026

items.title: DiscoveryRSI: Recursively Learning to Discover Valuable Hypotheses
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of automating scientific hypothesis generation and refinement by developing a framework that can recursively learn from its own research process. The authors introduce DiscoveryRSI, a multi-agent evolutionary system that builds hypothesis trees, compiles investigations into executable tasks, and improves itself through three mechanisms: attributing credit to research contributions, identifying productive and failed strategies, and applying learned improvements to new investigations. They also introduce a benchmark called DFM-Bench for evaluating hypothesis quality and cumulative research progress across multiple levels of analysis. Testing across four life-science domains, the framework demonstrated measurable improvements in hypothesis quality after successive rounds of self-improvement, with particular gains in falsifiability and data resolvability. The resulting model outperformed several prominent large language model-based research agents on expert-rated hypothesis importance, plausibility, and correspondence with literature published after the model's training cutoff.
items.citation: Jianyuan Zhong, Chenwei Wu, Zhaochen Yu et al.. DiscoveryRSI: Recursively Learning to Discover Valuable Hypotheses. arXiv. 2026

items.title: SparseMax-dSTL: Sound Robustness with Horizon-Independent Gradient Allocation for Temporal Logic Trajectory Optimization
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of using gradient-based optimization to enforce Signal Temporal Logic (STL) specifications in safety-critical trajectory planning, where smooth approximations of robustness must be both sound and maintain meaningful gradient signals regardless of task horizon length. The authors identify that existing approximations, such as log-sum-exp and generalized-mean robustness, fail to simultaneously satisfy both properties—soundness ensures non-negative robustness only for satisfying trajectories, while horizon-independent gradient allocation ensures that violating samples always receive non-negligible gradient weight. To overcome these limitations, the authors introduce new lower approximations of the minimum and maximum operators whose gradients correspond to sparsemax projections, and prove that the resulting robustness measure is sound, lies below the exact robustness, and has an approximation error bounded independently of the number of samples or horizon length. Experimental validation on a planar unicycle and a simulated seven-joint manipulator operating near a person demonstrates that existing approximations can yield positive robustness on violating trajectories and suffer from vanishing gradient weights as the horizon grows, whereas the sparsemax-based approach maintains a gradient weight of one on violating samples across all tested horizons. The proposed method consistently produces trajectories that satisfy the STL specification with the required margin, while competing approaches return constraint-violating solutions.
items.citation: Sai Sandeep Damera, Ryan Matheu, John S. Baras et al.. SparseMax-dSTL: Sound Robustness with Horizon-Independent Gradient Allocation for Temporal Logic Trajectory Optimization. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Branched Split Activator-Regulated Cas12a Biosensor For Methyltransferases Detection.
items.summary: This paper investigated the detection of DNA methyltransferases, which are epigenetic enzymes relevant to disease biology, addressing limitations of existing methods such as complex amplification requirements and high background signals. The researchers designed a branched split activator structure that exploits steric hindrance to control CRISPR/Cas12a activity, creating a biosensor called CDMS that becomes activated specifically in response to DNA methyltransferase activity without requiring nucleic-acid amplification. The steric hindrance embedded in split-and-reconstituted Cas12a-activating DNA fragments suppresses nonspecific activation, while methyltransferase-driven removal of this hindrance restores Cas12a activity and generates a detectable signal. The system demonstrated extremely low detection limits for two different methyltransferases, high specificity, and suitability for inhibitor screening. To extend the platform toward practical use, the authors also developed a compact portable optical device enabling point-of-care testing by non-expert users, positioning CDMS as a promising tool for decentralized epigenetic diagnostics.
items.citation: Hu L, Hu H, Liu F et al.. Branched Split Activator-Regulated Cas12a Biosensor For Methyltransferases Detection.. ACS sensors. 2026

items.title: Smartphone-Based Peptide Nucleic Acid (PNA) Probe-Assisted Potentiometric Biosensor for Point-of-Care Testing of SARS-CoV-2 Nucleic Acid
items.summary: This paper presents a potentiometric biosensor designed to detect SARS-CoV-2 nucleic acid at the point of care using peptide nucleic acid probes. The researchers functionalized amine magnetic beads with electrostatically neutral peptide nucleic acid probes specific to SARS-CoV-2, exploiting the neutral charge of these probes to minimize biofouling that plagues conventional negatively charged DNA probes. Upon hybridization with the complementary target DNA, the complex was incubated with cationic magnetic nanoparticles and concentrated onto a screen-printed carbon electrode modified with a plasticized polymeric membrane using an applied magnetic field. The system achieved detection of SARS-CoV-2 DNA across a broad linear range at femtomolar concentrations, with high recovery rates when tested in human saliva. To enable point-of-care application, the biosensor was coupled with a smartphone-based near-field communication electrochemical analyzer, demonstrating a practical and sensitive platform for COVID-19 screening in biological samples.
items.citation: Tuğba Özer, Sakda Jampasa, Atchara Lomae et al.. Smartphone-Based Peptide Nucleic Acid (PNA) Probe-Assisted Potentiometric Biosensor for Point-of-Care Testing of SARS-CoV-2 Nucleic Acid. Analytical Chemistry. 2026

items.title: The Oral–Gut–Brain Axis: From Periodontal Dysbiosis to Neuroinflammation—Mechanistic Pathways, Salivary and Intestinal Biomarkers, and Therapeutic Targets: A Narrative Review
items.summary: This narrative review examined the biological connections between periodontal disease, gut health, and brain function, conceptualized as an oral–gut–brain axis, with the aim of providing an integrative mechanistic framework linking these systems. The authors synthesized evidence from a broad literature search covering the molecular pathways by which periodontal dysbiosis may disrupt intestinal homeostasis and promote neuroinflammation, as well as the utility of salivary and intestinal biomarkers along this axis. Key findings indicate that periodontal pathogens such as Porphyromonas gingivalis and Fusobacterium nucleatum can translocate ectopically to the gut, where they are associated with reduced tight junction protein expression, altered microbial composition, increased blood–brain barrier permeability, microglial activation, and amyloid-beta accumulation in preclinical and observational studies. Salivary biomarkers including matrix metalloproteinases and interleukins, alongside intestinal markers such as short-chain fatty acids and calprotectin, were identified as promising non-invasive tools for monitoring systemic inflammatory burden across the axis. The authors conclude that while the framework is biologically plausible and may help explain comorbidities among periodontal, cardiometabolic, and neurodegenerative diseases, the current evidence remains largely associative and requires validation through longitudinal human studies before causal claims can be established.
items.citation: Caterina Nela Dumitru, Alina Oana Dumitru, Gabriel Valeriu Popa et al.. The Oral–Gut–Brain Axis: From Periodontal Dysbiosis to Neuroinflammation—Mechanistic Pathways, Salivary and Intestinal Biomarkers, and Therapeutic Targets: A Narrative Review. Dentistry Journal. 2026

items.title: Vitamin D<sub>3</sub> oral rinsing reduces salivary SARS-CoV-2 antigen detectability: a clinical trial with public health implications.
items.summary: This clinical trial investigated whether rinsing the mouth with a Vitamin D₃ solution could affect the accuracy of saliva-based rapid antigen tests for SARS-CoV-2. Adults with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection provided paired saliva samples immediately before and after a one-minute Vitamin D₃ oral rinse, with each sample analyzed by both rapid antigen test and rapid RT-PCR under blinded conditions. The oral rinse converted a substantial majority of antigen-positive samples to antigen-negative results, significantly reducing overall antigen positivity, while RT-PCR positivity rates and cycle threshold values remained largely unchanged. The persistence of viral RNA alongside diminished antigen detection suggests the rinse interfered with antigen detection rather than eliminating the virus itself. The authors conclude that Vitamin D₃ oral rinsing represents a previously unrecognized pre-analytical variable that can compromise saliva-based antigen screening, with important implications for infectious disease surveillance and public health testing programs.
items.citation: Feteih SMN, Heaphy ELG, Aljagthmi A et al.. Vitamin D<sub>3</sub> oral rinsing reduces salivary SARS-CoV-2 antigen detectability: a clinical trial with public health implications.. Frontiers in oral health. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Molecular Testing on Saliva and Oral Swabs for Pulmonary Tuberculosis.
items.summary: This study evaluated whether molecular testing on saliva and oral swabs could serve as accurate, non-sputum alternatives for diagnosing pulmonary tuberculosis. Using a nested case-control design within a prospective cohort of adults and children at primary care centers in Colombia, researchers collected paired saliva and nylon-flocked oral swab samples from participants with culture-confirmed tuberculosis and matched culture-negative controls, then tested these samples using Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra. Saliva demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity against sputum culture as the reference standard, exceeding the World Health Organization's minimum sensitivity target for a low-complexity non-sputum diagnostic, while oral swabs showed lower sensitivity but similarly high specificity. Saliva outperformed swabs in sensitivity by a clinically meaningful margin, though the two methods did not differ significantly in specificity. The vast majority of participants found both collection methods acceptable, supporting their feasibility as patient-friendly alternatives to sputum-based tuberculosis testing.
items.venue: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America

items.title: Lethal hantavirus at sea: Infectious disease outbreaks on cruise ships and limits of preparedness
items.summary: This paper examines a lethal hantavirus outbreak that occurred aboard the expedition cruise ship Hondius in 2026, representing an unusual and unprecedented cluster of rodent-borne zoonotic disease in a maritime setting. The authors analyzed the epidemiological circumstances of the outbreak, in which multiple passengers developed severe acute respiratory illness across a South Atlantic itinerary spanning remote and ecologically diverse locations, and reviewed the broader context of infectious disease outbreaks on cruise ships. Because hantavirus is transmitted primarily through inhalation of aerosolized infected rodent excreta rather than person-to-person spread, the outbreak likely reflects a point-source exposure that may have occurred onboard, during shore excursions, or prior to embarkation, though the precise origin remained under investigation. The paper highlights the unusual intersection of zoonotic disease risk with global travel and expedition tourism, noting that standard cruise ship outbreak preparedness frameworks are poorly suited to address pathogens with environmental and wildlife transmission dynamics. The authors call for viral sequencing and coordinated international public health investigation to clarify the source of infection, and discuss broader implications for outbreak preparedness in maritime environments.
items.citation: Alimuddin I. Zumla, Brian McCloskey, Giuseppe Ippolito et al.. Lethal hantavirus at sea: Infectious disease outbreaks on cruise ships and limits of preparedness. Travel Medicine and Infectious Disease. 2026

items.title: Andes virus outbreak linked to expedition cruise ship travel, multi-country investigation and response, April to June 2026
items.summary:
The abstract describes an active outbreak investigation rather than a completed study with findings, but sufficient information is present for a brief summary.

This report describes an outbreak of Andes orthohantavirus infection linked to an expedition cruise ship operating across multiple countries. Cases arose among both passengers and crew members aboard the vessel, spanning individuals of numerous nationalities, and the event prompted medical evacuations, repatriations, and coordinated international contact tracing, isolation, and quarantine measures. The outbreak is notable for the unusual cruise ship setting, given that Andes virus transmission typically involves rodent exposure in terrestrial environments. At the time of reporting the investigation remained ongoing, with authorities working to clarify the infection source, identify risk factors, and prevent further spread.
items.citation: Oda E. van den Berg, UKHSA ANDV Team, Ettore Severi et al.. Andes virus outbreak linked to expedition cruise ship travel, multi-country investigation and response, April to June 2026. Eurosurveillance. 2026

items.title: Human infection with Andes hantavirus: an update for the general physician
items.summary: Andes virus (ANDV), a rodent-borne hantavirus transmitted through inhalation of contaminated aerosols, is unique among hantaviruses in its capacity for sustained human-to-human transmission via respiratory droplets and close contact. This paper provides an updated clinical overview of ANDV infection for general physicians, covering its transmission dynamics, clinical spectrum, and management challenges. The most severe manifestation, Hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, involves acute respiratory failure, haemodynamic instability, kidney and liver injury, and dysregulated immune responses, with disease severity linked to specific haematological and biochemical markers. No approved antiviral treatments or vaccines exist, leaving care entirely supportive, and case fatality rates have exceeded one-third in recent outbreaks. A cruise ship outbreak in April 2026, which rapidly spread among passengers of many nationalities, is highlighted as a demonstration of how ANDV's combination of zoonotic origin and human-to-human transmissibility poses a significant global public health threat in the context of modern international travel.
items.citation: Emanuele Durante‐Mangoni, Iolanda Cafarella, Silvia Mercadante et al.. Human infection with Andes hantavirus: an update for the general physician. European Journal of Internal Medicine. 2026

items.title: Demonstration of Logical Error Suppression in a Surface Code Memory on a Cloud-Accessible IBM Superconducting Processor
items.summary: This paper investigates whether logical error suppression can be demonstrated in a surface code quantum memory running on a publicly accessible superconducting quantum processor. The researchers implemented rotated surface-code memory on an IBM Nighthawk processor, systematically optimizing the syndrome extraction circuit by combining short readout, fused measurement and reset, and an echo pulse on data qubits during ancilla readout. These optimizations substantially reduced the per-round logical error rate compared to a standard unoptimized baseline, with improvements differing between the X and Z bases due to noise asymmetry. Increasing the code distance while holding the other dimension fixed produced clear logical error suppression, with error-suppression factors approaching approximately two under maximum-likelihood decoding, though long-lived error correlations observed in extended memory experiments suggest a persistent noise component that weakens the distance advantage at longer timescales. The work highlights how circuit compilation choices critically affect fault-tolerant performance and motivates co-design of hardware and error correction circuits for near-term cloud quantum processors.

items.title: Plasmonic Nanoarray Biosensors for Non-Invasive Cancer Diagnostics.
items.summary: This review examines the use of plasmonic nanoarray biosensors for detecting cancer-associated biomarkers in urine and saliva, two non-invasively collected biofluids that present analytical challenges due to low biomarker abundance, biological variability, and interfering matrix components. The authors survey nanoarray architectures, fabrication strategies, surface functionalization approaches, and optical signal transduction mechanisms—including localized surface plasmon resonance, surface-enhanced Raman scattering, and metal-enhanced fluorescence—as applied to nucleic acids, proteins, and extracellular vesicles relevant to several cancer types. Plasmonic nanoarrays are highlighted for their ability to concentrate electromagnetic fields, enable multiplexed readout, and integrate with microfluidic handling systems to partially overcome the limitations of conventional surface-based sensing. The review identifies persistent barriers to clinical translation, including biofouling, pre-analytical variability, fabrication reproducibility, and insufficient validation with authentic clinical biofluids. The authors conclude that progress in standardized biofluid processing, scalable manufacturing, and fully integrated microfluidic platforms will be necessary to advance these sensors toward practical cancer screening applications.

items.title: Group A Streptococcus molecular point of care testing in a paediatric emergency department.
items.summary: This study examined whether molecular point-of-care testing for Group A Streptococcus could improve management of children presenting to a paediatric emergency department during a period of heightened streptococcal activity. The researchers conducted a pilot study in which children who had a clinician-requested throat swab also provided a second swab processed using a molecular point-of-care test, though clinical decisions remained based on conventional culture results alone. The study found that streptococcal prevalence was relatively low, yet the large majority of children who had throat swabs taken received antibiotics, and among those prescribed antibiotics, most had a negative point-of-care test result. Conventional culture results took several days to return, whereas the molecular test produced results within minutes. The authors conclude that point-of-care testing could potentially reduce unnecessary antibiotic prescribing by ruling out streptococcal infection rapidly, but emphasize that further research is needed to establish whether its use confers a net clinical benefit.
items.citation: Mills EA, Bingham R, Nijman RG et al.. Group A Streptococcus molecular point of care testing in a paediatric emergency department.. The Journal of antimicrobial chemotherapy. 2026

items.title: Biological characteristics and whole-genome sequencing analysis of an alpha-hemolytic Streptococcus pyogenes strain
items.summary: This study investigated an unusual alpha-hemolytic strain of *Streptococcus pyogenes* isolated from erysipelas skin secretions, a species that typically displays beta-hemolysis. The researchers used whole-genome sequencing combined with phenotypic testing, multilocus sequence typing, emm gene typing, and bioinformatic analyses to characterize the strain's virulence factors, antibiotic resistance genes, and phylogenetic relationships. The isolate belonged to sequence type ST176 and emm type emm58.7, carried macrolide and tetracycline resistance genes, and harbored numerous virulence factor-encoding genes despite its atypical hemolytic phenotype. The alpha-hemolytic behavior was attributed to an amino acid substitution in the sagB gene that likely disrupts the functional expression of streptolysin S. The authors conclude that because this strain resembles commensal viridans streptococci in appearance, it poses a risk of clinical misidentification, and that integrating multiple diagnostic approaches is essential to improve detection of such atypically presenting strains.
items.citation: Mo Y, Wang Q, Qiu M. Biological characteristics and whole-genome sequencing analysis of an alpha-hemolytic Streptococcus pyogenes strain. 2026

items.title: Gut microbial-derived metabolites: key players in kidney disease and renal fibrosis
items.summary: This review examines the relationship between gut microbial-derived metabolites and kidney disease, focusing on how disruptions in the gut microbiome contribute to renal injury and fibrosis. The paper synthesizes current knowledge on how kidney disease leads to intestinal barrier dysfunction and microbial dysbiosis, which in turn reduces beneficial short-chain fatty acids while allowing uremic toxins to accumulate. The authors detail the signaling pathways through which these metabolites — particularly tryptophan metabolites — mediate communication between the gut microbiota and the kidneys, influencing conditions such as acute kidney injury, chronic kidney disease, diabetic kidney disease, and various nephropathies. The review identifies specific molecular targets, including aryl hydrocarbon receptors and nuclear factor kappa B pathways, that are modulated by these metabolites. The authors also survey therapeutic strategies — including natural products, prebiotics, probiotics, and renal replacement therapy — that target gut dysbiosis and its metabolic consequences as potential precision-based interventions for kidney disease.
items.citation: Wan-Ying Zhang, Yu-Lu Zhang, Qing-Qing Yu et al.. Gut microbial-derived metabolites: key players in kidney disease and renal fibrosis. International Journal of Biological Sciences. 2026

items.title: Editor's Choice – European Society for Vascular Surgery (ESVS) 2026 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
items.summary: These guidelines represent an updated clinical practice framework developed by the European Society for Vascular Surgery for managing vascular graft and endograft infections, succeeding a previous version. The guidelines were constructed by synthesising the best available scientific evidence with expert opinion, with recommendations graded by both strength and level of evidence according to an established classification system. The resulting document covers a broad range of topics including definitions, diagnosis, multidisciplinary team management, antimicrobial therapy, and management of both intracavity and extracavity infections, as well as follow-up care. A dedicated section addresses shared decision making and provides supporting information for patients, while unresolved clinical questions are also acknowledged. The guidelines aim to offer comprehensive, current guidance to clinicians and patients in selecting optimal management strategies for vascular graft and endograft infections.
items.venue: European Journal of Vascular and Endovascular Surgery
items.citation: Anne Lejay, Ben R. Saleem, Tara D. Barwick et al.. Editor's Choice – European Society for Vascular Surgery (ESVS) 2026 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections. European Journal of Vascular and Endovascular Surgery. 2026

items.title: Biodiversity and biogeography of the multi-kingdom cancer microbiome
items.citation: Anders B. Dohlman, Robin Mjelle, Henry M. Wood et al.. Biodiversity and biogeography of the multi-kingdom cancer microbiome. Cell. 2026

items.title: The Gut–Vagina Axis
items.summary: This review paper examines the emerging concept of the gut–vagina axis, focusing on how interactions between the gut and vaginal microbiomes may influence female health. The authors synthesize recent advances in microbiome research to characterize the bidirectional communication between these two distinct microbial communities, encompassing microbial migration, hormonal regulation, immune modulation, and metabolite exchange. They outline the most promising aspects of this gut–vaginal relationship and discuss how disruptions or shifts in these interactions could affect both local and systemic health outcomes. The abstract is relatively high-level, but the paper appears to argue that understanding this axis is important for advancing knowledge of female physiology and disease.
items.citation: Lorenzo Agoni, Elena Roselletti, Giovanni Marasco et al.. The Gut–Vagina Axis. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: In silico pharmacological analysis of Tinospora cordifolia compounds targeting African swine fever virus B175L
items.citation: Kasuni Karunarathne, Saumya Poorni, Nethra Jayampathi et al.. In silico pharmacological analysis of Tinospora cordifolia compounds targeting African swine fever virus B175L. PLoS ONE. 2026

items.title: Rapid Respiratory Microbiological Point-of-Care Testing and Antibiotic Use in Primary Care
items.summary: This randomized clinical trial investigated whether rapid multiplex microbiological point-of-care testing, capable of detecting numerous respiratory viral and bacterial pathogens within about 45 minutes, could safely reduce antibiotic prescribing for respiratory tract infections in primary care. The trial enrolled patients aged 12 months and older at general practices in Southwest England who were being considered for antibiotic treatment, randomizing them to receive the point-of-care test or usual care. Overall, the intervention did not reduce same-day antibiotic prescribing, with approximately equal proportions of each group receiving antibiotics, and patient-reported symptom severity did not differ between groups, indicating no harm from using the test. However, subgroup analyses revealed that when a virus was detected by the test, antibiotic prescribing was substantially reduced compared to usual care, and a similar reduction was observed in patients with chronic lung disease. The authors conclude that while the test did not broadly reduce antibiotic use across the whole population studied, targeted application in cases where a viral pathogen is identified may offer a pathway to more judicious prescribing.
items.citation: Alastair D Hay, Samantha Abbs, Matthew J Ridd et al.. Rapid Respiratory Microbiological Point-of-Care Testing and Antibiotic Use in Primary Care. JAMA Internal Medicine. 2026

items.title: Rethinking the design space of Vanilla Pixel Diffusion Transformers
items.summary: This paper revisits the design choices for pixel-space diffusion transformers, which generate images directly without a latent autoencoder. The authors introduce MFlow, an adaptive parameterization that learns to interpolate between clean image prediction and velocity prediction across principal directions of the data, trained end-to-end alongside the diffusion objective. They find that the preferred prediction parameterization depends systematically on both the data representation and model capacity, with larger models favoring velocity prediction. Evaluating across image and video generation benchmarks, MFlow achieves competitive or improved generative performance compared to fixed parameterization approaches. The authors also identify a persistent high-frequency deficit in pixel diffusion models regardless of parameterization, which they address with ConvRefiner, a lightweight convolutional module trained post-hoc with an adversarial loss that restores high-frequency image statistics while keeping the diffusion backbone frozen.
items.citation: Soumik Mukhopadhyay, Long Mai, Abhinav Shrivastava et al.. Rethinking the design space of Vanilla Pixel Diffusion Transformers. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Flashing with colours: Photometric indicators of an early interaction in type II supernovae
items.summary: This paper investigated whether early-time photometric observations alone can distinguish Type II supernovae that show evidence of interaction with dense circumstellar material from those that do not, without requiring spectroscopic confirmation. The researchers assembled a large sample of Type II supernovae combining newly published and literature events, obtaining high-cadence, high-precision multi-band optical photometry and classifying objects based on the presence or absence of transient narrow emission lines of highly ionised elements ("flash features") in spectra taken within four days of explosion. They found that supernovae exhibiting flash features tend to be more luminous at peak, show longer rise times in the blue band, and are systematically bluer than non-flash events, with distinct colour distributions persisting for weeks after explosion. Crucially, the study identified that breaks in colour-curve evolution occurring within the first month after explosion, combined with peak absolute magnitude, provide a strong photometric diagnostic capable of identifying circumstellar material interaction. This suggests that spectroscopic follow-up in the immediate post-explosion window may not be strictly necessary to identify such interacting supernovae, which has significant implications for large photometric surveys.
items.citation: A. Mendez-Llorca, G. Folatelli, C. P. Gutierrez et al.. Flashing with colours: Photometric indicators of an early interaction in type II supernovae. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Entering the Era of Circumplanetary Ring Detection with Direct Imaging
items.summary: This paper investigates how circumplanetary rings around exoplanets would affect reflected light observations from upcoming direct imaging missions, particularly the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. The researchers developed a hybrid forward model that combines ray casting to account for mutual planet-ring shadowing with empirical reflectance spectra derived from Cassini observations of Saturn's rings, simulating Jupiter-like planets with icy rings of varying sizes, inclinations, and obliquities. Their simulations demonstrate that rings can substantially enhance the planet-ring system's flux ratio at favorable geometries, with Saturn-equivalent rings boosting peak flux considerably and more extended rings producing even greater contrast enhancements, while at other geometries rings can actually suppress total system brightness below that of a ringless planet. The flux contribution of rings is shown to be highly sensitive to orbital geometry and obliquity, and multi-band photometry is proposed as a complementary diagnostic tool for identifying exorings. The authors conclude that circumplanetary rings have the potential to bias inferred planetary properties from direct imaging data and must be carefully accounted for in observation planning and interpretation.
items.citation: Samantha N. Hasler, Alexandra Z. Greenbaum, Geoffrey Bryden et al.. Entering the Era of Circumplanetary Ring Detection with Direct Imaging. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Blind Precise Assembly: Proprioceptive Sim-to-Real Peg-in-Hole for Diverse Parts
items.summary: This paper investigates whether proprioceptive sensing alone—using only joint positions, velocities, and actions—is sufficient for robots to perform precise, contact-rich assembly tasks without any visual, force, torque, or tactile feedback. The researchers trained blind assembly policies using reinforcement learning entirely in simulation, randomizing part geometries, grasp configurations, and contact conditions across thousands of procedurally generated assemblies. These policies were applied to three challenging tasks: peg insertion, gear meshing, and nut threading, with neither the fixture pose nor the part pose known to the policy. The peg insertion policy transferred zero-shot to the real world at a meaningful success rate, and controlled comparisons against vision-based policies in simulation revealed that blind proprioceptive policies generalize substantially better to unseen part shapes and sizes, albeit at the cost of speed. The authors also released an open-source procedural geometry generator for MuJoCo that preserves assembly clearances and outperforms standard convex decomposition methods in both accuracy and computational efficiency.
items.citation: Antonia Bronars, Younghyo Park, Kushal Kedia et al.. Blind Precise Assembly: Proprioceptive Sim-to-Real Peg-in-Hole for Diverse Parts. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Geometric Viewpoint of $L^\infty$ Estimates for Linearized Monge-Ampère Equations
items.summary: The paper studies interior boundedness properties of solutions to the linearized Monge–Ampère equation, approaching the problem through differential geometry rather than classical real-analysis techniques. The authors establish a Harnack inequality by working on gradient graphs of Monge–Ampère solutions, treating the problem in an extrinsic geometric setting and applying Moser iteration on extrinsic balls combined with a gradient estimate for the extrinsic distance function. This geometric framework yields interior supremum estimates for the linearized equation under suitable geometric bounds on the graph. Notably, the approach bypasses the standard Caffarelli–Gutiérrez Harnack inequality as well as the engulfing and covering properties of Monge–Ampère sections that are central to more classical treatments.
items.citation: Arghya Rakshit, Derek Wu. Geometric Viewpoint of $L^\infty$ Estimates for Linearized Monge-Ampère Equations. arXiv. 2026

items.title: AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery
items.summary: This paper investigated whether large language model agents could automate the evaluation of reproducibility and analytical robustness in scientific research, addressing the high cost of performing such assessments manually. The authors created a benchmark dataset of published studies based on a major U.S. cancer registry, pairing each paper with the data and resources needed to reproduce its findings. An AI agent was then developed to reproduce published claims, achieving success on a substantial majority of atomic claims while generating executable code as a baseline for further work. Beyond reproduction, an agentic pipeline was designed to probe the robustness of findings by identifying underlying analytical choices, generating defensible alternatives, and re-running analyses to assess whether different choices alter conclusions. The pipeline flagged a notable subset of fully reproduced findings as potentially sensitive to analytical decisions, demonstrating that LLM agents can meaningfully support scientific peer review by automating reproduction and directing expert scrutiny toward vulnerable analytical choices.
items.citation: Shicheng Liu, Krista Opsahl-Ong, Andrew Drozdov et al.. AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Rapid Molecular Detection Method for Streptococcus agalactiae Based on Bacteriophage Lysin Lysis and Real-Time PCR.
items.summary: This study developed a rapid point-of-care molecular diagnostic method for detecting Group B Streptococcus, a major cause of neonatal infections, with the goal of overcoming the slow turnaround time of conventional culture methods. The approach used a bacteriophage lysin to achieve complete bacterial lysis and nucleic acid extraction within five minutes, followed by real-time fluorescence quantitative PCR targeting the GBS cylA gene, completing the entire assay in approximately thirty-five minutes. The method was evaluated across two clinical cohorts using vaginal swab samples and demonstrated perfect sensitivity in both phases, with high specificity that improved further after confirmatory sequencing of discordant samples. Compared to antigen testing in the second cohort, the new assay showed substantially superior sensitivity, while conventional culture required up to forty-eight hours versus the assay's thirty-five minute turnaround. The authors conclude that this bacteriophage lysin-based molecular assay holds promise for intrapartum or near-patient GBS screening, though further validation in real-world clinical workflows is needed.
items.venue: European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology
items.citation: Zhu H, Zeng X, Huang X et al.. A Rapid Molecular Detection Method for Streptococcus agalactiae Based on Bacteriophage Lysin Lysis and Real-Time PCR.. European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Temporal trends in pediatric group A streptococcal pharyngitis across the coronavirus disease 2019 era: A large retrospective cohort study.
items.summary: This study examined how the COVID-19 pandemic and its associated public health measures affected the rates of Group A Streptococcus pharyngitis in children over time. Using a large retrospective cohort of pediatric patients presenting with suspected tonsillopharyngitis at a tertiary clinic across pre-pandemic, pandemic, and post-pandemic periods, researchers compared positivity rates and applied multivariable logistic regression to identify independent predictors of Group A Streptococcus detection. Positivity rates increased progressively across all three periods, rising from the pre-pandemic era through the pandemic and reaching the highest levels in the post-pandemic period. Older age and male sex were also independently associated with a greater likelihood of testing positive. The authors conclude that this progressive rise likely reflects a combination of factors including changes in healthcare utilization, diagnostic practices, and transmission dynamics, and they call for ongoing surveillance to better characterize these trends.
items.venue: The Journal of international medical research
items.citation: Nas Y, Gözüküçük S, Bayırlı H et al.. Temporal trends in pediatric group A streptococcal pharyngitis across the coronavirus disease 2019 era: A large retrospective cohort study.. The Journal of international medical research. 2026

items.title: Rapid molecular culture versus conventional culture for periprosthetic joint infection: diagnostic performance and clinical relevance.
items.summary: This study evaluated a rapid PCR-based assay called Molecular Culture as a diagnostic tool for periprosthetic joint infection, a serious complication following joint replacement surgery. Researchers retrospectively analysed sonication fluid samples collected during hip and knee revision arthroplasty procedures, comparing the molecular assay's performance against conventional culture using established infection criteria for patient classification. The molecular assay demonstrated improved negative percentage agreement after clinical correlation compared to analytical results alone, and it identified additional clinically relevant pathogens that conventional culture missed, while delivering results in approximately four hours rather than the extended turnaround times associated with conventional culture. The findings suggest that the molecular assay performs best as an adjunctive rather than standalone diagnostic method, complementing rather than replacing conventional culture. The authors conclude its greatest clinical utility may be in patients with prior antibiotic exposure or uncertain infection status, where rapid pathogen exclusion could accelerate appropriate antimicrobial decision-making.
items.venue: Journal of bone and joint infection
items.citation: Morreel E, Savelkoul P, van Loo I. Rapid molecular culture versus conventional culture for periprosthetic joint infection: diagnostic performance and clinical relevance.. Journal of bone and joint infection. 2026

items.title: Diagnosing Sepsis and Identifying Bacterial Resistance Genes Directly from Whole Blood Using a Rapid Real-Time PCR System.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of a rapid real-time PCR system for identifying pathogens and antimicrobial resistance genes directly from whole blood in adult sepsis patients. The researchers compared results from the rapid PCR panel, which can detect a broad range of pathogens and resistance genes within four hours, against conventional automated blood culture methods collected simultaneously from the same patients. The most commonly isolated organisms were Staphylococcus aureus, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Escherichia coli, and resistance genes including mecA, OXA-48, and CTX-M were among those detected. The rapid PCR method demonstrated strong specificity and good sensitivity, with a statistically significant agreement rate with blood culture results, and patients in the concordant group showed shorter time to positive blood culture signals. The authors conclude that the ability to identify causative pathogens and resistance profiles within four hours provides a meaningful clinical advantage in enabling early targeted therapy, potentially preventing progression to septic shock and reducing mortality.
items.citation: Begmyradova S, Öksüz L, Aktas Z et al.. Diagnosing Sepsis and Identifying Bacterial Resistance Genes Directly from Whole Blood Using a Rapid Real-Time PCR System.. International journal of molecular sciences. 2026

items.title: Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.
items.summary: This paper reviews advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarker research over a five-year period, examining how new evidence has shaped updated WHO policy guidance that consolidates recommendations for detecting tuberculosis disease and drug resistance into a single framework. Key developments include the expanded role of digital chest radiography with computer-aided detection as a core screening tool, and the broadened deployment of decentralised molecular diagnostics such as low-complexity automated and manual nucleic acid amplification tests across diverse specimen types. Novel specimen approaches, including tongue swabs, stool, gastric aspirate, and nasopharyngeal samples, together with innovations like sputum pooling, have improved bacteriological confirmation particularly in children and other populations unable to produce sputum. Rapid molecular drug-resistance testing has progressed, and targeted next-generation sequencing is now endorsed at the reference laboratory level, while urine lipoarabinomannan assays offer diagnostic benefit in people with HIV and advanced disease. Despite these advances, the paper identifies substantial performance, implementation, and equity gaps, and notes that no biomarker has yet met WHO target product profile criteria for a point-of-care test capable of reliably distinguishing infection from disease, including subclinical tuberculosis.
items.citation: Walzl G, McHugh TD, Chakaya J et al.. Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.. The Lancet. Microbe. 2027

items.title: Molecular point-of-care: technological evolution, clinical applications, and future perspectives
items.citation: Zhang D, Cui X, Zhang R et al.. Molecular point-of-care: technological evolution, clinical applications, and future perspectives. Frontiers in bioengineering and biotechnology. 2026

items.title: Molecular Diagnostics of Infectious Diseases.
items.summary: This review examines the current landscape of molecular diagnostic technologies used to detect and characterize pathogens responsible for infectious diseases. The paper surveys two principal approaches: nucleic acid amplification methods, including polymerase chain reaction variants and isothermal amplification techniques, and next-generation sequencing for comprehensive genomic characterization. Advances in polymerase chain reaction development are described with emphasis on improving reaction speed through microfluidic systems, enabling quantification via real-time and digital formats, and expanding accessibility through point-of-care and fully automated platforms. Isothermal amplification methods are highlighted as particularly suited for point-of-care settings due to their lack of requirement for thermal cycling equipment, and CRISPR-based detection is identified as an emerging complementary tool frequently combined with these approaches. Next-generation sequencing is presented as capable of identifying novel pathogens, tracking outbreak transmission, monitoring pathogen evolution, and characterizing microbiomes as potential disease biomarkers, with the authors anticipating future progress through hybrid platforms that integrate multiple technologies.
items.citation: Takata M, Chikumi H, Yoshifuji A. Molecular Diagnostics of Infectious Diseases.. Yonago acta medica. 2026

items.title: Molecular Detection of Feline Hemotropic <i>Mycoplasma</i> from Blood Samples of Sick Cats: A Comparative Study Between a Commercial Nucleic Acid Test Card and Conventional Polymerase Chain Reaction.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of a rapid commercial nucleic acid test card for detecting feline hemotropic *Mycoplasma* species in clinically ill cats, comparing it against conventional polymerase chain reaction targeting the 16S rRNA gene as the reference method. Whole blood samples from sick cats presented to a veterinary teaching hospital were tested using both methods, with sequence analysis performed on discordant results to identify contributing factors. Conventional PCR revealed that *Candidatus* Mycoplasma haemominutum was the predominant species detected, followed by *Mycoplasma haemofelis* and *Candidatus* Mycoplasma turicensis. The commercial test card demonstrated high sensitivity, specificity, overall accuracy, and precision relative to conventional PCR, delivering results within thirty minutes, with false-negative cases attributed to likely low bacterial burdens or other assay-related factors. The authors conclude that the rapid nucleic acid test card represents a practical point-of-care molecular diagnostic tool capable of supporting timely clinical decision-making in cats with suspected hemotropic mycoplasmosis.
items.citation: Nimsuphan B, Ruenphet S, Kengradomkij C et al.. Molecular Detection of Feline Hemotropic <i>Mycoplasma</i> from Blood Samples of Sick Cats: A Comparative Study Between a Commercial Nucleic Acid Test Card and Conventional Polymerase Chain Reaction.. Veterinary sciences. 2026

items.title: Nanomaterials-enabled point-of-care diagnostics for pathogens.
items.summary: This review paper examines how nanomaterials can enhance point-of-care testing technologies for detecting pathogens, addressing persistent limitations in sensitivity, specificity, multiplexing, and quantitative accuracy that affect conventional approaches when handling low-abundance pathogens in complex clinical samples. The authors surveyed the functional roles that representative nanomaterials play in diagnostic contexts, encompassing optical signal output, catalytic signal amplification, target enrichment, and interfacial regulation. They then analyzed how these nanomaterial properties improve specific diagnostic platforms, including lateral flow assays, biosensors, microfluidic systems, and isothermal nucleic acid amplification methods. Three principal nanomaterial-assisted recognition mechanisms were identified—pathogen surface recognition, reactive oxygen species-mediated signal conversion, and nucleic acid recognition—and their applications across respiratory, urinary, and fecal specimen types were discussed. The authors conclude that these advances collectively support the development of more sensitive, integrated, and field-deployable diagnostic systems for controlling infectious disease.
items.citation: Wu J, Wang D, Ye W et al.. Nanomaterials-enabled point-of-care diagnostics for pathogens.. Frontiers in medicine. 2026

items.title: Development of a microfluidic isothermal amplification nucleic acid detection (mFIND) platform for simultaneous detection of respiratory pathogens.
items.summary: The paper describes the development of a centrifugal microfluidic platform designed to simultaneously detect multiple respiratory pathogens, including influenza A and B, SARS-CoV-2, and RSV, which are major causes of acute respiratory infections. The system integrates four independent reaction chambers preloaded with lyophilized reagents on a chip, paired with a portable analyzer that automates sample handling, isothermal amplification, and real-time fluorescence detection in a simplified two-step workflow. The platform operates at a consistent temperature, uses very small reaction volumes per chamber, and completes detection within fifteen minutes while being storable at room temperature. Testing demonstrated extremely low limits of detection for all four target pathogens, no cross-reactivity against a broad panel of non-target organisms, and complete agreement with quantitative PCR across a large set of clinical samples. The authors conclude that the platform offers a practical point-of-care nucleic acid testing solution suitable for decentralized settings by combining rapid turnaround, minimal reagent use, and parallel multi-target detection.
items.citation: He P, Feng Y, Zhou X et al.. Development of a microfluidic isothermal amplification nucleic acid detection (mFIND) platform for simultaneous detection of respiratory pathogens.. Biosensors & bioelectronics. 2026

items.title: Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications
items.summary: This review examines how the integration of multiomics technologies and artificial intelligence is reshaping precision drug discovery and clinical translation. The authors synthesize how approaches spanning genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics generate deep insight into disease mechanisms, while deep learning architectures are applied to decode these complex biological datasets and build predictive models. The review covers the application of this combined framework across the drug development pipeline, including target identification, drug repositioning, de novo compound design, virtual screening, pharmacokinetic modeling, and safety assessment. Disease areas such as oncology, neurodegeneration, and cardiovascular conditions are used to illustrate the practical potential of these converging technologies. The authors also acknowledge persistent challenges, including the harmonization of heterogeneous omics data, reproducibility concerns, and the need to address algorithmic bias, while arguing that the fusion of multiomics and artificial intelligence marks a new era in bench-to-clinic translational medicine.
items.citation: Yuqing Liu, Kun Zhu, Weijun Peng et al.. Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Loss-of-function mutation in Omicron variants reduces spike protein expression and attenuates SARS-CoV-2 infection
items.citation: Michelle N. Vu, R. Elias Alvarado, Dorothea R. Morris et al.. Loss-of-function mutation in Omicron variants reduces spike protein expression and attenuates SARS-CoV-2 infection. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: mRNA vaccine immunity is enhanced by hepatocyte detargeting and not dependent on dendritic cell expression
items.summary: This paper investigated how cell-type-specific expression of mRNA vaccine-encoded proteins influences immune responses, a question that had been poorly understood despite the diversity of cell types transfected by lipid nanoparticle delivery. The researchers used synthetic microRNA target sites incorporated into mRNA vaccines to selectively silence expression in professional antigen-presenting cells, hepatocytes, or myocytes, then assessed the resulting immune responses. They found that expression in professional antigen-presenting cells was dispensable for T cell priming, while myocyte expression drove similar or stronger immune responses, suggesting cross-presentation or cross-dressing mechanisms are more important than direct antigen presentation. Hepatocyte expression, by contrast, suppressed antigen-specific T cell responses partly through the PD1/PDL1 pathway, and silencing hepatocyte expression enhanced vaccine-induced immunity and reduced tumor burden in a lymphoma model. These findings demonstrate that non-professional antigen-presenting cell expression critically shapes mRNA vaccine immunogenicity, and that incorporating microRNA target sites represents a strategy to tune immune outcomes by restricting expression to specific cell types.
items.citation: Adam R. Marks, Sophia Siu, Filippo Bianchini et al.. mRNA vaccine immunity is enhanced by hepatocyte detargeting and not dependent on dendritic cell expression. Nature Biotechnology. 2026

items.title: Regulatory Challenges and Opportunities for Cell‐Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Pharmaceutical Development: A European and Global Perspective
items.summary: This paper examines the regulatory landscape surrounding cell-derived extracellular vesicles as therapeutic and diagnostic agents, focusing on how their acellular nature creates classification difficulties within existing pharmaceutical frameworks. The authors critically analyzed current regulatory approaches across major jurisdictions, noting that the European Union, the United States, and other regions apply divergent classification criteria, creating inconsistencies in how these products are governed during clinical development. Key technical and regulatory challenges identified include the lack of harmonized critical quality attributes, potency strategies, and comparability standards across regions. The authors argue that extracellular vesicle-based products can be developed within existing medicinal product frameworks such as biologics or related instruments, provided that regulatory tools are applied consistently and ambiguous classification zones are resolved through ongoing dialogue. The work is positioned as a synthesizing resource intended to support regulatory convergence among international agencies and scientific societies working toward safe and reproducible clinical translation of these therapies.
items.citation: Tania Limongi, Paola Milla, Barbara Stella et al.. Regulatory Challenges and Opportunities for Cell‐Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Pharmaceutical Development: A European and Global Perspective. Journal of Extracellular Vesicles. 2026

items.title: Dairy cows infected with influenza A(H5N1) reveals low infectious dose and transmission barriers
items.citation: Carolyn M. Lee, Natalie N. Tarbuck, Hannah J. Cochran et al.. Dairy cows infected with influenza A(H5N1) reveals low infectious dose and transmission barriers. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: Evolutionary characterization of lung cancer metastasis
items.summary: This study investigated how non-small cell lung cancer evolves from initial diagnosis through metastatic spread to death, using an extensive collection of primary and metastatic tumor samples gathered longitudinally from patients enrolled in two clinical programs. By applying DNA sequencing to samples covering the large majority of radiologically detected metastases alongside multi-region sampled primary tumors, the researchers reconstructed the evolutionary trajectories of tumors over time. They found that metastatic genomes diverge substantially from their primary tumor ancestors, acquiring additional driver alterations and genome doubling events after dissemination, and that multiple distinct primary tumor subclones commonly seeded separate metastases in the same patient. Critically, more than half of sampled metastases were themselves seeded by other metastases rather than directly from the primary tumor, with the duration a metastasis existed influencing its likelihood of further spread, and most metastatic migrations remaining within the same anatomical cavity. The small fraction of subclones that spread beyond the thorax disseminated widely and showed enrichment for somatic copy-number alterations, implicating chromosomal instability as a potential facilitator of extrathoracic metastasis.
items.citation: Sonya Hessey, Abigail Bunkum, Ariana Huebner et al.. Evolutionary characterization of lung cancer metastasis. Nature. 2026

items.title: Flashing with colours: Photometric indicators of an early interaction in type II supernovae
items.summary: This paper investigated early-time photometric and spectroscopic properties of type II supernovae to explore signatures of interaction between the explosion and dense circumstellar material. The researchers assembled a large sample of supernovae, combining newly observed events with literature data, obtaining high-cadence, high-precision multi-band optical photometry and classifying events based on whether their early spectra showed transient narrow emission lines from highly ionised elements, known as flash features. They found that supernovae exhibiting these flash features tend to be more luminous at peak and show longer rise times in the blue band compared to non-flash events. Notably, flash supernovae are systematically bluer than non-flash events at around three weeks post-explosion, with distinct breaks in their colour curves within the first month that differ markedly between the two classes. These results demonstrate that photometric observations alone, specifically the colour-curve break characteristics combined with peak magnitude, can serve as a reliable diagnostic for identifying supernovae undergoing circumstellar interaction even without early spectroscopic data.
items.citation: A. Mendez-Llorca, G. Folatelli, C. P. Gutierrez et al.. Flashing with colours: Photometric indicators of an early interaction in type II supernovae. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Entering the Era of Circumplanetary Ring Detection with Direct Imaging
items.summary: This paper investigated how circumplanetary rings affect the reflected light signals of exoplanets in the context of upcoming direct imaging missions. The authors developed a hybrid forward model combining a ray casting framework for computing planet-ring shadowing with empirical reflectance spectra from Cassini observations of Saturn's rings, applied to Jupiter-like planets with varying ring sizes, inclinations, and obliquities. Their simulations demonstrate that rings can substantially enhance flux ratios at favorable geometries, with Saturn-equivalent rings boosting peak flux significantly in the visible and more extended rings producing even greater contrast enhancements, though certain geometries can actually suppress system brightness below that of a ringless planet. The flux contribution of rings is highly sensitive to orbital geometry, and multi-band observations are proposed as a complementary diagnostic for identifying exorings. The authors conclude that unaccounted-for rings could bias inferred planetary properties from direct imaging data and must be considered in observation planning and interpretation, particularly for instruments like the Roman Coronagraph.
items.citation: Samantha N. Hasler, Alexandra Z. Greenbaum, Geoffrey Bryden et al.. Entering the Era of Circumplanetary Ring Detection with Direct Imaging. arXiv. 2026
