items.title: Mechanism-informed diagnostic accuracy of blood biomarkers for sepsis-associated encephalopathy: a systematic review and Bayesian diagnostic network meta-analysis.
items.summary: This systematic review and network meta-analysis investigated the diagnostic accuracy of blood biomarkers for sepsis-associated encephalopathy, a serious form of acute brain dysfunction complicating sepsis. The authors searched multiple databases and applied a Bayesian diagnostic network meta-analysis framework to compare biomarkers spanning an immune activation–blood-brain barrier–glial–neuronal injury biological axis, characterizing heterogeneity by reference standard type and sampling timing relative to an anchor event. Blood-brain barrier and glial markers such as GFAP and S100β demonstrated more balanced diagnostic discrimination than classical neuronal injury markers, while upstream immune and alarmin candidates ranked highly in Bayesian comparative analyses, though several top-ranked biomarkers were supported by only single studies. A key limitation was that few included studies assessed whether biomarkers provide incremental diagnostic value beyond established clinical predictors such as illness severity scores or sedation-related confounders. The authors conclude that findings are hypothesis-generating and call for prospective head-to-head validation under standardized phenotyping and anchor-based sampling protocols to determine whether mechanism-staged biomarker panels offer meaningful added diagnostic utility.
items.citation: Zhang Q, Zhu R, Li Y et al.. Mechanism-informed diagnostic accuracy of blood biomarkers for sepsis-associated encephalopathy: a systematic review and Bayesian diagnostic network meta-analysis.. Frontiers in molecular neuroscience. 2026

items.title: Dynamic Changes of Neutrophil Nuclear Membrane CD63 as a Potential Biomarker for Early Adjunctive Diagnosis and Prognostic Evaluation of Sepsis in Critically Ill Patients: A Prospective Cohort Study.
items.summary: This study investigated whether neutrophil nuclear membrane CD63 (nmCD63), a marker reflecting the early pathological process of targeted nuclear degranulation during neutrophil extracellular trap formation, could serve as a biomarker for sepsis diagnosis and prognosis in critically ill patients. The researchers developed a flow cytometry assay to quantify nmCD63 and validated it prospectively across two centers, establishing diagnostic cutoffs and combined models in a derivation cohort before applying them without modification to an independent validation cohort. nmCD63 levels rose progressively with disease severity and outperformed conventional inflammatory markers such as C-reactive protein and procalcitonin in distinguishing non-infectious systemic inflammation from non-severe infection. When combined with the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment score, nmCD63 achieved high discriminatory performance for identifying sepsis in infected patients. Crucially, dynamic changes in nmCD63 preceded shifts in all conventional biomarkers, and trajectory analysis over seven days provided reliable prognostic stratification, supporting its dual diagnostic and prognostic utility in sepsis.
items.citation: Gao X, Zhang M, Li L et al.. Dynamic Changes of Neutrophil Nuclear Membrane CD63 as a Potential Biomarker for Early Adjunctive Diagnosis and Prognostic Evaluation of Sepsis in Critically Ill Patients: A Prospective Cohort Study.. MedComm. 2026

items.title: Clinical utility of combined serum IL-6, PCT, and SAA assays for early diagnosis and severity stratification of neonatal sepsis.
items.summary: This study investigated whether combining three serum biomarkers could improve early diagnosis and severity assessment of neonatal sepsis, a condition notoriously difficult to identify due to nonspecific clinical signs. Neonates admitted to a neonatal intensive care unit were enrolled and classified into confirmed sepsis, suspected sepsis, and non-infective control groups, with sepsis patients further divided by disease severity; serum interleukin-6, procalcitonin, and serum amyloid A were measured at admission before antibiotic treatment. All three biomarkers were significantly elevated in confirmed sepsis compared to the other groups, and were further elevated in severe versus mild-to-moderate cases. While each individual marker demonstrated good discriminatory ability, the combined panel achieved a higher area under the ROC curve than any single biomarker alone, along with strong sensitivity and specificity. The authors conclude that simultaneous measurement of these three markers substantially enhances diagnostic accuracy and severity stratification for neonatal sepsis, supporting its use as a rapid adjunct to blood culture in intensive care settings.
items.citation: Jiang Y, Yang J, Yang S. Clinical utility of combined serum IL-6, PCT, and SAA assays for early diagnosis and severity stratification of neonatal sepsis.. Frontiers in medicine. 2026

items.title: Interpretable admission-stage machine learning for early Sepsis-3 identification in the emergency department.
items.summary: This study developed and evaluated interpretable machine learning models to identify Sepsis-3-defined sepsis at the admission stage in emergency department patients with suspected community-onset sepsis, comparing their performance against conventional biomarkers and the Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome criteria. Using a prospective cohort of adult emergency department patients, the researchers applied feature selection and trained four models — penalized logistic regression, Explainable Boosting Machine, Extreme Gradient Boosting, and Light Gradient Boosting Machine — on demographic, physiological, and laboratory variables routinely available at admission. All machine learning models achieved moderate discrimination and generally outperformed conventional biomarkers and SIRS criteria, though differences in discriminative performance among the machine learning approaches were not statistically significant. The most influential predictors across models were age, procalcitonin, oxygen saturation, respiratory rate, and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, and the interpretable modeling framework provided transparent insight into how these variables contributed to predictions. The authors conclude that such models show promise as clinical decision support tools for early sepsis recognition but require external validation before implementation in practice.
items.citation: Cantaş Türkiş F, Varol B. Interpretable admission-stage machine learning for early Sepsis-3 identification in the emergency department.. Frontiers in medicine. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic accuracy of procalcitonin for identifying paediatric sepsis: A retrospective study in a Malaysian tertiary hospital.
items.summary: This study evaluated whether serum procalcitonin (PCT) could accurately identify sepsis in children presenting to a Malaysian tertiary referral hospital, where early diagnosis is complicated by non-specific clinical signs and delays in microbiological culture results. Using a retrospective design, researchers analysed PCT, C-reactive protein, and white cell count measurements taken at initial presentation in children aged one month to eighteen years who were tested for suspected infection, classifying sepsis according to established international paediatric consensus criteria. PCT concentrations were significantly higher in children with sepsis than in those without, and at a cut-off of 0.5 ng/mL the biomarker achieved moderate sensitivity and specificity, with receiver operating characteristic analysis confirming only moderate overall diagnostic accuracy. PCT showed a moderate positive correlation with C-reactive protein but no meaningful correlation with white cell count. The authors conclude that PCT can serve as a useful adjunctive biomarker in the early evaluation of paediatric sepsis but should not be used in isolation, and must be interpreted alongside clinical assessment and microbiological investigations.
items.citation: Razak SMA, Taib MNA, Abdul Jalil K et al.. Diagnostic accuracy of procalcitonin for identifying paediatric sepsis: A retrospective study in a Malaysian tertiary hospital.. The Medical journal of Malaysia. 2026

items.title: A comprehensive survey of AI agents in healthcare
items.summary: This survey systematically maps the landscape of AI agents applied to healthcare, addressing the challenge of adapting general-purpose agentic frameworks—characterized by autonomy, planning, and tool use—to the safety-critical demands of medical decision-making. The authors reviewed over two hundred recent studies drawn from major academic databases, developing a taxonomy that organizes the field around three pillars: perception of multi-modal clinical data, core agent capabilities such as reasoning and memory, and an application ecosystem structured by stakeholder roles including clinicians, patients, researchers, and administrators. The review finds that the field is experiencing exponential growth but remains heavily concentrated in benchmark and controlled evaluation settings rather than real-world clinical deployment. The authors also categorize evaluation frameworks and assess deployment readiness across technical, evidentiary, and governance dimensions. They conclude that while AI agents hold significant potential to enhance healthcare through autonomous reasoning and workflow integration, translating these systems into clinical practice will require substantial advances in reliability, privacy protection, and operational governance.
items.citation: Gelei Xu, Xueyang Li, Yixiong Chen et al.. A comprehensive survey of AI agents in healthcare. Journal of Biomedical Informatics. 2026

items.title: A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression
items.summary: This systematic literature review examined how different forms of exercise influence the expression of Toll-like receptors, a family of immune-cell receptors that trigger inflammatory signalling cascades and have been implicated in the chronic low-grade inflammation associated with sedentary lifestyles and non-communicable diseases. The authors searched multiple databases and included studies in which exercise was used as an isolated intervention in human participants, ultimately analysing a substantial body of literature spanning several exercise modalities and durations. Acute resistance exercise tended to upregulate TLR expression, whereas acute aerobic exercise showed a neutral or, particularly in healthy individuals, downregulatory effect. Chronic resistance and combined training programmes predominantly left TLR levels unchanged or reduced them, while chronic aerobic training produced more mixed results with most measurements showing no significant change. The authors conclude that exercise interacts with TLR signalling in a modality- and duration-dependent manner, but note that considerable heterogeneity in study designs limits firm conclusions and that further standardised research is needed to clarify the underlying mechanisms and clinical implications.
items.citation: Kasper Favere, Matthias Bosman, Peter Delputte et al.. A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Gut microbial-derived metabolites: key players in kidney disease and renal fibrosis
items.summary: This review paper examined the relationship between gut microbial-derived metabolites and kidney disease, including acute kidney injury and various forms of chronic kidney disease. The authors synthesized current evidence showing that kidney injury disrupts intestinal barrier function and causes gut microbial dysbiosis, which in turn alters the balance of microbial metabolites—reducing beneficial short-chain fatty acids while allowing uremic toxins to accumulate. These metabolic disturbances were found to influence kidney pathology through multiple signaling pathways, with tryptophan metabolites identified as particularly important mediators of gut-kidney communication. The review also mapped out how specific molecular pathways, including aryl hydrocarbon receptor and nuclear factor kappa B signaling, are regulated by these microbial metabolites to drive renal fibrosis and disease progression. Finally, the authors highlight potential therapeutic strategies targeting gut dysbiosis, including natural products, prebiotics, probiotics, and renal replacement therapy, as avenues for more precise treatment of kidney diseases.
items.citation: Wan-Ying Zhang, Yu-Lu Zhang, Qing-Qing Yu et al.. Gut microbial-derived metabolites: key players in kidney disease and renal fibrosis. International Journal of Biological Sciences. 2026

items.title: Federated Learning in Multimodal Healthcare Diagnostics: Privacy-Preserving AI for Biomedical Imaging, Electronic Health Records, Wearables, and Clinical Decision Support
items.summary: This review paper examines the application of federated learning as a privacy-preserving approach to training artificial intelligence models across multimodal healthcare data sources, including biomedical imaging modalities, electronic health records, wearable devices, and clinical decision support systems. The authors conducted a literature review spanning multiple healthcare domains to assess how federated learning enables collaborative model training across institutions without transferring raw patient data, instead sharing only model updates between participating sites. The paper finds that while federated learning substantially reduces direct exposure of sensitive clinical data and improves alignment with privacy regulations, it does not guarantee confidentiality on its own, as vulnerabilities such as gradient leakage, model inversion, and membership inference attacks require additional safeguards. The review also identifies persistent implementation barriers including system heterogeneity, data imbalance, communication bottlenecks, and fairness concerns that limit widespread adoption. Based on this synthesis, the authors offer actionable recommendations for regulators, developers, and healthcare systems aimed at advancing safe and equitable federated learning deployments across diverse geographic and institutional contexts.
items.venue: Archives of Computational Methods in Engineering
items.citation: Shon G. Nemane, Vaishnavi M. Sarad, Dhiraj P. Tulaskar et al.. Federated Learning in Multimodal Healthcare Diagnostics: Privacy-Preserving AI for Biomedical Imaging, Electronic Health Records, Wearables, and Clinical Decision Support. Archives of Computational Methods in Engineering. 2026

items.title: Pseudomonas aeruginosa: associated pathogenesis, epidemiology, resistance mechanisms, host response and emerging treatment strategies
items.summary: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a critical-priority pathogen responsible for a substantial proportion of healthcare-associated infections globally, with particularly high mortality in intensive care settings and progressive lung damage in chronic conditions such as cystic fibrosis. This review examines the bacterium's pathogenesis, epidemiology, resistance mechanisms, and host responses, as well as emerging treatment strategies. The organism's virulence is driven by a coordinated arsenal of factors including quorum sensing, phenazines, rhamnolipids, exopolysaccharides, and the toxin pyocyanin, while biofilm formation dramatically elevates antimicrobial tolerance and enables chronic infection. During persistent infection, key host defences including mucociliary clearance, antimicrobial peptides, and immune cell responses become progressively overwhelmed, and biofilms sustain damaging inflammation. Rising rates of multidrug and carbapenem resistance across multiple continents are fuelling interest in alternative therapeutic approaches such as anti-virulence agents, biofilm-disrupting enzymes, nanoparticles, bacteriophage therapy, and host-directed immunomodulation.
items.citation: Sheeba Sawant, Safura Shaikh, Timothy Baldwin et al.. Pseudomonas aeruginosa: associated pathogenesis, epidemiology, resistance mechanisms, host response and emerging treatment strategies. Archives of Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Stimuli-responsive nanocarriers for precision targeted and controlled antimicrobial drug delivery in drug-resistant infections
items.summary: This review examines stimuli-responsive nanocarriers as a strategy to overcome the limitations of conventional antibiotics, which fail to achieve sustained therapeutic concentrations at infection sites and inadvertently promote antimicrobial resistance through non-specific systemic distribution. The authors systematically analyze how infected tissues present distinct microenvironmental features—including acidic pH, elevated reactive oxygen species, pathogen-associated enzymatic activity, and hypoxia—that can serve as triggers for spatiotemporally controlled drug release. The review covers the mechanistic basis of pH-, enzyme-, redox-, and multi-stimuli-responsive nanocarrier systems, detailing how trigger-induced physicochemical changes govern drug retention, penetration, and release within drug-resistant infection niches. The authors also assess how these platforms address resistance-associated barriers such as biofilm tolerance, intracellular pathogen persistence, efflux-mediated drug extrusion, and enzymatic antibiotic degradation, while critically comparing their performance against passive nanocarriers and free antibiotics. The review concludes by identifying translational challenges including microenvironmental heterogeneity, trigger variability, manufacturing scalability, and regulatory complexity, positioning stimuli-responsive nanocarriers as a context-aware approach to antimicrobial therapy that may help address drug resistance beyond the capacity of conventional antibiotic discovery.
items.citation: Li Dai, Xiaoyan Sun. Stimuli-responsive nanocarriers for precision targeted and controlled antimicrobial drug delivery in drug-resistant infections. Frontiers in Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Can Language Models Play the Wikipedia Game?
items.summary: This paper investigated whether language models can effectively navigate large document networks by playing the Wikipedia Game, in which players must reach a target article by traversing only hyperlinks between articles. The researchers tested sentence embedding models and large language models across five Wikipedia language editions and five academic literature datasets, constructing large local graphs of Wikipedia pages and paper citations to enable evaluation without dependence on external APIs. Models were benchmarked against human players and a term-frequency baseline to provide meaningful comparisons. No model significantly outperformed human players, though a small set of frontier reasoning and large-parameter models achieved comparable performance. Performance and rankings varied considerably across languages and subject domains, with practical implications for deploying these models in real-world information retrieval settings.
items.citation: Alexander Hickey, Joanna Knight, James Bishop. Can Language Models Play the Wikipedia Game?. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Can machines reason non-verbally?
items.summary: The paper investigates whether machines can perform visual non-verbal reasoning, a domain where even advanced AI systems struggle with tasks such as completing abstract patterns or delineating ambiguous regions of interest. The authors identify a core challenge: unlike verbal reasoning, where intermediate steps can be checked through logic or automated tests, visual reasoning involves implicit steps that are difficult to verify. To address this, they introduce GenVerOpt, a framework that integrates generation, verification, and iterative optimisation into a unified reasoning pipeline, enabling models to refine solutions on a per-sample basis rather than relying on patterns learned during training. Testing across diverse tasks including abstract IQ puzzles, prostate cancer segmentation, liver vessel reconstruction, and tumour boundary delineation, the framework surpassed human performance on the IQ puzzles and matched or exceeded clinical and expert benchmarks on the medical imaging tasks. The authors conclude that machine reasoning can extend meaningfully beyond language, and that visual non-verbal reasoning represents a viable foundation for more general and flexible artificial intelligence.
items.citation: Shaheer U. Saeed, Zion Tse, Gregory Slabaugh et al.. Can machines reason non-verbally?. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Comprehensive JWST Slitless Spectroscopic Census of $\sim$12,000 Emission-Line Galaxies at Redshift $0\sim9$ in COSMOS
items.summary: This paper presents a large-scale census of emission-line galaxies using James Webb Space Telescope slitless spectroscopy from the COSMOS-3D program, covering a contiguous wide-field area with grism spectroscopy in the near-infrared. The authors developed a multi-step source identification framework that incorporates information from spectra, imaging, spectral energy distributions, and spatial distributions, and notably introduced convolutional neural networks and large language models to automate and improve the identification process. The resulting catalog contains over twelve thousand objects spanning redshifts from essentially zero to nine, with detections of numerous emission lines enabling continuous coverage of galaxy populations across cosmic time. Composite spectra constructed in multiple redshift bins reveal faint spectral features — including higher-order hydrogen recombination lines, CO absorption bands, and iron emission lines — that are undetectable in individual spectra. The work demonstrates the power of wide-field slitless spectroscopy for building large, homogeneous spectroscopic samples and provides a key reference dataset for studies of star formation, chemical enrichment, and AGN activity throughout cosmic history.
items.citation: Shuqi Fu, Zijian Zhang, Danyang Jiang et al.. A Comprehensive JWST Slitless Spectroscopic Census of $\sim$12,000 Emission-Line Galaxies at Redshift $0\sim9$ in COSMOS. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Where to Look Matters: Rethinking Sub-Volume Sampling in 3D Medical Self-supervised Learning
items.summary: This paper investigates a largely overlooked component of self-supervised learning for three-dimensional medical images: the strategy used to sample sub-volumes during pretraining. The authors first demonstrate through controlled experiments that the quality of cropped sub-volumes directly influences downstream transfer performance, establishing sub-volume sampling as a meaningful bottleneck. To address this, they reframe cropping as a "where-to-look" problem and propose a plug-and-play framework that replaces random cropping with an offline, coarse-to-fine probe bank that selects sub-volumes guided by anatomy-awareness, informativeness, and diversity. The framework is instantiated in two variants—a lightweight version relying on geometric and image-statistical cues, and a richer diagnostic version using frozen visual features—to assess whether simple volume-intrinsic signals suffice or semantic features provide additional benefit. Experiments across multiple self-supervised backbones and downstream tasks show that the lightweight variant consistently outperforms random sampling, with mechanistic analyses linking the gains to more anatomically meaningful observations, reduced spatial redundancy, more efficient learning dynamics, and better-structured representations.
items.citation: Junkai Liu, Le Zhang. Where to Look Matters: Rethinking Sub-Volume Sampling in 3D Medical Self-supervised Learning. arXiv. 2026

items.title: RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models
items.summary: This paper introduces RSI-Anything, a domain-general framework designed to enable recursive self-improvement by using predictive world models to guide both action selection and learning-data curation, reducing reliance on costly external feedback. The framework builds on JEPA-Anything and incorporates mechanisms for conditional world-model adaptation and compatibility checks to determine whether updated policy-model pairs should be retained as policies evolve. Across a range of computational and scientific tasks—including code repair, graphical user interface navigation, laboratory planning, and chemical reaction optimization—the framework demonstrates consistent performance gains over static baselines and standard optimization approaches. Notably, laboratory-planning scores more than doubled across successive policy versions, and reaction optimization substantially outperformed Bayesian optimization under equivalent experimental budgets. The authors conclude that combining predictive world models with structured system update retention enables robust recursive self-improvement across diverse and heterogeneous environments.
items.citation: Taoyong Cui, Pinxian Zeng, Wanghan Xu et al.. RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models. arXiv. 2026

items.title: When VLMs Destroy What They Know: Spatial Representations Fall Below Lexical Priors
items.summary: Vision-Language Models are widely used for image understanding and reasoning, but this paper investigates whether their internal representations actually encode structured spatial relationships reliably. The authors developed a new metric called EICS to assess whether concepts are consistently represented under controlled interventions, and a benchmark called CASP-VL that uses causally controlled spatial perturbations derived from scene graphs. Testing across multiple VLM architectures, they found that spatial relations are encoded far less faithfully in internal representations than lexical information, even in models that perform well on standard compositional benchmarks. Although spatial relation information is detectable at the token level corresponding to the predicate itself, this information is lost when sentences are aggregated into global representations via end-of-sequence tokens or mean pooling. The findings reveal a systematic representational failure that output-based evaluations cannot detect: relational information present in the input is not preserved in the downstream representations VLMs actually use.
items.citation: Shubh Garg, Chen Shani. When VLMs Destroy What They Know: Spatial Representations Fall Below Lexical Priors. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Integrated evaluation of rapid diagnostic testing, genotypic-phenotypic resistance profiling, and AI-Assisted prediction models for antimicrobial stewardship and clinical outcomes in a resource-limited setting.
items.summary: This prospective observational study investigated whether combining rapid diagnostic testing, molecular resistance gene profiling, and an artificial intelligence prediction model could improve antimicrobial stewardship and patient outcomes in a resource-limited hospital setting. Adult patients with suspected bacterial infections were enrolled and underwent conventional antibiotic susceptibility testing alongside rapid diagnostics and genotypic resistance characterization, with an AI model developed from clinical and laboratory data to predict resistance. The integrated approach dramatically shortened the time to pathogen identification and initiation of effective therapy compared to conventional testing alone, while also substantially increasing the proportion of patients receiving appropriate antibiotics and reducing broad-spectrum antibiotic use. These improvements were accompanied by shorter hospital stays and lower mortality in the integrated diagnostic group, and the AI model showed strong discriminatory performance. The authors conclude that this combined strategy represents a potentially cost-effective and scalable approach to combating antimicrobial resistance, particularly in settings with limited resources.
items.citation: Hammad M, Arif R, Fardoos S et al.. Integrated evaluation of rapid diagnostic testing, genotypic-phenotypic resistance profiling, and AI-Assisted prediction models for antimicrobial stewardship and clinical outcomes in a resource-limited setting.. PloS one. 2026

items.title: Recent Advances and Future Perspectives in the Detection of Carbapenem-Resistant <i>Acinetobacter Baumannii</i>.
items.summary: This review examines the landscape of detection technologies for carbapenem-resistant *Acinetobacter baumannii*, a pathogen classified by the World Health Organization as a critical priority due to its multidrug resistance and limited treatment options. The authors surveyed a broad range of diagnostic approaches, from conventional phenotypic and antimicrobial susceptibility testing through molecular amplification methods, mass spectrometry, whole-genome and metagenomic sequencing, AI-assisted diagnostics, and biosensor or CRISPR-integrated platforms. Conventional culture-based testing remains the reference standard but is constrained by lengthy turnaround times, whereas molecular methods such as PCR substantially reduce this delay, and isothermal amplification platforms like LAMP and RPA offer even faster results compatible with point-of-care use. Emerging genomic and AI-driven approaches enable comprehensive resistance profiling and outbreak surveillance, while biosensor platforms promise highly sensitive portable detection, though hurdles around multiplexing, standardization, and clinical validation persist. The review concludes that CRAB diagnostics are transitioning toward integrated, automated platforms and stresses the importance of balancing analytical performance, speed, cost, and point-of-care suitability.
items.citation: Ye Q, Liu Y, Zhang K et al.. Recent Advances and Future Perspectives in the Detection of Carbapenem-Resistant <i>Acinetobacter Baumannii</i>.. Infection and drug resistance. 2026

items.title: Concordance of AI-driven antimicrobial recommendations using rapid molecular versus phenotypic-optimized workflows for bloodstream infections: a prospective study in a resource-limited setting
items.summary: This study evaluated an integrated diagnostic-therapeutic program that combined rapid molecular diagnostics with AI clinical decision support to guide early antimicrobial therapy in bloodstream infections, followed by conventional culture-based phenotypic testing with AI-driven optimization. Conducted prospectively in a resource-limited setting, the study analyzed consecutive monomicrobial bloodstream infection episodes processed through parallel molecular and conventional diagnostic workflows, comparing turnaround times, identification accuracy, resistance detection, and therapeutic recommendation concordance between the two approaches. Molecular diagnostics dramatically reduced diagnostic turnaround time compared to conventional culture-based methods, and concordance between the two workflows was high for bacterial identification and substantial for antimicrobial resistance detection, though therapeutic recommendation concordance was moderate. Resistance detection discordance was identified as the sole independent predictor of therapeutic recommendation discordance, while the integrated strategy delivered appropriate therapy substantially earlier in the majority of cases and phenotypic optimization ensured fully appropriate therapy in all cases. The authors conclude that combining molecular-AI initial guidance with phenotypic-AI optimization represents a viable approach for antimicrobial stewardship programs, balancing speed of treatment initiation with accuracy of definitive therapeutic optimization.
items.citation: Torre JCGdl, Frenkel A, Chavez-Lencinas C et al.. Concordance of AI-driven antimicrobial recommendations using rapid molecular versus phenotypic-optimized workflows for bloodstream infections: a prospective study in a resource-limited setting. 2026

items.title: Rapid Diagnostics and Rapid Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing for Bloodstream Infections: A Narrative Review and Proposed Clinical Actionability Framework.
items.summary: This narrative review examined the landscape of rapid diagnostic technologies for bloodstream infections, including rapid organism identification, molecular and non-molecular resistance-marker methods, and rapid phenotypic susceptibility testing, with the goal of proposing a framework for translating these results into clinical action. The authors searched major biomedical databases for relevant publications over roughly a decade and a half, prioritizing high-quality study designs and implementation research. The most consistent benefit identified across technologies was faster time to appropriate or optimized antimicrobial therapy, including earlier escalation for inactive empirical regimens and earlier de-escalation to narrower agents, whereas effects on mortality, length of stay, and costs were less reproducible. A key finding was that rapid phenotypic susceptibility testing did not demonstrate superiority over standard care on a composite outcome endpoint in a major recent trial, suggesting that the value of any given technology depends heavily on context rather than the technology itself. The authors propose a five-domain actionability framework—encompassing result type and certainty, patient risk, pre-test probability of resistance, institutional capacity to act on results, and stewardship interpretation quality—while explicitly noting the framework is a heuristic requiring prospective validation and local adaptation rather than a validated clinical tool.
items.citation: Chen Q, Qu YG, Li JS et al.. Rapid Diagnostics and Rapid Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing for Bloodstream Infections: A Narrative Review and Proposed Clinical Actionability Framework.. International journal of general medicine. 2026

items.title: Accelerating scientific discovery with Co-Scientist
items.summary: This paper introduces Co-Scientist, a multi-agent AI system built on Gemini designed to augment scientific discovery by generating novel research hypotheses conditioned on researcher objectives and existing scientific evidence. The system employs an asynchronous task execution framework in which agents continuously generate, critique, and refine hypotheses, with hypothesis quality improved over time through a tournament-based evolutionary process and scaling of test-time compute. Automated evaluations confirmed that increasing test-time compute yields progressively better hypothesis quality. The system was validated in three biomedical domains—drug repurposing, novel target discovery, and antimicrobial resistance mechanism elucidation—with Co-Scientist–generated drug repurposing candidates and combination therapies for acute myeloid leukaemia confirmed through in vitro experiments. The authors argue these real-world validations demonstrate the potential of such AI systems to meaningfully accelerate the pace of scientific discovery.
items.citation: Juraj Gottweis, Wei‐Hung Weng, Alexander Daryin et al.. Accelerating scientific discovery with Co-Scientist. Nature. 2026

items.title: Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications
items.summary: This review examines how the integration of multiomics technologies and artificial intelligence is reshaping precision drug discovery and clinical translation. The authors surveyed how genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic approaches, combined with deep learning architectures, can decode complex biological datasets to reveal disease mechanisms and molecular targets. The review covers the application of this combined framework across the drug development pipeline, including target deconvolution, drug repositioning, de novo compound discovery, virtual screening, pharmacokinetic modeling, and safety assessment. Case discussions spanning oncology, neurodegenerative diseases, and cardiovascular conditions illustrate the practical promise of these approaches, while the authors also highlight persistent challenges such as harmonizing disparate omics data, ensuring reproducibility, and addressing algorithmic bias. The authors conclude that the convergence of multiomics and artificial intelligence enables more comprehensive molecular understanding and more precise therapeutic interventions, heralding a new era in bench-to-clinic translational medicine.
items.citation: Yuqing Liu, Kun Zhu, Weijun Peng et al.. Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Artificial intelligence in additive Manufacturing: advances in smart materials, lattice optimization, and process intelligence
items.summary: This review paper examines the convergence of artificial intelligence and additive manufacturing, exploring how data-driven methods are transforming the design, optimization, and control of complex manufacturing systems. The authors trace the historical development of AI integration in additive manufacturing, from early rule-based approaches through to modern deep learning, reinforcement learning, and physics-informed frameworks. The review covers a broad range of applications including machine learning-driven topology and lattice optimization, predictive modeling of process and structural properties, and the use of AI to tailor smart materials such as piezoelectric, shape-memory, and self-healing systems within four-dimensional printing contexts. The authors find that AI replaces labor-intensive experimentation with adaptive predictive models capable of autonomous parameter tuning and multiphysics optimization. They conclude by identifying persistent challenges such as data scarcity and limited model interpretability, and advocate for hybrid physics-informed machine learning combined with digital twin approaches as a pathway toward closed-loop, intelligent manufacturing.
items.venue: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
items.citation: Saqlain Zaman, Md Shahjahan Mahmud, Ali Akber Mollick et al.. Artificial intelligence in additive Manufacturing: advances in smart materials, lattice optimization, and process intelligence. The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology. 2026

items.title: Arc mediates intercellular tau transmission via extracellular vesicles
items.summary: The paper investigated how tau protein spreads between cells in the context of neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal dementia. The researchers focused on the neuronal gene Arc and its potential role in packaging tau into extracellular vesicles, using transgenic mouse models expressing human tau alongside Arc knockout mice to compare vesicle-associated tau content and seeding capacity. They found that Arc is essential for loading tau into extracellular vesicles through a pathway involving the I-BAR protein IRSp53, and that Arc protein directly binds tau to form a complex detectable in both mouse and human brain tissue. When Arc was absent, extracellular vesicles contained substantially less tau and lost the ability to seed tau aggregation, while intracellular tau accumulated within neurons and correlated with accelerated hippocampal neuron loss. The authors conclude that Arc-dependent packaging of tau into extracellular vesicles serves a dual function in clearing tau from neurons and enabling its intercellular transmission.
items.citation: Mitali Tyagi, Eric de Hoog, Matthew Grega et al.. Arc mediates intercellular tau transmission via extracellular vesicles. Cell. 2026

items.title: Synthesis and multilevel evaluation of benzimidazole-based anticancer compounds: DNA/serum albumin interaction, and in-depth theoretical insights
items.summary: Two novel benzimidazole-based compounds were synthesized and comprehensively evaluated for their potential as anticancer agents against multiple cancer cell lines, including lung, breast, and liver cancer, as well as healthy kidney cells. Cytotoxicity assays revealed that one compound showed particularly potent activity against liver and breast cancer cell lines, and mechanistic studies using gene expression analysis demonstrated that both compounds shifted the apoptotic balance by downregulating anti-apoptotic genes while upregulating pro-apoptotic genes in breast cancer cells. The compounds also elevated cellular oxidative stress, increased antioxidant enzyme gene expression, and induced cellular senescence, collectively pointing to a multi-pronged mechanism of cancer cell killing. Fluorescence spectroscopy showed strong DNA binding through an intercalative mode and moderate affinity for serum albumin, suggesting favorable transport properties, while molecular docking and quantum chemical calculations corroborated these experimental observations. Taken together, the findings support these benzimidazole derivatives as promising candidates for further development as anticancer therapeutics.
items.citation: Sevgi Kundu, Senem Akkoç, Yalçın Erzurumlu et al.. Synthesis and multilevel evaluation of benzimidazole-based anticancer compounds: DNA/serum albumin interaction, and in-depth theoretical insights. Molecular and Cellular Biochemistry. 2026

items.title: Soil microbes are the tiny bioengineers running Earth’s underground factory
items.summary: This paper examines the functional roles of diverse microbial communities in soils and the mechanisms by which they regulate critical ecosystem processes. The authors synthesize research across ecological, agricultural, and environmental contexts using a function-centred framework to organize current understanding of soil microbiome science. They identify four conserved functional axes — secondary metabolism, nutrient cycling, community interactions, and stress tolerance — that together govern ecosystem-level outcomes including plant productivity, climate regulation, and pollutant transformation. The authors argue that soil operates as a self-organizing system in which microbial interactions produce emergent behaviour, though the expression of these functions is strongly context dependent. This framework is proposed as a foundation for predictive, ecology-informed strategies to manage soils for sustainable agriculture, environmental remediation, and climate mitigation.
items.citation: Suzanne Hassan-Dalléac, Wafa Guiga, Antonia Suau. Soil microbes are the tiny bioengineers running Earth’s underground factory. Communications Earth & Environment. 2026

items.title: AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities
items.summary: This paper investigates whether capability evaluations — a key safety measure for AI systems before deployment — can reliably uncover dangerous hidden behaviors in models. The researchers constructed backdoor attacks that embed encrypted neural networks within a host model's weights, designed to activate only when a secret trigger is provided, using cryptographic structures called digital lockers. These hidden circuits are provably difficult to detect or elicit under standard cryptographic assumptions, even when an auditor has complete access to the model weights, and this approach extends prior work from concealing fixed strings to hiding arbitrary computations. Testing their constructions on a chemical reaction prediction task as a proxy for capabilities relevant to chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear risks, they found that common elicitation methods — including fine-tuning, weight noising, gradient-based trigger search, and latent adversarial training — failed to uncover the hidden capabilities. The findings reveal a fundamental limit of elicitation-based capability auditing and suggest that current evaluation frameworks cannot provide reliable safety guarantees under adversarial conditions.
items.citation: Andis Draguns, Sumeet Ramesh Motwani, Raymond Douglas et al.. AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Comprehensive JWST Slitless Spectroscopic Census of $\sim$12,000 Emission-Line Galaxies at Redshift $0\sim9$ in COSMOS
items.summary: This paper presents a large-scale spectroscopic survey of emission-line galaxies using JWST's near-infrared slitless spectroscopy mode, covering a substantial contiguous area of sky within the COSMOS field. The team analyzed wide-field slitless spectroscopy data from the COSMOS-3D program, combining grism spectra with deep multi-band imaging and spectral energy distribution fitting to identify and characterize sources spanning redshifts from zero to nine. To overcome the source confusion that is characteristic of slitless spectroscopy, they developed a multi-step identification framework that incorporates convolutional neural networks and large language models to emulate human judgment and improve classification efficiency. The resulting catalog contains over twelve thousand emission-line objects with spectroscopic redshifts, line measurements, and derived physical properties, detecting a broad suite of emission lines that enable a continuous census of star formation, chemical enrichment, and AGN activity across cosmic time. By stacking spectra in redshift bins, the authors also recovered faint features such as higher-order hydrogen recombination lines, CO absorption bands, and iron emission lines that are undetectable in individual spectra, demonstrating the power of wide-field slitless spectroscopy for constructing large, unbiased galaxy samples.
items.citation: Shuqi Fu, Zijian Zhang, Danyang Jiang et al.. A Comprehensive JWST Slitless Spectroscopic Census of $\sim$12,000 Emission-Line Galaxies at Redshift $0\sim9$ in COSMOS. arXiv. 2026

items.title: DyssomniaNN: Multi-Scale Spiking Neural Modeling of Human Sleep Disorders and Perceived Restedness
items.summary: This paper presents DyssomniaNN, a computational framework designed to model human sleep disorders and the disconnect between objective sleep duration and subjective restorative quality. The model integrates established theories of sleep regulation—including homeostatic and circadian drive processes and a hypothalamic flip-flop switching circuit—with a recurrent corticothalamic spiking neural network to simulate sleep-wake dynamics across five clinical cohorts over a standardized multi-day period. Synthetic neural activity generated by the model closely matched empirical human electroencephalography recordings across standard frequency bands, validating the approach. A novel metric called the Well-Rested Index was introduced to quantify restorative sleep efficacy, and simulations demonstrated that total sleep time alone fails to predict recovery, as paradoxical insomnia produced normal sleep duration yet poor restoration due to elevated cortical beta-band activity, while narcolepsy generated severe sleep fragmentation characteristic of hypocretin deficiency. The authors propose DyssomniaNN as an in silico platform for investigating sleep disorder mechanisms and testing virtual pharmacological interventions.
items.citation: Daniel Szelogowski. DyssomniaNN: Multi-Scale Spiking Neural Modeling of Human Sleep Disorders and Perceived Restedness. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Where to Look Matters: Rethinking Sub-Volume Sampling in 3D Medical Self-supervised Learning
items.summary: This paper investigates the role of sub-volume sampling strategies in self-supervised learning for 3D medical images, challenging the common practice of random cropping during pretraining. The authors first demonstrate through controlled crop-quality experiments that the quality of sampled sub-volumes directly influences downstream transfer performance, identifying the observation policy as a previously overlooked bottleneck. They propose a plug-and-play framework that replaces random cropping with an offline coarse-to-fine probe bank designed to select sub-volumes according to principles of anatomy-awareness, informativeness, and diversity. Two variants are introduced—a lightweight version relying on geometric and image-statistical cues, and a more diagnostically oriented version using frozen visual features—to assess whether simple volume-intrinsic priors are sufficient or whether richer semantic information provides additional benefit. Experiments across multiple backbones and downstream tasks show that the lightweight variant consistently outperforms random sampling, with mechanistic analyses attributing the gains to more anatomically meaningful and informative observations, reduced spatial redundancy, and more structured learned representations.
items.citation: Junkai Liu, Le Zhang. Where to Look Matters: Rethinking Sub-Volume Sampling in 3D Medical Self-supervised Learning. arXiv. 2026

items.title: RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics
items.summary: This paper addresses the problem of tool retrieval for AI agents, specifically the gap between selecting semantically relevant tools and selecting tools that are actually available and reliable at runtime. The authors propose RATED, a retrieval framework that combines a frozen dual-encoder with contrastive fine-tuning for semantic matching alongside a lightweight contextual bandit module that re-ranks tool candidates based on real-time execution feedback, enabling adaptation to tool failures without retraining the underlying model. To support evaluation, they introduce EcoAgent, a large-scale benchmark comprising real-world tools and hundreds of thousands of query-tool pairs designed to assess both offline retrieval quality and dynamic reliability under failure conditions. Experiments show that RATED substantially improves retrieval ranking over existing baselines and dramatically reduces the rate at which faulty or unavailable tools are selected, even under severe simulated outage conditions, with minimal added latency.
items.citation: Weiliang Chen, Song Liao. RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics. arXiv. 2026

items.title: An Annealing-based Quantum Neural Network with Discrete Wavelet Transforms for Enhanced Air Pollution Nowcasting
items.summary: This paper investigates whether quantum machine learning can improve short-term air pollution prediction, specifically targeting particulate matter concentrations in urban environments. The researchers developed a hybrid framework combining variational quantum circuits with quantum annealing, implemented on a neuromorphic quantum computing platform to overcome the qubit limitations typical of current noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices, and tested it using high-density urban air quality data from the UK. The model was scaled to a large number of qubits and combined with discrete wavelet transforms to decompose the input signal before prediction. The quantum neural networks demonstrated an inherent robustness to noisy, high-entropy environmental data, outperforming classical deep learning baselines including multilayer perceptrons and long short-term memory networks. The authors argue that the combination of quantum annealing, neuromorphic computing, and wavelet decomposition achieves state-of-the-art predictive accuracy, establishing a benchmark for practical quantum utility on real-world nonlinear problems.
items.citation: Otto Menegasso Pires, André Saimon, Daniela Herrmann et al.. An Annealing-based Quantum Neural Network with Discrete Wavelet Transforms for Enhanced Air Pollution Nowcasting. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Translational Barriers and AI-Driven Challenges of Microfluidics-Enabled Wearables and Implantable Systems in Personalized Medicine.
items.summary: This review examines the trajectory of wearable and implantable microfluidic systems from laboratory prototypes toward clinical deployment, focusing on their capacity to continuously and minimally invasively sample biomarkers from biofluids such as sweat, saliva, tears, and interstitial fluid. Rather than addressing materials or fabrication in isolation, the authors construct an integrated framework spanning functional biomaterials, advanced fabrication, diagnostic performance benchmarking, and closed-loop theranostic platforms that combine sensing with autonomous therapeutic delivery. The review further analyzes how artificial intelligence is incorporated across sensor self-calibration, multiplexed molecular decoding, and on-device decision-making to shift these systems from passive monitoring toward adaptive intervention. A critical focus is placed on socio-technical barriers to translation, particularly how heterogeneity in biofluid data and disparities in population baselines can introduce and propagate algorithmic bias. The authors conclude that achieving equitable and responsible deployment in personalized medicine will require robust hardware-software interfaces, standardized validation benchmarks, and alignment with emerging regulatory frameworks.
items.citation: Huang K, Fong CY, Huang X et al.. Translational Barriers and AI-Driven Challenges of Microfluidics-Enabled Wearables and Implantable Systems in Personalized Medicine.. Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany). 2026

items.title: Recent advances in microfluidic-based biosensors for nucleic acid detection: From amplification strategies to point-of-care diagnostic devices.
items.summary: This review examines recent progress in microfluidic-based biosensors designed for nucleic acid detection, with a focus on their potential to enable point-of-care diagnostics. The authors survey how microfluidic integration addresses key limitations of conventional centralized molecular diagnostic approaches, including lengthy analysis times, high costs, and restricted accessibility in resource-limited settings. The review covers both thermocyclic amplification methods such as polymerase chain reaction and a range of isothermal amplification techniques, as well as emerging detection technologies and strategies for integrating these components into compact platforms. By critically comparing analytical performance across different approaches, the authors highlight how miniaturized systems can reduce reagent consumption, accelerate amplification, and consolidate sample preparation and detection. The review also identifies persistent technological challenges that must be overcome to successfully translate laboratory-demonstrated microfluidic nucleic acid detection systems into practical, reliable point-of-care diagnostic devices for infectious and non-infectious disease applications.
items.citation: Kulkarni MB, Vineela, Mandal N et al.. Recent advances in microfluidic-based biosensors for nucleic acid detection: From amplification strategies to point-of-care diagnostic devices.. SLAS technology. 2026

items.title: Machine Learning-Guided Synthetic Microbial Communities Enable Functional and Sustainable Degradation of Persistent Environmental Pollutants
items.summary: This paper developed a machine learning-guided framework called GENIA for rationally designing synthetic microbial communities capable of degrading multiple persistent environmental pollutants simultaneously. The researchers used a microfluidic high-throughput cultivation platform to isolate and screen thousands of bacterial strains from pollutant-enriched environments, then performed whole-genome sequencing on prioritized candidates to identify metabolic traits relevant to degrading lignin, atrazine, and PFAS compounds. Genomic data were encoded as spline-based graph representations and processed through a pipeline combining graph neural networks, pathway complementarity modeling, and functional redundancy minimization to predict optimal community assemblies. The resulting nine-member synthetic community achieved high removal rates for all three pollutants simultaneously in kinetic experiments, representing a multi-fold improvement over existing single-strain or naturally occurring consortia approaches. The authors conclude that GENIA provides a scalable, generalizable framework for engineering ecologically coherent microbial consortia by integrating systems-level genomics, phenotypic screening, and predictive modeling for complex bioremediation applications.
items.citation: Esaú De la Vega-Camarillo, Jorge Arreola‐Vargas, Sanjay Antony‐Babu et al.. Machine Learning-Guided Synthetic Microbial Communities Enable Functional and Sustainable Degradation of Persistent Environmental Pollutants. Environmental Science & Technology. 2026

items.title: Interaction-aware dexterous robot for minimally invasive transcanal inner ear interventions
items.summary: This paper developed a miniaturized continuum robot designed to enable minimally invasive access to the inner ear through the ear canal for diagnostic and therapeutic purposes such as drug delivery and microsampling. The robot features a dual-segment design driven by antagonistic cables, with a transition-free saddle-shaped joint backbone that achieves a very small bending radius, allowing it to navigate complex anatomy in programmable configurations. It integrates catheter, endoscopic, and instrumental functions, with a central microneedle end-effector and Fiber Bragg grating sensors that measure tool-tissue interaction forces to help prevent tissue damage. The system was validated in cadaver and live animal models, demonstrating atraumatic transcanal navigation to the round window membrane with high positional accuracy. The authors conclude that this robotic platform offers a practical approach for early diagnosis and treatment of inner ear diseases, with potential to extend precision medicine to underserved populations.
items.citation: Haiming Li, Peiyuan Gao, Haoyue Tan et al.. Interaction-aware dexterous robot for minimally invasive transcanal inner ear interventions. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: Soil microbes are the tiny bioengineers running Earth’s underground factory
items.summary: This paper synthesizes soil microbiome research to better understand how microbial communities drive critical ecosystem processes such as nutrient cycling, carbon storage, and ecosystem resilience. The authors developed a function-centred framework built around four conserved functional axes — secondary metabolism, nutrient cycling, community interactions, and stress tolerance — drawing on studies across ecological, agricultural, and environmental contexts. They argue that these functional axes collectively govern plant productivity, climate regulation, and pollutant transformation, though their expression varies strongly with environmental context. The synthesis proposes that soil operates as a self-organizing system in which microbial interactions produce emergent ecosystem-level behaviors. This framework is presented as a foundation for predictive, ecology-informed strategies to manage soils for sustainable agriculture, environmental remediation, and climate mitigation.
items.citation: Suzanne Hassan-Dalléac, Wafa Guiga, Antonia Suau. Soil microbes are the tiny bioengineers running Earth’s underground factory. Communications Earth & Environment. 2026

items.title: Regulatory Challenges and Opportunities for Cell‐Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Pharmaceutical Development: A European and Global Perspective
items.summary: This paper examines the regulatory landscape governing cell-derived extracellular vesicles as therapeutic and diagnostic products, focusing on inconsistencies across major jurisdictions. The authors analyze how existing medicinal product frameworks in the European Union, United States, Japan, and other regions classify and regulate EV-based products, noting that the acellular nature of EVs does not map cleanly onto pre-existing regulatory categories such as advanced therapy medicinal products or biologics. A key development discussed is a recent European regulatory guideline clarifying that minimally modified EVs fall outside the advanced therapy medicinal product definition, contrasting with the approach taken by other regulatory bodies that treat such products as drugs or biological products subject to premarket requirements. The paper identifies operational grey zones including classification criteria, critical quality attributes, potency strategies, and comparability standards as areas requiring clarification to enable consistent cross-regional development. Without prescribing new normative frameworks, the authors argue that EV-based products can and should be developed within existing medicinal product frameworks, provided these tools are applied consistently and supported by ongoing regulatory dialogue among international agencies and scientific societies.
items.citation: Tania Limongi, Paola Milla, Barbara Stella et al.. Regulatory Challenges and Opportunities for Cell‐Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Pharmaceutical Development: A European and Global Perspective. Journal of Extracellular Vesicles. 2026
