items.title: A Comprehensive JWST Slitless Spectroscopic Census of $\sim$12,000 Emission-Line Galaxies at Redshift $0\sim9$ in COSMOS
items.summary: This paper presents a large-scale census of emission-line galaxies using JWST near-infrared slitless spectroscopy from the COSMOS-3D program, covering a contiguous area of sky and targeting a wide redshift range from approximately zero to nine. The study combined wide-field slitless spectroscopy with deep multi-band imaging to construct a homogeneous spectroscopic catalog of over twelve thousand objects, detecting multiple emission lines spanning from oxygen and hydrogen recombination lines to molecular and iron features. To overcome the source confusion problem inherent to slitless spectroscopy, the authors developed a multi-step identification framework that incorporates convolutional neural networks and large language models to emulate and streamline human identification of spectral sources. The resulting catalog delivers spectroscopic redshifts, emission-line measurements, and derived physical properties, while composite spectra constructed in redshift bins reveal faint features—including higher-order hydrogen recombination lines, CO absorption bands, and iron lines—that are undetectable in individual spectra. The work demonstrates the power of wide-field slitless spectroscopy for building large, unbiased samples to study galaxy evolution and AGN activity across cosmic time.
items.citation: Shuqi Fu, Zijian Zhang, Danyang Jiang et al.. A Comprehensive JWST Slitless Spectroscopic Census of $\sim$12,000 Emission-Line Galaxies at Redshift $0\sim9$ in COSMOS. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Where to Look Matters: Rethinking Sub-Volume Sampling in 3D Medical Self-supervised Learning
items.summary: This paper investigates how sub-volume sampling strategies during self-supervised pretraining affect representation learning on three-dimensional medical images. The authors first demonstrate through controlled experiments that the quality of crops used during pretraining directly influences downstream transfer performance, identifying the observation policy as an underexplored bottleneck in medical self-supervised learning. To address this, they propose a plug-and-play framework that replaces random cropping with a structured, offline coarse-to-fine probe bank designed to select sub-volumes according to anatomy-awareness, informativeness, and diversity. The framework is instantiated in two variants: a lightweight version relying on geometric and image-statistical cues, and a more diagnostically oriented version using frozen visual features to assess whether simple priors suffice or richer semantic information provides additional benefit. Experiments across multiple self-supervised backbones and downstream tasks show that the lightweight variant consistently outperforms random sampling, with analyses attributing the gains to more anatomically meaningful and informative observations, reduced spatial redundancy, and more structured learned representations.
items.citation: Junkai Liu, Le Zhang. Where to Look Matters: Rethinking Sub-Volume Sampling in 3D Medical Self-supervised Learning. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Enhanced analogue quantum computation with a logically-encoded XX gadget
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of implementing two-body XX interactions on analogue quantum devices, which typically only support one-body fields and two-body ZZ interactions natively. The authors introduce the "truss gadget," an exact construction that synthesizes effective XX interactions using only these natively available components, without approximation. They experimentally validated the gadget by reproducing target XX Hamiltonian dynamics on a trapped-ion quantum processor. Applying the gadget to weighted maximum-independent-set problem instances on a superconducting quantum annealer, they found a dramatic improvement in the probability of identifying near-ground-state solutions compared to implementations lacking XX interactions. The results suggest that logically encoding XX interactions through such gadgets can substantially enhance the performance of analogue quantum computation for combinatorial optimization.
items.citation: Robert J. Banks, Natasha Feinstein, Roopayan Ghosh et al.. Enhanced analogue quantum computation with a logically-encoded XX gadget. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Phononic Frequency Combs in Twisted Bilayer Transition Metal Dichalcogenide Heterostructures from First Principles
items.summary: This paper investigates whether phononic frequency combs can be predicted entirely from first principles, without treating anharmonic coupling as a free parameter fitted to experiment. The authors studied twisted bilayer heterostructures of two transition metal dichalcogenide compounds at a specific commensurate twist angle, using density functional theory to compute all relevant phonon properties, including mode frequencies from second-order force constants, quality factors via the Boltzmann transport equation from third-order force constants, and anharmonic intermode coupling strengths from the same third-order tensor. Both bilayer systems were found to host mode pairs extremely close to a two-to-one frequency resonance, satisfying a key condition for parametric phononic frequency comb generation. Numerical integration of the resulting two-mode equations revealed that both materials generate frequency combs through a subcritical (discontinuous) transition, with spectral entropy peaking before the abrupt onset of comb formation. The two compounds exhibit similar anharmonic coupling strengths, but differ substantially in their signal-mode quality factors, which the authors identify as the dominant factor governing the drive threshold required to excite a comb.
items.citation: Naman Arora, Adarsh Ganesan. Phononic Frequency Combs in Twisted Bilayer Transition Metal Dichalcogenide Heterostructures from First Principles. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Physical-state supervision for design-only Gaussian process surrogates of implosion simulations
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of building accurate surrogate models for inertial confinement fusion implosion simulations, where physical diagnostics recorded during simulation can help organize a sharply varying response but are unavailable at prediction time without additional computation. The authors developed a Gaussian process surrogate framework that learns to predict these physical diagnostics (such as burn-weighted states) directly from design variables, using cross-fitted estimates to augment the design representation without requiring extra simulations at inference. The approach was evaluated on a large database of paired one-dimensional implosion simulations, comparing a global Gaussian process predictor against an optional soft mixture-of-experts formulation across multiple material configurations and test conditions. Physical-state supervision substantially reduced prediction error for both random holdout and design-space extrapolation compared to control conditions using random projections or shuffled states, confirming that the gains arise specifically from the physical content of the learned diagnostics. The study finds that expert specialization provides benefit primarily at smaller training set sizes and should be chosen by validation, while physical-state supervision broadly improves surrogate accuracy for finite-data regimes, with an open implementation released alongside the data.
items.citation: Chang Liu, Hao Shen, Chuanying Li. Physical-state supervision for design-only Gaussian process surrogates of implosion simulations. arXiv. 2026

items.title: QTestBench: A Test Framework for Evaluating LLM-Generated Quantum Code
items.summary: This paper investigates whether large language models can generate effective unit tests for quantum software, a problem distinct from classical code testing due to the probabilistic nature of quantum programs, numerical tolerances, and domain-specific correctness criteria. The authors introduce QTestBench, a framework that evaluates LLM-generated test suites by comparing their verdicts against independent benchmark checkers rather than treating the generated tests themselves as ground truth. The framework prompts models to produce syntactic, semantic, and behavioral tests across tasks drawn from two quantum programming ecosystems, injects candidate solutions at runtime, and assesses test quality across multiple validation cohorts designed to answer specific diagnostic questions. Testing five large language models revealed that while generated test suites almost always execute successfully, their ability to discriminate correct from faulty implementations is substantially weaker, with the best-performing model achieving a test quality score considerably higher on one benchmark than the other, demonstrating that executability alone overstates practical test quality. The study also shows that oracle-verified synthetic mutants help stabilize bug-detection estimates when naturally occurring faulty solutions are rare, and the framework is positioned as a reproducible cross-framework benchmark for assessing the trustworthiness of LLM-generated quantum tests.
items.citation: Meriem Terki, Nouhaila Innan, Minghao Shao et al.. QTestBench: A Test Framework for Evaluating LLM-Generated Quantum Code. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Advancements in biosensor Technologies for Pathogen Detection: Innovations and comparison with conventional diagnostic approaches.
items.summary: This review paper examines biosensor technologies developed for the rapid and sensitive detection of pathogens across clinical, food safety, and environmental monitoring contexts, comparing them against established conventional diagnostic approaches. The authors surveyed electrochemical, optical, nanoparticle, microfluidic, and paper-based biosensor platforms, discussing their underlying sensing principles, design strategies, applications, and respective advantages and limitations. Conventional methods such as culture-based assays, ELISA, and PCR, while analytically proven, are noted to be constrained by lengthy processing times, complex instrumentation, and the requirement for trained personnel, whereas biosensors offer portability, multiplexing capability, high sensitivity, and suitability for point-of-care use. Advances in nanomaterials, biorecognition strategies, and signal-transduction mechanisms have expanded the potential of biosensors for pathogen detection, though challenges including sensor stability, reproducibility, fabrication scalability, and regulatory validation continue to hinder their widespread practical implementation. The review concludes by outlining future perspectives for integrating these biosensor technologies into real-world diagnostic and monitoring applications.
items.citation: Singhal P, Misra S, Prakash A et al.. Advancements in biosensor Technologies for Pathogen Detection: Innovations and comparison with conventional diagnostic approaches.. Journal of microbiological methods. 2026

items.title: Development of a NiCoFe-LDH/Ketjenblack-enhanced electrochemical antibacterial peptide biosensor for Aeromonas hydrophila detection in seawater samples.
items.summary: This paper developed an electrochemical biosensor for detecting the fish pathogen Aeromonas hydrophila in aquaculture settings, with particular emphasis on applicability to seawater samples. The sensor was constructed by modifying a screen-printed carbon electrode with a nanocomposite of ternary NiCoFe layered double hydroxide combined with Ketjenblack carbon, synthesized via one-pot precipitation, and functionalized with an antibacterial peptide as the biorecognition element. The nanocomposite was characterized as a high-activity nanosheet structure with rapid electron transfer properties, and the peptide layer provided selective bacterial capture confirmed through affinity studies. Under optimized room-temperature conditions, the biosensor achieved detection across a broad bacterial concentration range within thirty minutes, with a very low limit of detection, minimal cross-reactivity with other bacterial species, and recovery values in spiked seawater that closely matched buffer responses. The authors claim this represents the first electrochemical antibacterial peptide-based biosensor for A. hydrophila validated in seawater, offering a rapid and sensitive tool for pathogen monitoring in aquaculture environments.
items.citation: Kızılkurtlu AA, Arancı K, Gülyüz S et al.. Development of a NiCoFe-LDH/Ketjenblack-enhanced electrochemical antibacterial peptide biosensor for Aeromonas hydrophila detection in seawater samples.. Mikrochimica acta. 2026

items.title: Automated machine learning framework for interpreting paper-based biosensing of pathogens.
items.summary: This paper investigated automated machine learning approaches for interpreting images from paper-based colorimetric biosensors designed to detect microbial pathogens. The researchers developed and compared several image analysis strategies, including conventional normalized intensity extraction, region-of-interest descriptors, and convolutional neural networks, evaluating their performance both within individual studies and across distinct biosensor studies targeting different pathogens. While all approaches performed well within a single study, performance degraded when decision thresholds trained on one study were applied to another, revealing a systematic study-dependent shift in classification boundaries. To address this, the authors introduced a color-space normalization method that characterized each test signal relative to paired positive and negative controls rather than relying on single-channel intensity alone, which stabilized decision thresholds and improved cross-study classification consistency. The results suggest that this normalization strategy enables more generalizable machine learning models for paper-based biosensor interpretation, supporting broader adoption of automated, standardized readout approaches across different assay contexts.
items.citation: Park S, Yang Z, He Z. Automated machine learning framework for interpreting paper-based biosensing of pathogens.. Environmental research. 2026

items.title: Self-Cleaning Electrochemical Biosensor Based on MCOF@Ag for Simultaneous Pathogen Detection and Photocatalytic Inactivation.
items.summary: This paper developed a dual-function electrochemical biosensor capable of both detecting and killing bacterial pathogens using a single electrode material. The researchers synthesized a silver nanoparticle-decorated metal-covalent organic framework with a nanoflower-like structure, then functionalized it with aptamers specific to Staphylococcus aureus to enable selective bacterial capture and electrochemical quantification. The biosensor achieved highly sensitive detection of S. aureus across a broad concentration range with an exceptionally low detection limit. Beyond detection, the material's strong photocatalytic activity under visible light enabled near-complete inactivation of captured bacteria through reactive oxygen species generation, after which the electrode could be regenerated and reused. This work demonstrates that a single MCOF-based electrode can integrate ultrasensitive pathogen detection with photocatalytic disinfection and self-cleaning regeneration, offering a promising platform for infectious disease monitoring and control.
items.citation: Bai Y, Xiao L, Cai L et al.. Self-Cleaning Electrochemical Biosensor Based on MCOF@Ag for Simultaneous Pathogen Detection and Photocatalytic Inactivation.. Analytical chemistry. 2026

items.title: One-step MCDA-CRISPR/Cas12b platform for point-of-care testing of Shewanella algae.
items.summary: The paper addresses the need for rapid, accurate detection of *Shewanella algae*, an emerging marine zoonotic pathogen associated with high mortality, for which existing diagnostic methods are inadequate. The researchers developed a one-pot, one-step detection platform called MCTOS, which combines Multiple Cross Displacement Amplification with CRISPR/Cas12b-based signal readout at a constant temperature, targeting a *S. algae*-specific gene identified through pan-genome analysis of hundreds of bacterial genomes. The assay can be completed within an hour, with results readable via real-time fluorescence or a lateral flow biosensor, and achieves a detection limit of ten copies with no cross-reactivity against other related templates. When evaluated on clinical isolates and samples, the platform demonstrated complete specificity and near-complete sensitivity, outperforming recent comparable one-pot CRISPR and loop-mediated isothermal amplification methods in sensitivity and primer design simplicity. The authors conclude that MCTOS represents a simple, rapid, and highly accurate point-of-care tool suitable for clinical diagnosis and epidemiological surveillance across diverse laboratory settings.
items.citation: Wang X, Dong L, Zhang S et al.. One-step MCDA-CRISPR/Cas12b platform for point-of-care testing of Shewanella algae.. Talanta. 2026

items.title: Paper-Based Biosensor Using Dual-Recognition Molecules for Detection of <i>Staphylococcus aureus</i> in Milk.
items.summary: This study developed a paper-based biosensor for the rapid, on-site detection of *Staphylococcus aureus* in milk, addressing the need for simple methods to identify this common foodborne pathogen in dairy products. The biosensor employed a dual-recognition strategy combining a milk matrix-adapted aptamer, selected through a SELEX process optimized for the milk environment, with polyclonal antibodies that enable multi-epitope capture on the paper substrate, while colloidal gold nanoparticles served as visual signal reporters. This combination of aptamer-based specificity and antibody-based broad capture synergistically improved both sensitivity and selectivity compared to single-recognition approaches. The biosensor achieved visual detection of *S. aureus* at a very low concentration within minutes, requiring no instrumentation, making it a cost-effective tool for dairy safety monitoring.
items.citation: Hou W, Li X, Li J et al.. Paper-Based Biosensor Using Dual-Recognition Molecules for Detection of <i>Staphylococcus aureus</i> in Milk.. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: Synergistic Multicomponent Nucleopeptide-Based Hydrogels: Harnessing DNA-Base Pairing and Electrostatic Complementarities
items.summary: This study investigated peptide-based low-molecular-weight hydrogels incorporating DNA nucleobases, known as nucleopeptides, to understand how combining electrostatic and nucleobase-pairing interactions influences hydrogel properties. The researchers synthesized six nucleopeptides derived from two complementary peptide sequences — one negatively charged and one positively charged at physiological pH — each functionalized with one of the four DNA nucleobases introduced via a peptide nucleic acid moiety. Using a systematic multiscale approach, they examined how charge complementarity and nucleobase-pair complementarity, individually and in combination, affect mechanical and physicochemical properties including gelation time, stiffness, sol-gel transition temperature, stress resistance, and fibrillar network morphology. The findings demonstrate that careful selection of complementary components allows fine-tuning of hydrogel properties, while also revealing unexpected behaviors that highlight the complexity of these bioinspired multicomponent systems. Overall, the work underscores the potential of nucleopeptide-based multicomponent hydrogels as versatile, high-performance supramolecular materials for biomedical and biotechnological applications.
items.citation: Tristan Giraud, Marine Koch, Paul Hoschtettler et al.. Synergistic Multicomponent Nucleopeptide-Based Hydrogels: Harnessing DNA-Base Pairing and Electrostatic Complementarities. ACS Materials Au. 2026

items.title: Self-amplifying RNA (saRNA) and circular RNA (circRNA) vaccines: Progress, evidence gaps, and translational pathways for durable and scalable immunization
items.summary: This review examines two next-generation RNA vaccine platforms — self-amplifying RNA and circular RNA — as alternatives to conventional non-replicating mRNA vaccines. Self-amplifying RNA uses an encoded replicase to amplify intracellular RNA, achieving high antigen expression at lower doses, while circular RNA's covalently closed structure resists enzymatic degradation and enables sustained, cap-independent translation. The authors integrate clinical, animal, and mechanistic evidence across both platforms, noting a substantial asymmetry in maturity: self-amplifying RNA has advanced through human trials including late-phase evaluation of COVID-19 vaccines and has received regulatory authorization in some jurisdictions, whereas circular RNA vaccines remain predominantly preclinical. To guide cross-platform development, the review proposes a "3D" framework organized around durability, dose-sparing, and deployability, and identifies critical barriers including delivery system design, innate immune sensing, and manufacturing and chemistry controls. The authors conclude by mapping translational pathways needed to enable robust comparison and broader deployment of these modalities for durable and scalable immunization.
items.citation: Ugwu Okechukwu Paul-Chima, Michael Ben Okon, Ogenyi Fabian C. et al.. Self-amplifying RNA (saRNA) and circular RNA (circRNA) vaccines: Progress, evidence gaps, and translational pathways for durable and scalable immunization. Human Vaccines & Immunotherapeutics. 2026

items.title: CRISPR-Cas systems as next-generation antimicrobials: a systemic review of mechanisms, delivery strategies, and translational challenges
items.summary: This systematic review examined CRISPR-Cas systems as potential alternatives to conventional antibiotics in the context of rising multidrug-resistant bacterial infections. The authors synthesized preclinical and experimental evidence on how different CRISPR effectors, primarily Cas9 alongside Cas12 and Cas13, can be deployed to kill resistant bacteria or restore antibiotic sensitivity through mechanisms such as chromosomal double-strand break induction, resistance plasmid curing, and RNA-targeted cleavage. Delivery platforms evaluated included bacteriophages, conjugative plasmids, and nanoparticles, with phage-mediated delivery showing the most reliable efficacy across complex environments and animal models. The review found broad support for CRISPR-Cas antimicrobials as a precision approach to combating resistance, and noted that one CRISPR-enhanced engineered bacteriophage cocktail has progressed to clinical evaluation. Nevertheless, significant translational barriers persist, including limited bacterial host range, physiological instability, emergence of escape mutations, and insufficient long-term safety data, with the authors concluding that optimized delivery systems, multiplex targeting, and standardized regulatory frameworks will be essential before clinical adoption.
items.citation: Maha S.I. Wizrah. CRISPR-Cas systems as next-generation antimicrobials: a systemic review of mechanisms, delivery strategies, and translational challenges. Frontiers in Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Advancing Fruit Quality Monitoring with Artificial Intelligence-Augmented Non-Destructive Technologies
items.summary: This review paper examines how artificial intelligence can be integrated with non-destructive sensing technologies to improve fruit quality monitoring across pre- and postharvest stages. The authors surveyed a broad range of sensing modalities, including spectroscopic, imaging, and sensor-based systems, and evaluated how traditional machine learning, deep learning, and hybrid models have been applied to tasks such as ripeness classification and bruise detection. The review also assessed deployment considerations including real-time processing, edge AI, and multimodal data fusion. AI-driven approaches were found to achieve high accuracy in quality assessment tasks while substantially reducing postharvest losses, though persistent challenges include sensor costs, model fragility under real-world field conditions, and the absence of standardized protocols. The authors identify explainable AI, IoT-enabled digital twins, and autonomous agri-robotics as key future directions, emphasizing that realizing AI's transformative potential in this domain will require interdisciplinary collaboration and scalable implementation strategies.
items.citation: Ying Fu, Da‐Wen Sun. Advancing Fruit Quality Monitoring with Artificial Intelligence-Augmented Non-Destructive Technologies. Food Engineering Reviews. 2026

items.title: Traditional fermented food microbial ecosystems oriented towards industrial standards: multi-dimensional characterization and artificial regulation
items.summary: This review examined the microbial ecosystems underlying traditional fermented foods, focusing on the challenge that spontaneous fermentation introduces variability in quality and safety that hinders industrial standardization. The authors surveyed how multi-omics approaches can be integrated to comprehensively characterize microbial community composition, dynamics, metabolite production, microbial interactions, and phage activity. They also summarized strategies for artificially regulating these ecosystems, including the use of functional starter strains, synthetic microbial communities, bacteriophage manipulation, and physicochemical environmental controls. The review concludes by outlining future directions and outstanding challenges in transitioning traditional fermentation from empirical, artisanal practice toward predictable and scalable industrial production.
items.citation: M T Wu, Yi-Xiang Wang, Yu Wang et al.. Traditional fermented food microbial ecosystems oriented towards industrial standards: multi-dimensional characterization and artificial regulation. npj Science of Food. 2026

items.title: Federated Learning in Multimodal Healthcare Diagnostics: Privacy-Preserving AI for Biomedical Imaging, Electronic Health Records, Wearables, and Clinical Decision Support
items.summary: This review paper examines the application of federated learning as a privacy-preserving approach to training artificial intelligence models across diverse healthcare data modalities, including biomedical imaging, electronic health records, wearable sensor outputs, and clinical decision support systems. The authors conducted a broad literature review spanning multiple healthcare domains to assess how federated learning enables multi-institutional AI model training without transferring raw patient data, instead sharing only model updates between collaborating sites. The paper finds that while federated learning substantially reduces direct exposure of sensitive clinical data and improves alignment with privacy regulations, confidentiality is not guaranteed and requires additional protections against threats such as gradient leakage, model inversion, and membership inference attacks. The review also identifies significant practical barriers to deployment, including system heterogeneity across institutions, data imbalance, communication bottlenecks, and fairness concerns. Drawing on both research findings and practical experience, the authors offer actionable guidance for regulators, developers, and healthcare systems aimed at advancing safe, equitable, and geographically distributed federated learning in medicine.
items.venue: Archives of Computational Methods in Engineering
items.citation: Shon G. Nemane, Vaishnavi M. Sarad, Dhiraj P. Tulaskar et al.. Federated Learning in Multimodal Healthcare Diagnostics: Privacy-Preserving AI for Biomedical Imaging, Electronic Health Records, Wearables, and Clinical Decision Support. Archives of Computational Methods in Engineering. 2026

items.title: OGLE-2016-BLG-0523: A Low-mass Brown Dwarf or super-Jupiter in a $>100$ au Orbit
items.summary: This paper investigated a microlensing event, OGLE-2016-BLG-0523, identified through cross-matching survey data spanning over a decade as a candidate for hosting a very wide-orbit binary lens. The researchers analyzed a light curve exhibiting two short-lived brightness bumps separated by more than eight years, evaluating three possible interpretations: a binary-lens single-source, a single-lens binary-source, and two entirely unrelated microlensing events. After ruling out the latter two scenarios based on poorer data fits, implausible source fluxes, and low event rates, the binary-lens interpretation was favored, revealing a mass ratio between the two lensing bodies consistent with a low-mass M dwarf primary hosting a brown dwarf or super-Jupiter companion. Bayesian analysis placed the projected separation of the companion at roughly several hundred astronomical units, making it the widest low-mass object discovered through microlensing to date. The authors note that while future space-based observatories will improve sensitivity to such wide-orbit systems, distinguishing genuine binary-lens events from variable star contaminants and other degeneracies remains a critical challenge for statistical studies of wide-orbit companions.
items.citation: Hongjing Yang, Weicheng Zang, Yoon-Hyun Ryu et al.. OGLE-2016-BLG-0523: A Low-mass Brown Dwarf or super-Jupiter in a $>100$ au Orbit. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Comprehensive JWST Slitless Spectroscopic Census of $\sim$12,000 Emission-Line Galaxies at Redshift $0\sim9$ in COSMOS
items.summary: This paper presents a large-scale census of emission-line galaxies using JWST's near-infrared wide-field slitless spectroscopy as part of the COSMOS-3D program, covering a substantial contiguous sky area with grism spectroscopy across a mid-infrared wavelength range. The study combined slitless spectroscopy with deep multi-band imaging to build a homogeneous spectroscopic catalog spanning redshifts from zero to nine, and introduced a novel multi-step source identification framework that incorporates convolutional neural networks and large language models to handle the source confusion inherent to slitless spectroscopy. The resulting catalog provides spectroscopic redshifts, emission-line measurements, and derived physical properties for tens of thousands of sources, detecting numerous emission lines that enable a continuous census of galaxies across cosmic time. Composite spectra constructed in multiple redshift bins reveal faint spectral features — including higher-order hydrogen recombination lines, CO absorption bands, and iron lines — that are undetectable in individual spectra. The work demonstrates the power of wide-field slitless spectroscopy for assembling large, unbiased samples suited to studying galaxy evolution, star formation, chemical enrichment, and AGN activity across most of cosmic history.
items.citation: Shuqi Fu, Zijian Zhang, Danyang Jiang et al.. A Comprehensive JWST Slitless Spectroscopic Census of $\sim$12,000 Emission-Line Galaxies at Redshift $0\sim9$ in COSMOS. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Fundamental Limits of Covert queueing under Busy-Period Observations
items.summary: This paper investigates the fundamental limits of covert communication within a queueing framework, where an operator attempts to secretly serve unauthorized jobs alongside legitimate traffic without detection. The setting involves a Markovian queueing system in which the legitimate user monitors summary statistics from each busy period, specifically either the number of jobs served or the busy period duration. Using hypothesis testing as the detection framework, the authors derive that the maximum number of covert jobs that can be served follows a square-root law with respect to the number of observed busy periods, consistent with square-root laws found in other covert communication settings. They further characterize the precise scaling constant of this square-root law, termed the covert queueing constant, for each of the two monitoring statistics. Comparing the two cases, they establish that observing the number of jobs served is a strictly more powerful detection statistic than observing busy period duration, as it yields a smaller covert queueing constant for the operator.
items.citation: Anumula Venkata Sai Sree Sahithi, Arti Yardi, Jithin Ravi. Fundamental Limits of Covert queueing under Busy-Period Observations. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Beyond the Snowflakes: Disentangling Weather Effects from Confounding Meta-Factors in LiDAR Object Detection
items.summary: This paper investigated how adverse weather, specifically snowfall, affects LiDAR-based object detection in autonomous vehicles. Using two datasets and ablation studies, the researchers analyzed detection performance across varying snow intensities while examining correlated metadata. Counter-intuitively, they found that detection accuracy improves as snow intensity increases, which they explain not as a benefit of snow itself but as a consequence of a confounding factor: snow accumulation on vehicle surfaces increases point cloud density by expanding effective surface area and shifting reflectance from specular to diffuse. The authors argue that existing evaluation frameworks conflate atmospheric noise effects with surface accumulation effects, leading to misleading conclusions about detector robustness in adverse weather. They conclude that meaningful evaluation of perception systems requires disentangling these two physically distinct phenomena rather than grouping data by broad weather-severity categories alone.
items.citation: Yiming Yang, Jeremy P. Bos. Beyond the Snowflakes: Disentangling Weather Effects from Confounding Meta-Factors in LiDAR Object Detection. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Tracking the Invisible: Self-Supervised Wheel Track Detection with Thermal-RGB Fusion
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of detecting wheel tracks on snow-covered roads for autonomous driving, arguing that following existing tracks provides traction and stability benefits that general traversability methods fail to exploit. The authors developed a self-supervised approach that fuses standard RGB imagery with long-wave infrared thermal imaging, using synchronized GNSS recordings to automatically generate training labels by projecting future wheel trajectories onto the image plane. A neural network was trained on the resulting four-channel RGB-thermal images to identify wheel tracks on visually featureless, white-out road surfaces without requiring manual annotation. The method was validated experimentally in adverse winter conditions, demonstrating robustness where conventional vision-based approaches struggle, and the authors also released a new dataset called ThermalTrack to support further research in this area.
items.citation: Yiming Yang, Jeremy P. Bos. Tracking the Invisible: Self-Supervised Wheel Track Detection with Thermal-RGB Fusion. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Ask Your Advisor: Learning When to Consult Stronger Models in Agentic Systems
items.summary: This paper investigates how agentic AI systems can balance task performance against computational cost by selectively consulting a stronger "advisor" model rather than relying on it throughout execution. The challenge is that the weaker "executor" model must decide when its own reasoning is insufficient, a task current language models handle poorly through self-assessment alone. The authors introduce ARIA, a meta-controller that learns consultation timing by framing the problem as a sequential resource-allocation task, mapping execution evidence to a compact state representation and choosing between remaining silent or seeking advice, with action values learned via Monte Carlo control from cost-penalized outcomes. Evaluated across several agentic benchmarks, ARIA recovers a substantial portion of the performance gap between using only the weak model and always using the strong model, while spending less than half the cost of the stronger model. ARIA outperforms a range of alternative strategies including routing, cascading, fixed consultation schedules, and random advice placement, and its policies remain compact, inspectable, and adjustable through a single cost parameter without retraining the underlying models.
items.citation: Pascal Sowietzki, Steffen Holter, Yannick Metz et al.. Ask Your Advisor: Learning When to Consult Stronger Models in Agentic Systems. arXiv. 2026
